sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
paragraphs: Hmong (pronounced mung; H silent). White Hmong and Green Hmong / Mong Leng. Compass ACS 2019–2023 near 99,900. Census Asian mixes this with Chinese, Indian, Vietnamese, Karen. Date the number you cite.
There is no single Hmong client. Defer to this family. Do not open a Karen or Lao case with this page. Say mung.

This brief is about Hmong people — Hmoob in White Hmong, Moob in Green Hmong / Mong Leng. It is a people with ancient roots in southern China, a highland life in Laos, and a Minnesota community built after 1975. Pronounce it mung. The H is silent. If you say Huh-mong in a lobby, you have already told the household you did not study.

### Who this is

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Hmong ancestry near 99,900. About 94 percent Twin Cities, about 6 percent Greater Minnesota. About 38 percent age 17 or younger. About 33 percent foreign-born — which means a majority of this community was born here. Pew (May 2025, 2021–2023 ACS) put Minnesota near 95,000 on a Hmong-alone count and named it the second-largest state community after California. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

St. Paul is a national hub. It is not the map. Frogtown, the East Side, Little Mekong on University Avenue, Hmongtown Marketplace, Hmong Village, Brooklyn Center, Maplewood, and a smaller Greater Minnesota share are not one client.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Secret War veteran who came through Ban Vinai, a Christian grandmother, a txiv neeb (traditional healer) whose altar is in the living room, a U.S.-born nurse, a farmer at the summer market, a college student who uses English with friends and Hmong with an elder, a person who left clan obligation and still shows up at New Year — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### Who this is not

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Chinese New Year. It is not Karen, Vietnamese, Lao as a synonym, Cambodian, or a generic Southeast Asian interpreter. Shared continent is not shared culture.

### How to read this

Read it as an orientation. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

The facts that follow are meant to help you meet people well — how family is named, what respect looks like, what a greeting carries, what a form may land on. Counts are dated. History is here so the meeting is clearer, not so you deliver a lecture.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
paragraphs: Southern China origin; highland Laos; no nation-state. RPA writing in the 1950s. Oral literature and paj ntaub older than the camp file.
History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with embroidery tourism.

Hmong peoplehood is older than Laos, older than the CIA file, and older than the refugee camp. Oral history and scholarship place origin in southern China; movement into the highlands of what became Laos, Vietnam, and Thailand under pressure from imperial states. Statelessness is a political fact, not a personality.

### Clan, language, writing

There is no Hmong nation-state. Clan, language, agriculture, and ritual organized life without a capital city. Writing systems came late. The Romanized Popular Alphabet (RPA), developed in the 1950s in Laos, is the common Latin script in Minnesota. Historically the language was oral. Paj ntaub / paaj ntaub — story cloth and embroidery — carried memory when paper did not.

### White Hmong and Green Hmong

Two large dialect-and-dress groups live in Minnesota: White Hmong (Hmoob Dawb) and Green Hmong, also called Blue Hmong or Mong Leng (Hmoob Leeg / Moob). The names come from dress, not politics. The dialects are close and not always interchangeable in an interpreter. Green Hmong often write the people-name without the H: Moob. That is the same instruction as this page: say mung.

### What people brought

Clan, ancestor obligation, shamanic healing and Christianity both, farming knowledge, oral skill, a memory of being recruited to fight someone else’s war and then left. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled “Hmong.”

sections.heading: The Geography of the Hmong World
paragraphs: Laos highlands; China; Vietnam; Thailand; U.S. concentration in California, Minnesota, Wisconsin. St. Paul is a hub, not the map.
Do not assume Frogtown. Do not assume they have been to Laos.

Homeland is not one flag. Southern China remains a Hmong (Miao) geography. The Laos highlands — Xieng Khouang, Long Tieng, the places named in veteran stories — are the origin of most Minnesota families.

### Diaspora

There are Hmong communities in Vietnam, Thailand, Burma/Myanmar, and a global diaspora: California, Minnesota, Wisconsin, North Carolina, France, Australia.

Pew (May 2025): California is the largest U.S. state community; Minnesota second; Wisconsin third. Fresno and Sacramento sit next to Minneapolis–St. Paul as sister maps. Secondary migration built Minnesota. Church sponsors scattered people; clan pulled them back together.

### In Minnesota

St. Paul is the national urban hub. East Side. Frogtown. University Avenue / Little Mekong. Ramsey County. Brooklyn Center and inner-ring suburbs. A small Greater Minnesota share. Frogtown is not the whole. The person in front of you may not have been to Laos.

sections.heading: The Secret War, 1975, and the Camps — Foundational Event
paragraphs: CIA Secret War 1961–1975; Vang Pao; May 1975 airlift and flight; Thai camps including Ban Vinai; first Minnesota family December 1975; secondary migration.
If you only know “refugee,” you will miss the 20-year-old who has never lived in Laos and still cannot get Mong Leng in the lobby.

If the Great Migration is the foundational demographic event of modern Black America, and 1991 of Somali Minnesota, the Secret War and 1975 are the foundational event of Hmong Minnesota.

### The Secret War

From 1961 to 1975 the United States, through the CIA, recruited Hmong forces under General Vang Pao to fight in Laos — a war the Geneva Accords had said should not be there. Hmong soldiers blocked supply lines and died in large numbers. Boys were recruited. When the United States left in 1975, the Pathet Lao and Vietnamese forces treated Hmong allied families as the enemy.

### Airlift, walk, camps

May 12–14, 1975: airlift from Long Tieng. About 2,500 people in those days. General Vang Pao left May 14. Minnesota later marked that date. Most people were not on the planes. They walked. Thai camps followed — Ban Vinai among the named ones. Years. Then resettlement.

### Minnesota

The first Hmong family in Minnesota, Dang Her and Shoua Moua, arrived in December 1975. Church and voluntary-agency sponsors (Lutheran, Catholic, and others) placed people across the country so no one state would “take too many.” Clan and secondary migration undid the scatter. St. Paul became a hub because people chose each other.

U.S. policy at first treated Hmong people as “too primitive” for asylum. The Indochina Migration and Refugee Assistance Act had to be amended. That sentence is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech you give the family.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: About 18 clans; patrilineal; marry outside the clan. Compass average household size about 4.4.
Ask who should be in the room. A nuclear English form already has a who. Clan is not an icebreaker.

Clan organizes family. About 18 clans are commonly named among Hmong from Laos now in the United States. The clan name is the last name: Chang, Cheng, Chue, Fang, Hang, Her, Khang, Kong, Kue, Lee, Lor, Moua, Pha, Thao, Vang, Vue, Xiong, Yang — English spellings of Hmong names. Same last name often means same clan. Marriage is supposed to be outside the clan.

### Household size

Households are larger than a nuclear English form. Compass: average household size about 4.4. Elders, in-laws, adult children, and clan obligation sit in the same week. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox.

### Marriage and labor

Bride wealth and clan negotiation are real in some marriages. Minnesota law still stands. A wedding custom is not a crime scene. Mandated reporting still stands.

Women’s labor — market, factory, farm, professional second generation — sits next to a patrilineal clan. Both can be true in the same room. Ask who should be in the room.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Hmong History
paragraphs: St. Paul national hub. Compass ~94% Twin Cities. HAP; Hmong Cultural Center; Hmong Museum; Hmongtown 2004; Hmong Village 2010; New Year since 1977.
Partners, not a harvest list. Staff are colleagues, not the interpreter. Guest at New Year. A market visit does not make you the expert.

St. Paul is one of the largest urban Hmong communities in the world. That is why this page has to be as complete as the African American and Somali intelligences — because this department will meet this community on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment.

### Places, not a blob

East Side St. Paul; Frogtown; University Avenue and Little Mekong; Hmongtown Marketplace (opened 2004, a former lumberyard); Hmong Village (2010, Johnson Parkway); Brooklyn Center; Maplewood; a small Greater Minnesota share. Compass: about 94 percent Twin Cities.

### Institutions

Partners include Hmong American Partnership; Hmong Cultural Center of Minnesota; Hmong Museum; Center for Hmong Studies (Concordia); Hmong 18 Council and clan structures some families name; CECLC as a department door — not the whole community.

Public calendar: Hmong New Year in St. Paul (weekend near the end of November, RiverCentre in recent years; held since 1977); Hmong International Freedom Festival at Como Park — sport, not consultation. Hmong American Day / May 14 is literacy. A calendar click is not community engagement.

Hmong staff are colleagues, not a stand-in for the community. A New Year visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Hmoob / Moob — the heart of a people
paragraphs: Peoplehood without a state. Kwvtij. Face. Asian in a U.S. checkbox that does not fit.
Do not fold this household into “Asian Pacific.” Do not copy a Somali or African American sentence onto this page.

To be Hmong is to be a people without a state and with a long memory of being used by states.

### In Minnesota

In Minnesota it sits inside another fact: many Hmong Minnesotans are Asian in a U.S. racial order that files them under a checkbox that also holds Chinese, Indian, and Korean histories they do not share; veterans of a war the United States ran and then classified; Christians and traditionalists in the same cousin-line.

### Kwvtij

Kwvtij — clan-kin — is not a metaphor. Face, ancestor obligation, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. A smile is not consent.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
paragraphs: Clan; ancestors; txiv neeb; Christianity; face; hu plig / poob plig; market and farm.
You work with these. You do not perform them. If they name a healer, listen. Do not make the healer the case plan unless they asked.

These concepts recur. They express differently by clan, church, generation, and how this family lives ritual. They are hypotheses — not a script for the person in front of you.

### Clan

About 18. Patrilineal. Exogamous. The last name is not a decoration. Staff do not use it as an icebreaker. If the family names it, you listen.

### Ancestors

Household ritual, soul, and funeral are not extras. A missed funeral obligation can be a crisis in the family when the English form thinks the crisis is a missed appointment.

### Txiv neeb

Traditional healer / shaman. An altar in a living room is not a case plan and not a museum. If they name a healer, listen. The healer is the case plan when they asked. A soul-calling is not DHS programming.

### Christianity

Catholic, Protestant, evangelical streams are large in Minnesota Hmong life. Church can be the information channel. It is not “the community.”

### Face and harmony

Direct refusal may be costly. A yes that is courtesy is not a signature. Ask again, plainly, without humiliation.

### Hu plig / poob plig

Soul-calling and soul-loss are meaning systems some families use for illness, fright, and developmental difference. They can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

### Farming and market

Garden plots, farmers markets, and the two St. Paul markets are economy and culture. A food-court visit is not consultation.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing
paragraphs: Traditional household religion and Christianity both live here. MDH 2014: late autism identification, stigma, unclear meaning of the word.
Do not make a pastor or a txiv neeb the case plan unless this family asked. Illness meaning may not be the DSM sentence.

Traditional Hmong religion is household-centered: ancestors, spirits (dab), shamanic healing, soul. It is not a Sunday service you can BCC. Christianity arrived through mission and camp and is now ordinary in Minnesota — sometimes in the same extended family as a traditional altar.

### Pastor and healer

A pastor or a txiv neeb is the case plan when this family asked. Traditional practice is not witchcraft. Church is not the evolved version.

### Funerals

Funerals can last days and gather clan. Burial timing, animal offering in traditional practice, and who must be there are not delays for your convenience. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it.

Illness meaning may not be the DSM sentence. MDH’s 2014 qualitative work with Hmong parents on autism: unclear meaning of the word, stigma, waiting to share concerns, professionals who were not responsive. Late identification is a gate. Stigma is a gate. English-only is a gate.

sections.heading: Greetings
paragraphs: Elders first. Nyob zoo. Clan last name.
Do not force a handshake on an elder. Do not import Somali or African American greeting rules.

Elders first. A slight bow or nod with an older person is safer than a hard handshake you assume is universal. Many second-generation people will shake hands in English-language rooms. Follow this room.

### Names

Nyob zoo is a common White Hmong greeting. English “hello” is ordinary. Say the name. The clan name is the last name; it is not optional.

Somali right-hand rules and the Black nod are not this page. This is not those grammars.

Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
paragraphs: Last name is clan name. Eighteen common clans. Given names may be Hmong, English, or both.
Ask how to say it. Do not joke about “too many Vangs.” Do not treat unmatched last names as fraud by default.

The last name is a clan name. Eighteen common clans. People who share it may be kin in a way the database cannot see — or strangers who still should not marry. Every Lee is not related. Two Lees in a household are not automatically a married couple; they may be clan-kin of a kind your form does not have a box for.

### Given names

Given names may be Hmong, English, or both. Soul names, nicknames, and generation names exist. The form that demands first-middle-last and a hyphen will invent a person.

Pronounce it. Ask. “Too many Vangs” is a closed door, not a joke.

Women may or may not take a husband’s clan name in U.S. records. Ask how to file. A mother and child who do not share a last name is not a fraud signal until you have a reason.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
paragraphs: Hmong New Year (St. Paul, since 1977). May 14, 1975 / Hmong American Day. Freedom Festival.
A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement.

Hmong New Year — traditionally after harvest; in St. Paul a public weekend near the end of November since 1977. Courtship ball-toss (pov pob) is public history at the celebration, not a file. Guest, not researcher.

### May 14 and public life

May 14 — General Vang Pao’s 1975 departure from Laos; marked in Minnesota as Hmong American / Hmong-Lao veterans memory. Literacy.

Fourth of July / Freedom Festival soccer and sport at Como Park — community public life, not consultation.

Lunar and household ritual dates vary by family and by traditional vs Christian practice. Ask. “Asian holiday” does not belong on a case note.

sections.heading: Education
paragraphs: Compass: ~80% high school or higher (25+); ~26% bachelor’s or higher. Majority of children U.S.-born.
A parent who speaks fluent Hmong and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Put the dialect on the line.

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Hmong Minnesotans 25 and older, about 80 percent high school or higher; about 26 percent bachelor’s or higher. A majority of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### Language at the door

White Hmong and Mong Leng are not always interchangeable on an interpreter line. English-only parent forms are a gate. A parent who speaks fluent Hmong and limited English is not illiterate.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room which treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus poverty plus a school that never learned the name.

sections.heading: Etiquette
paragraphs: Shoes, food, elders, altars, funerals that last days.
Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Do not photograph the altar.

Shoes off in many homes. Accept a little food if offered. Elders first. Feet pointed at an altar or a person, in a traditional household, is not the default.

### Time and the plan

Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

A living room is not a photograph of the altar. Ritual objects are not for touching. An elder is not entertainment explaining shamanism.

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
paragraphs: White Hmong and Mong Leng. Compass: ~77% language other than English (5+); ~31% LEP. Tonal language. RPA.
Confirm the variety. A Hmong interpreter who does not speak this dialect is a closed door. Do not take a smile as consent.

White Hmong and Green Hmong / Mong Leng. Confirm the variety. An interpreter labeled Hmong who does not speak this household’s dialect is still a closed door. RPA is the common written form; many elders do not read it. Second-generation English is common. Compass: among those 5 and older, about 77 percent speak a language other than English; about 31 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number.

### Tone and yes

Hmong is tonal. The doubled vowels in RPA mark tone, not extra sound. You do not need to become a linguist. You need to put the variety on the interpreter request.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. A smile is not consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

A Hmong coworker is not the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
paragraphs: Early-marriage history; disability stigma; deportation to Laos; 1990s youth violence as history not a last-name score; LGBTQ people exist.
Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Marriage, disability, status

Early marriage and bride-wealth patterns exist in history and in some present families. Minnesota age-of-consent and forced-marriage law still stand. You follow the law. You still see a family, not a crime scene walking in.

Disability stigma and late autism identification are documented (MDH 2014; later qualitative work). Under-identification is the Hmong pattern in Minnesota autism surveillance; Somali over-concern is a different page. The two are not the same.

Deportation to Laos of people with certain convictions — including people who have lived here since childhood — is current structure, not folklore. It changes who opens the door, who signs, and who will not put a relative’s name on a form. Collect the status the work requires, not more. Fear is not noncompliance.

### History that still sits in the room

1990s youth violence in some St. Paul neighborhoods is a history some families carry. A clan last name is not a gang file.

LGBTQ Hmong Minnesotans exist. You use the name. Outing someone to kin is not culture.

Employee groups may fact-check this page. A hard fact still belongs here.

sections.heading: Health
paragraphs: MDH 2014 qualitative study. Later ADDM-style work: lower identified autism prevalence than white and non-Somali Black — date it. Under-identification is the pattern.
Do not skip screening. Peers who share language. Gender match in maternal care. If they name a healer, listen.

MDH 2014 qualitative study with Hmong community partners: parents unclear what autism meant, delayed sharing concerns, stigma, professionals who were not responsive. Late identification is the finding. Identification is not a community personality. Date the study.

### Under-count

Later Minnesota ADDM-style work has reported lower autism prevalence among Hmong children than among white and non-Somali Black children. Under-count, measurement, and meaning can sit together. Inventing a rate does not help. Skipping screening because “Hmong families don’t have that” does not help.

Chronic disease, trauma, and aging veterans of the Secret War sit in the same clinics as U.S.-born children. Traditional healing and biomedicine are often both in the household. Ask. Co-create. An altar is not a joke. A healer in the story is not a reason to skip the waiver.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it.

Believe reported pain. This history is not Tuskegee and not a generic “Asian stoicism” slide.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
paragraphs: Queer and trans Hmong Minnesotans exist. Conservative clan and church climates can mean silence.
Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture.

Queer and trans Hmong Minnesotans exist. Conservative clan and church climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private Hmong life. You use the name they use. Outing them to an elder is not cultural humility.

### Law

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. A whole people is not a family-values exhibit.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
paragraphs: Traditional dress is public at New Year, not a daily uniform.
Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch.

Traditional dress is public at New Year and not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. “Still wears the costume” is not a clinic question.

### Hair and silver

Hair and head: follow this person. Hair is not for touching. Silver, embroidery, and paj ntaub are art and history, not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.

sections.heading: Music
paragraphs: Qeej at funerals. New Year stages. Christian music in some churches.
A funeral qeej is not staff entertainment. A playlist is not engagement.

The qeej (reed pipe) is ritual and art, especially at funerals. New Year stages hold dance, pop, and Christian music.

### Not entertainment

A playlist is not engagement. A funeral qeej is not entertainment for staff.

sections.heading: Sports
paragraphs: Freedom Festival soccer; ordinary school sport in the second generation.
Sport clubs are not language access.

Soccer and the Freedom Festival matter in public Hmong Minnesota life. Volleyball, flag football, and school sport are ordinary for the second generation.

### Not a case plan

Sport clubs are not language access and not a case plan.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: Oral first. RPA. Minnesota Hmong writers and scholars.
You do not need to quote a novel. You need to know this is not a people without letters.

Oral literature first: proverb, funeral text, clan narrative. RPA made a written public possible.

### Letters

Minnesota and U.S. Hmong writers, scholars, and journalists exist. You do not need to quote a novel. You need to know this is not a people without letters.

sections.heading: Art
paragraphs: Paj ntaub / paaj ntaub. Hmong Cultural Center. Hmong Museum. MNHS 2025 fifty years.
Guest, not researcher. A story cloth is not a case plan.

Paj ntaub / paaj ntaub — story cloth, reverse appliqué, memory sewn when camps and exile made paper unsafe or unavailable. Hmong Cultural Center. Hmong Museum. 2025 Minnesota History Center exhibit on fifty years.

### Guest

Guest. A story cloth is not a case plan. A museum visit is not consultation.

sections.heading: Conflict, War, and the State
paragraphs: Secret War; 1975; camps; later policing and deportation.
A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not use 1975 as a personality.

The Secret War, the walk to Thailand, Ban Vinai, dispersal, secondary migration, and a United States that recruited then delayed asylum — that is the political event. Later: policing, youth violence in some 1990s neighborhoods, and deportation of people with records. A DHS badge is not automatically help.

### Not a personality

1975 is not a personality. A veteran is not a narrator of killing for your professional development.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
paragraphs: Factory, farm, markets, professional second generation, Hmong staff in government.
Hmong employees are not unpaid interpreters. Identity is not a staffing plan.

Factory, farm, small business, professional second generation, public employment. Hmongtown and Hmong Village are commercial hubs. Hmong staff inside the department are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Relationship and the notice

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
paragraphs: Dialect, who is in the room, healer or pastor, late developmental concern, deportation climate.
Confirm variety. Offer gender match. Believe reported pain. Mandated reporting still exists.

Language and dialect. Who is in the room. Gender. An altar or a pastor in the story. Late developmental concern. Deportation climate. A nuclear form that cannot see clan.

### In the encounter

Confirm the variety. Offer gender match. Ask who should hear. Staff are not the interpreter. If they name a healer, listen. Mandated reporting still exists.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
paragraphs: Not Karen, not Lao as synonym, not Vietnamese, not Chinese, not “Asian American” as the file.
Never one Asian module. Ask this household.

Not Karen. Not Lao as a synonym. Not Vietnamese. Not Chinese. Not “Asian American” as the file.

### Open the right page

Open the Karen brief for Karen. Open this for Hmong. Some households are mixed. Ask this household.

Miao in China is a related but not identical administrative story. A St. Paul family does not need a lecture on Chinese taxonomy.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
paragraphs: Compass ACS 2019–2023: ~99,912; 94.4% metro; 38.3% 17 or younger; poverty 9.1%; owner 63.2%. Pew MN ~95,000 Hmong-alone. Date them.
A rate is not the person. Autism under-ID and child-welfare figures are gates.

Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Hmong cultural community: about 99,912; Twin Cities 94.4%; Greater Minnesota 5.6%; age 17 or younger 38.3%; 65+ about 3.7%; foreign-born 33.4%; language other than English (age 5+) 77.3%; English less than “very well” 31.1%; high school or higher (25+) 80.3%; bachelor’s or higher 26.4%; median household income about $90,000 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 9.1%; owner-occupied 63.2%; average household size 4.40.

### Other counts

Pew, May 2025 (2021–2023 ACS / 2023): U.S. Hmong-alone about 330,000; including combinations about 360,000; Minnesota about 95,000 on that count; median age about 26.8.

Counts disagree because definitions disagree. Date the number. A young age structure is not a personality. A poverty rate that fell over decades is not proof the gates closed.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
paragraphs: Compass, Pew May 2025, MNHS, HAP, Hmong Cultural Center, Hmong Museum, MDH 2014, Center for Hmong Studies.
Learn on your own time. Do not make a Hmong colleague your unpaid tutor. Pay partners.

Minnesota Compass Hmong profile (ACS 2019–2023). Pew fact sheet on Hmong in the U.S. (May 2025). Minnesota Historical Society / MNHS Hmong in Minnesota; MNopedia. Hmong Cultural Center of Minnesota. Hmong Museum. Hmong American Partnership. Center for Hmong Studies, Concordia University, St. Paul. MDH 2014 qualitative autism study with community partners. Chaxiong 2022. EthnoMed Hmong page for clan-name spellings — a clinical literacy door, not a bible.

### Learn on your own time

CECLC is a door, not the whole community. Learn on your own time. A Hmong colleague is not an unpaid tutor. Pay partners.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
paragraphs: White Hmong vs Mong Leng; clan last names on nuclear forms; English IEPs; late autism identification; deportation climate; harvesting Hmong staff; eList comment periods.

Confirm the dialect. Ask who is in the room. Toolkit disposition on the packet. If the family cannot run the exception in English, the cap is the policy. Statute may still stand. Name who the packet was built for.

Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: an interpreter labeled Hmong who does not speak White Hmong or Mong Leng as this household speaks it is a closed door. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: the last name is a clan name. The database that cannot see unmatched last names without a fraud flag is a gate.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare and disability: late identification and stigma are documented. Help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score.

Deportation climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater.

Workforce: Hmong staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned to say mung.

sections.heading: Why this can be missed
paragraphs: “Asian” on a form, one interpreter labeled Hmong, and a shamanism anecdote is not a brief. Treating everyone the same will not see White Hmong versus Mong Leng, clan as social order, a war this state recruited, or a New Year that is not Chinese New Year.

sections.heading: How they got to Minnesota
paragraphs: The United States ran a Secret War in Laos. Hmong forces allied with the CIA. After 1975 came persecution, Thai camps, and refugee resettlement. St. Paul is a national hub. This is not a generic immigrant story and not a Laos footnote. Deportation and racial-profiling anxiety are current structure, not folklore.

sections.heading: Clan, naming, language
paragraphs: Clan — about eighteen common clans — organizes marriage, help, and who speaks. Naming does not match first, middle, and last. White Hmong and Green Hmong (Mong Leng) are not always interchangeable on an interpreter line. Second-generation English is real. Clan is not yours to collect as an icebreaker. It is still how some families decide.

sections.heading: Healing and disability
paragraphs: Traditional healing and shamanism (txiv neeb) shape what illness means for many families; Christianity is also widespread. MDH 2014: Hmong parents of children with autism described late identification, unclear meaning of the word, stigma, and professionals who were not responsive. Under-identification sits next to Somali over-concern in the same state. Both are system plus meaning.

sections.heading: Collective, ancestors, face
paragraphs: Family and clan reputation matter. Respect for elders and ancestors is expected. Resilience is a fact of survival, not a compliment you put on a poster. Harmony can look like not contradicting a professional in the room — and then not following a plan that violated the household.

sections.heading: At the desk
paragraphs: Ask which Hmong the family speaks. Book that dialect. Ask who should be in the room. Do not skip traditional healers if the family names them, and do not make the healer the case plan if they did not. Hmong New Year in St. Paul is public; if you attend, you are a guest, not a field researcher.

sections.heading: In the work
paragraphs: Child welfare, waiver exceptions, and “family” definitions built for a nuclear English household will miss who actually cares for the child. Noticing that gap is casework, not a festival booth.

sections.heading: Minnesota context
paragraphs: Ancestry: Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 99,900. About 94% Twin Cities. Pew (May 2025) Hmong-alone Minnesota near 95,000. Date the number. Source: Minnesota Compass / ACS 2019–2023; Pew Research Center, May 2025.

Languages: White Hmong and Green Hmong (Mong Leng) are not always interchangeable. About 77% age 5+ speak a language other than English; about 31% speak English less than very well. Source: Minnesota Compass / ACS 2019–2023.

sections.heading: Ways to connect
paragraphs: Hmong American Partnership — Workforce, family, and community services. — https://www.hapmn.org/
Hmong Cultural Center (St. Paul) — Language, arts, and Hmong New Year. Public history, not a case plan.
Hmong Museum — History as Hmong Minnesotans tell it.

sections.heading: In the work
paragraphs: DHS: CECLC; language access in White Hmong and Mong Leng. Do not fold this community into “Asian.”
Unit: Clan leaders and traditional healers are gatekeepers some families name — not staff icebreakers.
You: Hmong New Year in St. Paul is a public gathering. If you attend, you are a guest. Do not write what you saw into a case file as expertise.

community.title: Hmong Minnesota

chapters.body:
This brief is about Hmong people — Hmoob in White Hmong, Moob in Green Hmong / Mong Leng. It is a people with ancient roots in southern China, a highland life in Laos, and a Minnesota community built after 1975. Pronounce it mung. The H is silent. If you say Huh-mong in a lobby, you have already told the household you did not study.

### Who this is

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Hmong ancestry near 99,900. About 94 percent Twin Cities, about 6 percent Greater Minnesota. About 38 percent age 17 or younger. About 33 percent foreign-born — which means a majority of this community was born here. Pew (May 2025, 2021–2023 ACS) put Minnesota near 95,000 on a Hmong-alone count and named it the second-largest state community after California. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

St. Paul is a national hub. It is not the map. Frogtown, the East Side, Little Mekong on University Avenue, Hmongtown Marketplace, Hmong Village, Brooklyn Center, Maplewood, and a smaller Greater Minnesota share are not one client.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Secret War veteran who came through Ban Vinai, a Christian grandmother, a txiv neeb (traditional healer) whose altar is in the living room, a U.S.-born nurse, a farmer at the summer market, a college student who uses English with friends and Hmong with an elder, a person who left clan obligation and still shows up at New Year — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### Who this is not

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Chinese New Year. It is not Karen, Vietnamese, Lao as a synonym, Cambodian, or a generic Southeast Asian interpreter. Shared continent is not shared culture.

### How to read this

Read it as an orientation. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

The facts that follow are meant to help you meet people well — how family is named, what respect looks like, what a greeting carries, what a form may land on. Counts are dated. History is here so the meeting is clearer, not so you deliver a lecture.
chapters.evidence: Hmong (pronounced mung; H silent). White Hmong and Green Hmong / Mong Leng. Compass ACS 2019–2023 near 99,900. Census Asian mixes this with Chinese, Indian, Vietnamese, Karen. Date the number you cite.
chapters.practitioner: There is no single Hmong client. Defer to this family. Do not open a Karen or Lao case with this page. Say mung.
chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Hmong peoplehood is older than Laos, older than the CIA file, and older than the refugee camp. Oral history and scholarship place origin in southern China; movement into the highlands of what became Laos, Vietnam, and Thailand under pressure from imperial states. Statelessness is a political fact, not a personality.

### Clan, language, writing

There is no Hmong nation-state. Clan, language, agriculture, and ritual organized life without a capital city. Writing systems came late. The Romanized Popular Alphabet (RPA), developed in the 1950s in Laos, is the common Latin script in Minnesota. Historically the language was oral. Paj ntaub / paaj ntaub — story cloth and embroidery — carried memory when paper did not.

### White Hmong and Green Hmong

Two large dialect-and-dress groups live in Minnesota: White Hmong (Hmoob Dawb) and Green Hmong, also called Blue Hmong or Mong Leng (Hmoob Leeg / Moob). The names come from dress, not politics. The dialects are close and not always interchangeable in an interpreter. Green Hmong often write the people-name without the H: Moob. That is the same instruction as this page: say mung.

### What people brought

Clan, ancestor obligation, shamanic healing and Christianity both, farming knowledge, oral skill, a memory of being recruited to fight someone else’s war and then left. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled “Hmong.”
chapters.evidence: Southern China origin; highland Laos; no nation-state. RPA writing in the 1950s. Oral literature and paj ntaub older than the camp file.
chapters.practitioner: History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with embroidery tourism.
chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
Homeland is not one flag. Southern China remains a Hmong (Miao) geography. The Laos highlands — Xieng Khouang, Long Tieng, the places named in veteran stories — are the origin of most Minnesota families.

### Diaspora

There are Hmong communities in Vietnam, Thailand, Burma/Myanmar, and a global diaspora: California, Minnesota, Wisconsin, North Carolina, France, Australia.

Pew (May 2025): California is the largest U.S. state community; Minnesota second; Wisconsin third. Fresno and Sacramento sit next to Minneapolis–St. Paul as sister maps. Secondary migration built Minnesota. Church sponsors scattered people; clan pulled them back together.

### In Minnesota

St. Paul is the national urban hub. East Side. Frogtown. University Avenue / Little Mekong. Ramsey County. Brooklyn Center and inner-ring suburbs. A small Greater Minnesota share. Frogtown is not the whole. The person in front of you may not have been to Laos.
chapters.evidence: Laos highlands; China; Vietnam; Thailand; U.S. concentration in California, Minnesota, Wisconsin. St. Paul is a hub, not the map.
chapters.practitioner: Do not assume Frogtown. Do not assume they have been to Laos.
chapters.title: The Geography of the Hmong World

chapters.body:
If the Great Migration is the foundational demographic event of modern Black America, and 1991 of Somali Minnesota, the Secret War and 1975 are the foundational event of Hmong Minnesota.

### The Secret War

From 1961 to 1975 the United States, through the CIA, recruited Hmong forces under General Vang Pao to fight in Laos — a war the Geneva Accords had said should not be there. Hmong soldiers blocked supply lines and died in large numbers. Boys were recruited. When the United States left in 1975, the Pathet Lao and Vietnamese forces treated Hmong allied families as the enemy.

### Airlift, walk, camps

May 12–14, 1975: airlift from Long Tieng. About 2,500 people in those days. General Vang Pao left May 14. Minnesota later marked that date. Most people were not on the planes. They walked. Thai camps followed — Ban Vinai among the named ones. Years. Then resettlement.

### Minnesota

The first Hmong family in Minnesota, Dang Her and Shoua Moua, arrived in December 1975. Church and voluntary-agency sponsors (Lutheran, Catholic, and others) placed people across the country so no one state would “take too many.” Clan and secondary migration undid the scatter. St. Paul became a hub because people chose each other.

U.S. policy at first treated Hmong people as “too primitive” for asylum. The Indochina Migration and Refugee Assistance Act had to be amended. That sentence is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech you give the family.
chapters.evidence: CIA Secret War 1961–1975; Vang Pao; May 1975 airlift and flight; Thai camps including Ban Vinai; first Minnesota family December 1975; secondary migration.
chapters.practitioner: If you only know “refugee,” you will miss the 20-year-old who has never lived in Laos and still cannot get Mong Leng in the lobby.
chapters.title: The Secret War, 1975, and the Camps — Foundational Event

chapters.body:
Clan organizes family. About 18 clans are commonly named among Hmong from Laos now in the United States. The clan name is the last name: Chang, Cheng, Chue, Fang, Hang, Her, Khang, Kong, Kue, Lee, Lor, Moua, Pha, Thao, Vang, Vue, Xiong, Yang — English spellings of Hmong names. Same last name often means same clan. Marriage is supposed to be outside the clan.

### Household size

Households are larger than a nuclear English form. Compass: average household size about 4.4. Elders, in-laws, adult children, and clan obligation sit in the same week. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox.

### Marriage and labor

Bride wealth and clan negotiation are real in some marriages. Minnesota law still stands. A wedding custom is not a crime scene. Mandated reporting still stands.

Women’s labor — market, factory, farm, professional second generation — sits next to a patrilineal clan. Both can be true in the same room. Ask who should be in the room.
chapters.evidence: About 18 clans; patrilineal; marry outside the clan. Compass average household size about 4.4.
chapters.practitioner: Ask who should be in the room. A nuclear English form already has a who. Clan is not an icebreaker.
chapters.title: Family

chapters.body:
St. Paul is one of the largest urban Hmong communities in the world. That is why this page has to be as complete as the African American and Somali intelligences — because this department will meet this community on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment.

### Places, not a blob

East Side St. Paul; Frogtown; University Avenue and Little Mekong; Hmongtown Marketplace (opened 2004, a former lumberyard); Hmong Village (2010, Johnson Parkway); Brooklyn Center; Maplewood; a small Greater Minnesota share. Compass: about 94 percent Twin Cities.

### Institutions

Partners include Hmong American Partnership; Hmong Cultural Center of Minnesota; Hmong Museum; Center for Hmong Studies (Concordia); Hmong 18 Council and clan structures some families name; CECLC as a department door — not the whole community.

Public calendar: Hmong New Year in St. Paul (weekend near the end of November, RiverCentre in recent years; held since 1977); Hmong International Freedom Festival at Como Park — sport, not consultation. Hmong American Day / May 14 is literacy. A calendar click is not community engagement.

Hmong staff are colleagues, not a stand-in for the community. A New Year visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.
chapters.evidence: St. Paul national hub. Compass ~94% Twin Cities. HAP; Hmong Cultural Center; Hmong Museum; Hmongtown 2004; Hmong Village 2010; New Year since 1977.
chapters.practitioner: Partners, not a harvest list. Staff are colleagues, not the interpreter. Guest at New Year. A market visit does not make you the expert.
chapters.title: Minnesota and Hmong History

chapters.body:
To be Hmong is to be a people without a state and with a long memory of being used by states.

### In Minnesota

In Minnesota it sits inside another fact: many Hmong Minnesotans are Asian in a U.S. racial order that files them under a checkbox that also holds Chinese, Indian, and Korean histories they do not share; veterans of a war the United States ran and then classified; Christians and traditionalists in the same cousin-line.

### Kwvtij

Kwvtij — clan-kin — is not a metaphor. Face, ancestor obligation, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. A smile is not consent.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization.
chapters.evidence: Peoplehood without a state. Kwvtij. Face. Asian in a U.S. checkbox that does not fit.
chapters.practitioner: Do not fold this household into “Asian Pacific.” Do not copy a Somali or African American sentence onto this page.
chapters.title: Hmoob / Moob — the heart of a people

chapters.body:
These concepts recur. They express differently by clan, church, generation, and how this family lives ritual. They are hypotheses — not a script for the person in front of you.

### Clan

About 18. Patrilineal. Exogamous. The last name is not a decoration. Staff do not use it as an icebreaker. If the family names it, you listen.

### Ancestors

Household ritual, soul, and funeral are not extras. A missed funeral obligation can be a crisis in the family when the English form thinks the crisis is a missed appointment.

### Txiv neeb

Traditional healer / shaman. An altar in a living room is not a case plan and not a museum. If they name a healer, listen. The healer is the case plan when they asked. A soul-calling is not DHS programming.

### Christianity

Catholic, Protestant, evangelical streams are large in Minnesota Hmong life. Church can be the information channel. It is not “the community.”

### Face and harmony

Direct refusal may be costly. A yes that is courtesy is not a signature. Ask again, plainly, without humiliation.

### Hu plig / poob plig

Soul-calling and soul-loss are meaning systems some families use for illness, fright, and developmental difference. They can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

### Farming and market

Garden plots, farmers markets, and the two St. Paul markets are economy and culture. A food-court visit is not consultation.
chapters.evidence: Clan; ancestors; txiv neeb; Christianity; face; hu plig / poob plig; market and farm.
chapters.practitioner: You work with these. You do not perform them. If they name a healer, listen. Do not make the healer the case plan unless they asked.
chapters.title: Core Concepts

chapters.body:
Traditional Hmong religion is household-centered: ancestors, spirits (dab), shamanic healing, soul. It is not a Sunday service you can BCC. Christianity arrived through mission and camp and is now ordinary in Minnesota — sometimes in the same extended family as a traditional altar.

### Pastor and healer

A pastor or a txiv neeb is the case plan when this family asked. Traditional practice is not witchcraft. Church is not the evolved version.

### Funerals

Funerals can last days and gather clan. Burial timing, animal offering in traditional practice, and who must be there are not delays for your convenience. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it.

Illness meaning may not be the DSM sentence. MDH’s 2014 qualitative work with Hmong parents on autism: unclear meaning of the word, stigma, waiting to share concerns, professionals who were not responsive. Late identification is a gate. Stigma is a gate. English-only is a gate.
chapters.evidence: Traditional household religion and Christianity both live here. MDH 2014: late autism identification, stigma, unclear meaning of the word.
chapters.practitioner: Do not make a pastor or a txiv neeb the case plan unless this family asked. Illness meaning may not be the DSM sentence.
chapters.title: Religion and Healing

chapters.body:
Elders first. A slight bow or nod with an older person is safer than a hard handshake you assume is universal. Many second-generation people will shake hands in English-language rooms. Follow this room.

### Names

Nyob zoo is a common White Hmong greeting. English “hello” is ordinary. Say the name. The clan name is the last name; it is not optional.

Somali right-hand rules and the Black nod are not this page. This is not those grammars.

Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default.
chapters.evidence: Elders first. Nyob zoo. Clan last name.
chapters.practitioner: Do not force a handshake on an elder. Do not import Somali or African American greeting rules.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
The last name is a clan name. Eighteen common clans. People who share it may be kin in a way the database cannot see — or strangers who still should not marry. Every Lee is not related. Two Lees in a household are not automatically a married couple; they may be clan-kin of a kind your form does not have a box for.

### Given names

Given names may be Hmong, English, or both. Soul names, nicknames, and generation names exist. The form that demands first-middle-last and a hyphen will invent a person.

Pronounce it. Ask. “Too many Vangs” is a closed door, not a joke.

Women may or may not take a husband’s clan name in U.S. records. Ask how to file. A mother and child who do not share a last name is not a fraud signal until you have a reason.
chapters.evidence: Last name is clan name. Eighteen common clans. Given names may be Hmong, English, or both.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to say it. Do not joke about “too many Vangs.” Do not treat unmatched last names as fraud by default.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
Hmong New Year — traditionally after harvest; in St. Paul a public weekend near the end of November since 1977. Courtship ball-toss (pov pob) is public history at the celebration, not a file. Guest, not researcher.

### May 14 and public life

May 14 — General Vang Pao’s 1975 departure from Laos; marked in Minnesota as Hmong American / Hmong-Lao veterans memory. Literacy.

Fourth of July / Freedom Festival soccer and sport at Como Park — community public life, not consultation.

Lunar and household ritual dates vary by family and by traditional vs Christian practice. Ask. “Asian holiday” does not belong on a case note.
chapters.evidence: Hmong New Year (St. Paul, since 1977). May 14, 1975 / Hmong American Day. Freedom Festival.
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement.
chapters.title: Dates of Significance

chapters.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Hmong Minnesotans 25 and older, about 80 percent high school or higher; about 26 percent bachelor’s or higher. A majority of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### Language at the door

White Hmong and Mong Leng are not always interchangeable on an interpreter line. English-only parent forms are a gate. A parent who speaks fluent Hmong and limited English is not illiterate.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room which treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus poverty plus a school that never learned the name.
chapters.evidence: Compass: ~80% high school or higher (25+); ~26% bachelor’s or higher. Majority of children U.S.-born.
chapters.practitioner: A parent who speaks fluent Hmong and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Put the dialect on the line.
chapters.title: Education

chapters.body:
Shoes off in many homes. Accept a little food if offered. Elders first. Feet pointed at an altar or a person, in a traditional household, is not the default.

### Time and the plan

Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

A living room is not a photograph of the altar. Ritual objects are not for touching. An elder is not entertainment explaining shamanism.

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.
chapters.evidence: Shoes, food, elders, altars, funerals that last days.
chapters.practitioner: Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Do not photograph the altar.
chapters.title: Etiquette

chapters.body:
White Hmong and Green Hmong / Mong Leng. Confirm the variety. An interpreter labeled Hmong who does not speak this household’s dialect is still a closed door. RPA is the common written form; many elders do not read it. Second-generation English is common. Compass: among those 5 and older, about 77 percent speak a language other than English; about 31 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number.

### Tone and yes

Hmong is tonal. The doubled vowels in RPA mark tone, not extra sound. You do not need to become a linguist. You need to put the variety on the interpreter request.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. A smile is not consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

A Hmong coworker is not the interpreter.
chapters.evidence: White Hmong and Mong Leng. Compass: ~77% language other than English (5+); ~31% LEP. Tonal language. RPA.
chapters.practitioner: Confirm the variety. A Hmong interpreter who does not speak this dialect is a closed door. Do not take a smile as consent.
chapters.title: Language and Communication

chapters.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Marriage, disability, status

Early marriage and bride-wealth patterns exist in history and in some present families. Minnesota age-of-consent and forced-marriage law still stand. You follow the law. You still see a family, not a crime scene walking in.

Disability stigma and late autism identification are documented (MDH 2014; later qualitative work). Under-identification is the Hmong pattern in Minnesota autism surveillance; Somali over-concern is a different page. The two are not the same.

Deportation to Laos of people with certain convictions — including people who have lived here since childhood — is current structure, not folklore. It changes who opens the door, who signs, and who will not put a relative’s name on a form. Collect the status the work requires, not more. Fear is not noncompliance.

### History that still sits in the room

1990s youth violence in some St. Paul neighborhoods is a history some families carry. A clan last name is not a gang file.

LGBTQ Hmong Minnesotans exist. You use the name. Outing someone to kin is not culture.

Employee groups may fact-check this page. A hard fact still belongs here.
chapters.evidence: Early-marriage history; disability stigma; deportation to Laos; 1990s youth violence as history not a last-name score; LGBTQ people exist.
chapters.practitioner: Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.
chapters.title: Other Considerations

chapters.body:
MDH 2014 qualitative study with Hmong community partners: parents unclear what autism meant, delayed sharing concerns, stigma, professionals who were not responsive. Late identification is the finding. Identification is not a community personality. Date the study.

### Under-count

Later Minnesota ADDM-style work has reported lower autism prevalence among Hmong children than among white and non-Somali Black children. Under-count, measurement, and meaning can sit together. Inventing a rate does not help. Skipping screening because “Hmong families don’t have that” does not help.

Chronic disease, trauma, and aging veterans of the Secret War sit in the same clinics as U.S.-born children. Traditional healing and biomedicine are often both in the household. Ask. Co-create. An altar is not a joke. A healer in the story is not a reason to skip the waiver.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it.

Believe reported pain. This history is not Tuskegee and not a generic “Asian stoicism” slide.
chapters.evidence: MDH 2014 qualitative study. Later ADDM-style work: lower identified autism prevalence than white and non-Somali Black — date it. Under-identification is the pattern.
chapters.practitioner: Do not skip screening. Peers who share language. Gender match in maternal care. If they name a healer, listen.
chapters.title: Health

chapters.body:
Queer and trans Hmong Minnesotans exist. Conservative clan and church climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private Hmong life. You use the name they use. Outing them to an elder is not cultural humility.

### Law

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. A whole people is not a family-values exhibit.
chapters.evidence: Queer and trans Hmong Minnesotans exist. Conservative clan and church climates can mean silence.
chapters.practitioner: Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture.
chapters.title: LGBTQ

chapters.body:
Traditional dress is public at New Year and not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. “Still wears the costume” is not a clinic question.

### Hair and silver

Hair and head: follow this person. Hair is not for touching. Silver, embroidery, and paj ntaub are art and history, not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.
chapters.evidence: Traditional dress is public at New Year, not a daily uniform.
chapters.practitioner: Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch.
chapters.title: Hair, Dress, and Body

chapters.body:
The qeej (reed pipe) is ritual and art, especially at funerals. New Year stages hold dance, pop, and Christian music.

### Not entertainment

A playlist is not engagement. A funeral qeej is not entertainment for staff.
chapters.evidence: Qeej at funerals. New Year stages. Christian music in some churches.
chapters.practitioner: A funeral qeej is not staff entertainment. A playlist is not engagement.
chapters.title: Music

chapters.body:
Soccer and the Freedom Festival matter in public Hmong Minnesota life. Volleyball, flag football, and school sport are ordinary for the second generation.

### Not a case plan

Sport clubs are not language access and not a case plan.
chapters.evidence: Freedom Festival soccer; ordinary school sport in the second generation.
chapters.practitioner: Sport clubs are not language access.
chapters.title: Sports

chapters.body:
Oral literature first: proverb, funeral text, clan narrative. RPA made a written public possible.

### Letters

Minnesota and U.S. Hmong writers, scholars, and journalists exist. You do not need to quote a novel. You need to know this is not a people without letters.
chapters.evidence: Oral first. RPA. Minnesota Hmong writers and scholars.
chapters.practitioner: You do not need to quote a novel. You need to know this is not a people without letters.
chapters.title: Literature

chapters.body:
Paj ntaub / paaj ntaub — story cloth, reverse appliqué, memory sewn when camps and exile made paper unsafe or unavailable. Hmong Cultural Center. Hmong Museum. 2025 Minnesota History Center exhibit on fifty years.

### Guest

Guest. A story cloth is not a case plan. A museum visit is not consultation.
chapters.evidence: Paj ntaub / paaj ntaub. Hmong Cultural Center. Hmong Museum. MNHS 2025 fifty years.
chapters.practitioner: Guest, not researcher. A story cloth is not a case plan.
chapters.title: Art

chapters.body:
The Secret War, the walk to Thailand, Ban Vinai, dispersal, secondary migration, and a United States that recruited then delayed asylum — that is the political event. Later: policing, youth violence in some 1990s neighborhoods, and deportation of people with records. A DHS badge is not automatically help.

### Not a personality

1975 is not a personality. A veteran is not a narrator of killing for your professional development.
chapters.evidence: Secret War; 1975; camps; later policing and deportation.
chapters.practitioner: A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not use 1975 as a personality.
chapters.title: Conflict, War, and the State

chapters.body:
Factory, farm, small business, professional second generation, public employment. Hmongtown and Hmong Village are commercial hubs. Hmong staff inside the department are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Relationship and the notice

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision.
chapters.evidence: Factory, farm, markets, professional second generation, Hmong staff in government.
chapters.practitioner: Hmong employees are not unpaid interpreters. Identity is not a staffing plan.
chapters.title: Work, Markets, and Government

chapters.body:
Language and dialect. Who is in the room. Gender. An altar or a pastor in the story. Late developmental concern. Deportation climate. A nuclear form that cannot see clan.

### In the encounter

Confirm the variety. Offer gender match. Ask who should hear. Staff are not the interpreter. If they name a healer, listen. Mandated reporting still exists.

### Open the right page

Open the Karen brief for Karen. Open this for Hmong. Some households are mixed. Ask this household.

Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Hmong cultural community: about 99,912; Twin Cities 94.4%; Greater Minnesota 5.6%; age 17 or younger 38.3%; 65+ about 3.7%; foreign-born 33.4%; language other than English (age 5+) 77.3%; English less than “very well” 31.1%; high school or higher (25+) 80.3%; bachelor’s or higher 26.4%; median household income about $90,000 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 9.1%; owner-occupied 63.2%; average household size 4.40.

### Other counts

Pew, May 2025 (2021–2023 ACS / 2023): U.S. Hmong-alone about 330,000; including combinations about 360,000; Minnesota about 95,000 on that count; median age about 26.8.

Counts disagree because definitions disagree. Date the number. A young age structure is not a personality. A poverty rate that fell over decades is not proof the gates closed.

chapters.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: an interpreter labeled Hmong who does not speak White Hmong or Mong Leng as this household speaks it is a closed door. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: the last name is a clan name. The database that cannot see unmatched last names without a fraud flag is a gate.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare and disability: late identification and stigma are documented. Help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score.

Deportation climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater.

Workforce: Hmong staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned to say mung.

frame: Open this brief when the household is Hmong. Say mung. The chapters cover clan, language, Minnesota life, and history after 1975. They are a starting point, not a verdict on the person in front of you.

Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity. Practitioner-based means Tuesday: White Hmong or Mong Leng on the interpreter line; clan as household not icebreaker; no harvesting Hmong staff; do not make a txiv neeb or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Employee groups may fact-check. They do not veto clan, late autism identification, or deportation anxiety because a Minimization room is uncomfortable.

Counts disagree. Compass (ACS 2019–2023) near 99,900; Pew’s Hmong-alone Minnesota figure near 95,000. About 94 percent Twin Cities. About 38 percent age 17 or younger. A majority were born here. Date the number. 1975 is literacy, not a speech you give the family.

intelligenceGuide.stand: Pronounce it mung — the H is silent. St. Paul is a national hub because Hmong forces allied with the United States in Laos, and after 1975 came persecution, Thai camps, and resettlement. This brief is an orientation to Hmong Minnesota. It is not a Census “Asian” mash, not Karen, and not Chinese New Year. Start with this family.

sections.heading: Begin here
paragraphs: Pronounce it kah-REN. Karen is not Burmese, not Hmong, and not “Asian.” S’gaw and Pwo are not one interpreter — put the dialect on the line. Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota towns such as Worthington and Albert Lea are part of this picture. A smile is not agreement with the plan. Start with this family.
Karen Minnesota is its own people — not Burmese as a synonym. Always defer to this household.
Not “also Asian.” Not Burmese as a synonym. Not a refugee souvenir. This brief is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Keep in mind
paragraphs: Open this brief when the household is Karen. Say kah-REN. Ask S’gaw or Pwo. Rural Minnesota is not an afterthought.

Evidence-based means dated counts, law, history, disparity.
