chapters.body:
This brief is about Latino / Hispanic Minnesota as a U.S. administrative umbrella — not a people. Mexican, Guatemalan, Salvadoran, Puerto Rican, Ecuadorian, Colombian, Cuban, Honduran, Venezuelan, Nicaraguan, Dominican, and others live in this state and do not share a Tuesday. Spanish is not the people. This is the CLAS Spanish line: you will book language access, and you will still ask who is in the home. Indigenous languages are in this state. Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door.

### Who this is

Mexican Minnesota is the largest origin. Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): 229,576; Twin Cities 61.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 38.9 percent — not an afterthought; foreign-born 26.7 percent, which means a majority of Mexican Minnesotans in that vintage were born here; language other than English (age 5+) 58.3 percent; English less than “very well” 23.7 percent; poverty 12.8 percent; median household income about $66,000. Same Compass vintage: Colombian 9,431; Cuban 9,406; Ecuadorian 18,271; Guatemalan 17,172 (nearly half Greater Minnesota); Puerto Rican 21,802 (U.S. citizens — do not run an immigration script by default); Salvadoran 17,571 (civil war and TPS history). Venezuelan, Honduran, Nicaraguan, Dominican and others live here — pattern now, date if you cite. Do not invent a statewide “Latino” total by adding profiles. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

### Who this is not

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one Latino blob, one “Spanish interpreter,” an SSN field on the first screen, and an English IEP written for a household the building never studied.

### How to read this

The diversity inside the umbrella is the point. A Mixtec dairy worker in a southern county, a U.S.-born Mexican professional in a first-ring suburb, a K’iche’-speaking mother in a plant town who does not use Spanish as a home language, a Puerto Rican household that has never been “immigrant,” a Salvadoran family with TPS memory, a Cuban elder, an Afro-Latino student, a queer second-generation kid who uses English with friends and Spanish with a grandmother — share a Census checkbox and do not share a case plan.

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact. Minnesota Nice deletes facts.
chapters.evidence: Latino/Hispanic is a U.S. administrative umbrella — not a people. Mexican is the largest MN origin. Spanish is not one Spanish. Indigenous languages are in this state. Date Compass origin profiles. Do not invent a blob total.
chapters.practitioner: There is no single Latino client. Name the origin. Open that brief. Ask language — including indigenous. Pronounce the name.
chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
There is no single Latino founding. Mexico is the largest Minnesota origin and is itself many peoples: mestizo majority narratives, and Mixtec, Zapotec, and other indigenous nations whose languages may be in the home in this state. Central America is not Mexico. Guatemala holds Maya nations — K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ and others — whose displacement is not a Spanish-accent story. El Salvador’s civil war and TPS history is a different stream. Honduras, Nicaragua. The Andes: Ecuador (indigenous languages may be in the home), Colombia. The Caribbean: Puerto Rico (U.S. citizens), Cuba, Dominican Republic. Venezuela is present — pattern now, date if you cite.

### History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, African enslavement in the Americas, indigenous survival, independence republics, and U.S. labor and foreign policy produced these streams. Shared Spanish is not shared culture. Shared Catholicism is not shared culture. “Hispanic” on a U.S. form is an ethnicity checkbox invented for administration. People in this umbrella check white, Black, American Indian, other, two or more. The form that treats Hispanic as a race has already mashed.

### What people brought

Language (Spanish varieties and indigenous languages), kinship, parish and later evangelical church, work knowledge, and a living memory of states and borders that used them. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Latino” module, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, and a rural plant town or a Minneapolis lobby that had not studied the difference.

History is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with food, dance, or a Heritage Month sentence.
chapters.evidence: Mexico (largest MN share), Central America, Puerto Rico, Andes, Caribbean. Indigenous nations inside those states. Shared Spanish is not shared culture.
chapters.practitioner: History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with food or Heritage Month.
chapters.title: Origins — many peoples, one checkbox

chapters.body:
Homeland is not one flag. Mexico, Guatemala, El Salvador, Puerto Rico, Ecuador, Colombia, Cuba, Honduras, Nicaragua, the Dominican Republic, Venezuela — and indigenous geographies inside those states that do not match the republic’s map.

### Homeland

The U.S. Latino map is California, Texas, Florida, New York, Illinois, and also the Upper Midwest plant and dairy counties that staff in St. Paul still treat as an afterthought.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota the split is the first operational fact. Mexican Compass ACS 2019–2023: 61.1 percent Twin Cities, 38.9 percent Greater Minnesota. Guatemalan Minnesota: nearly half Greater Minnesota. That is not a metro leftover. Food processing, dairy, and southern and western towns built households that a Minneapolis default will miss. Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea, and dairy counties are names you should be able to hold without turning them into a tour.

Metro is not one barrio. West Side St. Paul / District del Sol is historic Mexican Minnesota, not a museum. Lake Street and Phillips in Minneapolis, first-ring suburbs, and scattered apartments near plants are not one client. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to the country on the form.

Open the rural brief beside this page when the household is Greater Minnesota. Place and people are both in the room.
chapters.evidence: Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota — food processing, dairy, southern and western towns. Mexican Compass: 38.9% Greater Minnesota. Guatemalan: nearly half.
chapters.practitioner: A Worthington household is not a Minneapolis default. Do not assume they have been to the country on the form.
chapters.title: The Geography of Latino Minnesota and the Americas

chapters.body:
If the Great Migration is the foundational demographic event of modern Black America, and 1991 of Somali Minnesota, Latino Minnesota is not one event. It is stacked.

### Foundational events

Labor recruitment into agriculture and plants; IRCA-era settlement after 1986; post-1990s Central American displacement; later family and work migration; Puerto Rican movement as internal U.S. migration, not immigration; enforcement waves that reorganize who will open the door.

Mexican migrant farm labor in Minnesota — sugar beet, cannery, seasonal harvest — is older than the current plant map. Settlement followed work, church, and IRCA. Central American streams carry civil war, later gang and state violence, and TPS and asylum histories that are not a Mexican file. Puerto Ricans are U.S. citizens under the Jones Act (1917). Do not run an immigration script by default because the name is Spanish.

### Who you meet

Enforcement is current structure. When raids, rumors of raids, or a visible ICE climate spike, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. A notice mailed to a household afraid to open the door is a closed gate. Do not collect status you do not need. The desk that asks “are you legal?” on visit one has already chosen a who.

The desk in 2026 does not only meet a first wave. It meets U.S.-born children translating for parents, mixed-status households, a Puerto Rican family that has never been undocumented, and a Maya household that has been in Greater Minnesota for years and still cannot get K’iche’ or Mam in the lobby. If you only know “immigrant,” you will miss them.
chapters.evidence: Labor recruitment; IRCA-era settlement; post-1990s Central American displacement; Puerto Rican internal U.S. migration; enforcement waves.
chapters.practitioner: When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. Puerto Rican is citizenship — do not run an immigration script by default.
chapters.title: Labor, IRCA, Displacement, and Enforcement — Foundational Events

chapters.body:
Family is often larger than a nuclear English form. Elders, in-laws, adult children, padrinos, and cousins who are household in practice sit in the same week.

### Who is in the household

Grandparents may be the household. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox. Ask who should be in the room.

Mixed-status is structure: a U.S.-citizen child, a parent without status, a sibling with DACA or TPS, an aunt who works the plant. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names, a grandmother as caregiver, or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason. The form’s “family” is already a design choice.

Familismo is a hypothesis, not a rule: obligation to kin can mean fierce showing-up and can mean a woman who never signs for herself. Both can be true. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family, not a crime scene walking in. Do not skip the report and call it respeto.
chapters.evidence: Extended and mixed-status households. Who cares for the child may not match the form. Do not collect status you do not need.
chapters.practitioner: Ask who should be in the room. Do not use a child as interpreter. Mixed-status is structure. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.
chapters.title: Family

chapters.body:
Latino Minnesota is metro and Greater Minnesota at the same time. Human services will meet this community on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment, in a plant town and on Lake Street.

### Places

West Side St. Paul / District del Sol is historic Mexican Minnesota, not a museum; Minneapolis corridors including Lake Street and Phillips; first-ring suburbs; Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea, dairy counties, southern and western towns. Mexican Compass: about two in five outside the Twin Cities. Guatemalan: nearly half. A Worthington household is not a Minneapolis default. Do not assume the person in front of you has been downtown.

### Partners

CLUES — Comunidades Latinas Unidas En Servicio (https://clues.org/); Centro Tyrone Guzmán; rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. Churches are often the actual safe channel. CECLC is a department door, not the whole community. An eList BCC is not a partner list.

Public calendar: Hispanic Heritage Month (September 15–October 15); Día de los Muertos as public history. A calendar click is not community engagement. Latino staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A festival visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.
chapters.evidence: West Side St. Paul / District del Sol; Lake Street; first-ring suburbs; Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea. CLUES; Centro Tyrone Guzmán; rural parish and worker centers.
chapters.practitioner: Name the local partner. Do not assume Minneapolis. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  Latino staff. A Heritage Month table does not make you the expert.
chapters.title: Minnesota and Latino History

chapters.body:
To be filed “Latino” or “Hispanic” in Minnesota is to be placed in a U.S. checkbox that holds many nations, indigenous peoples, Afro-Latino histories, and U.S.-born lives. There is no single peoplehood word that does the work Somalinimo or Hmoob does. The honesty of this page is the mash: the state invented a category; you still have to meet a household.

### In this state

Mexican Minnesota is the largest origin here. That fact becomes a harm when the building treats Mexican Spanish, Mexican parish, and Mexican food as the Latino default. A Maya household, a Puerto Rican household, an Andean household, and an Afro-Latino household are not variants of Mexico.

In the U.S. racial order, Hispanic is ethnicity, not race. People in this umbrella are racialized as white, as Black, as indigenous, as “other,” as mixed — and then treated as one client. Colorism inside the umbrella is real. Indigenous erasure under “they all speak Spanish” is real. Afro-Latino people exist — ask, do not mash them into historic African American, and do not bleach them into a mestizo story.

This brief is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to this family.
chapters.evidence: Umbrella, not a people. Mexican default in this state is a count fact and a harm when it becomes the only file. Colorism and indigenous erasure are real.
chapters.practitioner: Do not fold this household into one Latino blob. Name the origin. Open the people brief that matches this household.
chapters.title: Latino / Hispanic — an umbrella, not a people

chapters.body:
These concepts recur. They are hypotheses you still test on this family.

### Familismo

Kin as the unit of decision and care. Hypothesis: the person who talks in the lobby may not be the person who decides, and the caregiver on the form may not be the caregiver at 2 a.m. Ask who should be in the room. Not a license to ignore the adult in front of you. Not a license to skip mandated reporting.

### Respeto

Titles, elders, register (usted). Hypothesis: a first-name lobby and a joking tone can read as contempt. Follow this room. Respeto is not submission, and it is not permission for staff to accept a courtesy-yes as a plan.

### Personalismo

Relationship before a long form. Hypothesis: the first visit may be about whether you are safe, not about the exception process. That is not delay. The clock still exists for medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing the relationship.

### Confianza

Trust is built. It is not demanded on visit one. Enforcement climate, a bad interpreter, a child used as the mouth, an SSN field that feels like a trap — these spend confianza before you have it.

Variation is the point. A U.S.-born professional, a Maya plant worker, a Puerto Rican household, and an evangelical grandmother do not share a Tuesday. You work with these hypotheses. You do not perform them. You do not write “noncompliant” when you mean “the form was a stranger.” Staff do not use familismo as an icebreaker or a risk score. If the family names it, you listen.
chapters.evidence: Familismo, respeto, personalismo, confianza as hypotheses. Two surnames. Spanish is not one Spanish. Indigenous languages in some homes.
chapters.practitioner: You work with these hypotheses. You do not perform them. Relationship before a long form. Not permission to skip mandated reporting.
chapters.title: Core Concepts — hypotheses, not rules

chapters.body:
Catholic majority in many streams — not all.

### Streams

The parish may be the trusted channel for information, mutual aid, baptismal records, and a room people will enter when they will not enter yours. Our Lady of Guadalupe is central in many Mexican Catholic lives. Evangelical and Pentecostal churches are large, especially in some Central American and second-generation streams. Indigenous practice lives here and is not a souvenir. Caribbean Catholic and Afro-diasporic practice exist; do not exoticize, and do not assume.

Do not make a priest, a pastor, or a curandero the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one parish and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic, or indigenous practice as witchcraft.

### Practice

Día de los Muertos is public history — ofrendas, November 1–2 — not a file and not a personality. Hispanic Heritage Month is not consultation. Holy Week, quinceañera as religious-family event, and funeral obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both. “God’s will” is not automatically non-compliance.
chapters.evidence: Catholic majority in many streams; evangelical and Pentecostal large; indigenous practice. Guadalupe in many Mexican Catholic lives. Parish may be the trusted channel.
chapters.practitioner: Do not make a priest or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Día de los Muertos is public history, not a file.
chapters.title: Religion

chapters.body:
Handshake is common in many rooms. A slight nod with an elder is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth.

### Titles

Some streams greet familiars with a cheek kiss — follow this room; do not initiate because a training slide said Latinos are tactile.

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña, sometimes Señorita. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it. Usted versus tú is respect in Spanish; a qualified interpreter matches register. You do not correct it.

### This room

Elders first. Greet the people in the room, not only the English speaker.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Cross-gender touch: follow this room. Do not make a scene in the lobby.
chapters.evidence: Handshake common. Titles — Señor, Señora, Don, Doña — until invited. Usted is respect in many Spanish rooms. Elders first.
chapters.practitioner: Do not force a first name on an elder. Do not import Somali or African American greeting rules. Follow this room.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno.

### Two surnames

José Luis García Hernández is not “José García” with leftover words. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Do not anglicize Jesús, Muñoz, Ñ as a convenience. Given names may be Spanish, indigenous, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask.

### How to file

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records; some add de plus the husband’s paternal surname; some keep both family surnames. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.
chapters.evidence: Two surnames: apellido paterno + apellido materno. U.S. databases that keep one invent a person. Given names may be Spanish, indigenous, English, or both.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
A calendar click is literacy for scheduling. It is not community engagement.

### Calendar

Hispanic Heritage Month — September 15 to October 15. Tied to independence days (Mexico September 16; several Central American republics September 15; Chile September 18). Literacy for the meeting. A poster is not language access. A Heritage Month table is not consultation.

Día de los Muertos — November 1–2. Public history in Minnesota. Guest if you are in a public ofrenda space. Not a file. Not a costume for staff.

Our Lady of Guadalupe — December 12. Major for many Mexican Catholic families. Las Posadas in some Mexican streams (mid-December). Día de los Reyes / Three Kings — January 6. Holy Week. Quinceañera is family-religious time, not a case note.

Independence days and national holidays vary by origin. Puerto Rican households may mark distinct days. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note. Ask.
chapters.evidence: Hispanic Heritage Month (Sept 15–Oct 15). Día de los Muertos (Nov 1–2). Independence days vary by origin. Guadalupe Dec 12 for many Mexican Catholic families.
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.
chapters.title: Dates of Significance

chapters.body:
U.S.-born children in English-dominant schools with parents who may not read the IEP in English — that is a gate, not a one-hour culture clash.

### School and language

Some parents do not read Spanish either. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. Oral Spanish is not print Spanish. Mixtec or K’iche’ in the home is not a Spanish IEP.

A parent who speaks fluent Spanish, or fluent Mixtec, and limited English is not illiterate. The form that only exists in English is. Do not use a child as interpreter. That is a closed door and a harm: it reverses respeto, it leaks adult business, and it is not CLAS.

Do not invent a dropout rate on this page. Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus poverty plus enforcement fear plus a school that never learned the second surname.

Puerto Rican, Mexican-American, and other U.S.-citizen students are not “immigrant students” by default. Do not collect status you do not need at enrollment theater.
chapters.evidence: U.S.-born children in English-dominant schools; parents who may not read the IEP. Mixtec or K’iche’ is not a Spanish IEP. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed.
chapters.practitioner: A parent who speaks fluent Spanish or Mixtec and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only form is the gate. Do not use a child as interpreter.
chapters.title: Education

chapters.body:
Hospitality: food, drink, time. Accepting a little is courtesy. Refusing everything can read as cold. You still keep medical and legal clocks.

### In the home

Titles and elders. Shoes: follow the household. Do not walk into a living room and photograph an ofrenda or a Guadalupe altar. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain “your culture” as entertainment.

### Time

Punctuality: social time can run long. Work, clinic, and court time should be treated as on time. Do not write a “Latino time” joke in a case note.

Relationship may precede a signature. That is personalismo as hypothesis — not permission to skip a notice. Confirm in the language they use. Ask whether they agree with the plan. Do not take a smile as consent.
chapters.evidence: Hospitality. Titles. Elders. Do not photograph an ofrenda or a Guadalupe altar.
chapters.practitioner: Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Do not use a child as the go-between. Do not take a smile as consent.
chapters.title: Etiquette

chapters.body:
This is the CLAS Spanish line — and Spanish is not the people.

### Spanish

Mexican Spanish, Central American Spanish, Caribbean Spanish, and Andean Spanish are not one interpreter accent test. Book a qualified Spanish interpreter AND ask this household. A Mexican interpreter from one region can still be a closed door for a Salvadoran elder, a Puerto Rican parent, or a rural Guatemalan speaker. Register matters: usted, not a buddy tú, until the room says otherwise.

### Indigenous languages

Mixtec and Zapotec in some Mexican homes. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ and other Mayan languages in some Guatemalan homes — nearly half of Guatemalan Minnesota is Greater Minnesota. Garifuna in some Honduran and Caribbean-coast households. Ecuadorian indigenous languages may be in the home. A Spanish interpreter for those households is still a closed door. Name the language on the request. A scarce interpreter is a gate, not an excuse to proceed in English only without recording the gap.

Portuguese is adjacent — Brazilian Minnesota is not this page. Do not file a Brazilian household under Latino-Spanish and call it done. Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not make a Latino coworker the interpreter. Compass (Mexican, ACS 2019–2023): among those 5 and older, 58.3 percent speak a language other than English; 23.7 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Do not invent a rate for the whole umbrella.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion, hierarchy, or the interpreter. Direct disagreement with a professional may be muted — and then the plan is not followed. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent. Do not write “noncompliant” when you mean “did not understand the English exception form.” Literacy in any language is not guaranteed: oral skill is not print.
chapters.evidence: Spanish varieties; Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna. Mexican Compass: 58.3% language other than English (5+); 23.7% LEP. Do not invent an umbrella rate.
chapters.practitioner: Book qualified Spanish AND ask. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Confirm the indigenous language. Do not use a child as interpreter. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  Latino staff.
chapters.title: Language and Communication — the CLAS gate

chapters.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

### Enforcement

ICE and enforcement climate is structure. Mixed-status households skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate. Puerto Rican is citizenship — do not run an immigration script by default.

### Named harms

Indigenous erasure under “they all speak Spanish” is a named harm. Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Colorism is real inside the umbrella. Intra-Latino hierarchy is real: Mexican default in this state will talk over a Maya or Caribbean household if you let it.

Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Who speaks in the meeting, who holds the papers, who is allowed to leave the house — ask, and follow law. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family.

LGBTQ Latinos exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it familismo. Hispanic Heritage Month is not consultation.
chapters.evidence: ICE/enforcement climate; mixed status; indigenous erasure; colorism; machismo as named harm; LGBTQ people exist; Puerto Rican is citizenship.
chapters.practitioner: Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Do not collect status you do not need.
chapters.title: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice

chapters.body:
Uninsured and delayed-care patterns sit in this umbrella. Date Minnesota figures when you have them. Do not invent a rate on this page.

### Access

Compass Mexican poverty (ACS 2019–2023) is 12.8 percent — a poverty figure, not an uninsured rate, not the whole umbrella. Pattern now: people delay, people use the emergency room as the door, people skip follow-up when the lobby feels like enforcement.

Fear of the lobby is a health access fact. A badge, a form that asks for SSN, a child called to interpret a diagnosis, an interpreter who does not speak this Spanish or this indigenous language — these are clinical events. When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic. That is not noncompliance.

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening because a stereotype said this community is dramatic, or stoic, or “they take care of their own.” Do not fold this history into Tuskegee (African American literacy) or into a generic “immigrant mistrust” slide. This community’s medical mistrust also runs through camps and war in some streams, dismissals, and child-protection fear.

Traditional healers, yerberías, and parish prayer can sit next to a fierce wish for biomedicine. If they name a healer, listen. Do not make the healer the case plan unless they asked. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Do not use a child as interpreter in a health encounter.
chapters.evidence: Uninsured and delayed-care patterns — date MN figures when you have them. Fear of the lobby is a health access fact. Compass Mexican poverty 12.8% is not an uninsured rate.
chapters.practitioner: Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. Gender match if they want it. Do not use a child as interpreter.
chapters.title: Health

chapters.body:
Queer and trans Latino Minnesotans exist. Conservative parish, evangelical, and family climates can mean silence, exile, or danger. That is not every family.

### This person

Familismo can be protection and can be pressure. You do not get to decide which one this household is from the doorway.

Staff duty: use the name they use. Do not out them to an elder, a parish, or a “supportive family” you invented as cultural humility. Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a family-values exhibit.

Afro-Latino and indigenous queer people exist inside this page. Do not mash them into the historic African American LGBTQ chapter, and do not bleach them. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.
chapters.evidence: Queer and trans Latino Minnesotans exist. Conservative parish and family climates can mean silence. Afro-Latino and indigenous queer people exist.
chapters.practitioner: Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture. Familismo is not a license to call kin.
chapters.title: LGBTQ

chapters.body:
There is no Latino uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota.

### Dress

Indigenous traje and Maya dress are public at fiesta and ceremony, not a daily costume, and not yours to request for a Heritage Month photo. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

Colorism and hair texture are real inside the umbrella. Afro-Latino hair is not the CROWN Act chapter copied over — and you still do not touch, still do not police, still do not treat tightness or looseness as a professionalism problem. Mestizo default beauty is a hierarchy. Name it if it is in the room. Do not rank.

Quinceañera dress, baptism white, funeral black, evangelical modesty, Catholic veil in some rooms — celebration and devotion, not a case note. Do not touch. Do not rank piety or indigeneity off clothing. Ask the person, with gender match if they want it.
chapters.evidence: No Latino uniform. Indigenous traje is public at fiesta, not a daily costume. Colorism and hair texture are real. Second generation looks like Minnesota.
chapters.practitioner: Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch. Do not rank.
chapters.title: Hair, Dress, and Body

chapters.body:
Not one playlist. Mariachi, ranchera, norteño, banda, cumbia, salsa, merengue, bachata, vallenato, música andina, marimba, corridos, reggaeton, church music — origin names the sound.

### Variation

A Mexican default playlist in a Guatemalan or Puerto Rican waiting room is the mash in speakers.

Corridos include narcocorridos in some streams. That is a named fact, not a joke and not a risk score you write on a last name.

A festival stage is not engagement. A playlist is not language access. Church music is not staff entertainment. Knowing that music is public life will not write the waiver. It will stop you from treating one Heritage Month speaker as the community.
chapters.evidence: Not one playlist. Mariachi, ranchera, norteño, cumbia, salsa, merengue, bachata, andina, marimba, corridos, church music — origin names the sound.
chapters.practitioner: A Mexican default playlist in a Guatemalan or Puerto Rican waiting room is the mash. A playlist is not engagement.
chapters.title: Music

chapters.body:
Fútbol is the default public sport for many boys and men, and for many girls. Boxing has prestige in some streams. Baseball and softball show up especially in Caribbean households. School sport is ordinary for the second generation.

### Not the whole person

Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

Leagues and pickup games are social infrastructure in metro and in plant towns. They are not a substitute for language access on a waiver. They are not consultation.

World Cup and club fútbol are public life. A viewing party is not community engagement. Sport clubs are not the interpreter pool.
chapters.evidence: Fútbol is common public sport. Boxing in some streams. Baseball especially in Caribbean households. School sport in the second generation.
chapters.practitioner: Do not assume the kid plays. Sport clubs are not language access.
chapters.title: Sports

chapters.body:
Spanish-language literature is world literature. That fact does not mean the person in the lobby can read your form — in English or in Spanish.

### Literacy in the lobby

Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. Indigenous oral literature — Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, and others — is older than the Spanish file and is not “no letters.”

Minnesota has Latino journalists, poets, and scholars. You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby. You do need to know this is not a people without letters, and not a people who can all read the exception process.

Print Spanish from Spain, Mexico, or a machine translation is not automatically this household’s Spanish. CLAS is qualified language, not Google and not a child.
chapters.evidence: Spanish-language literature is world literature. Indigenous oral literature is older. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed.
chapters.practitioner: You do not need to quote a novel. You need the language this person reads — or hears. CLAS is not Google and not a child.
chapters.title: Literature

chapters.body:
Murals on the West Side and on Lake Street are public Minnesota art, not a booth. Ofrendas at Día de los Muertos are public history. Textiles and indigenous weaving are art and memory, not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. Do not photograph an altar because it is pretty. An ofrenda is not a case plan. A mural tour is not consultation.

Contemporary Latino and indigenous artists work in this state. Knowing that will not write the waiver. It will stop you from treating the umbrella as a people without a public culture — and from treating that public culture as engagement.

There is no single Civil Rights Movement to copy onto this page. The political literacy here is stacked.

### The badge

U.S. labor recruitment; IRCA 1986 and settlement; Mexican and Central American displacement; Salvadoran civil war and TPS; Guatemalan war and Maya flight; Nicaraguan streams; Cuban and Venezuelan political flight (date those if you cite); Puerto Rican colonial status and citizenship without treating that household as foreign; and U.S. enforcement that reorganizes Tuesday.

When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. A DHS badge is not automatically help. That is not paranoia. It is pattern. Do not tell people the climate is fine so the form is fair now. Do not use a civil war or a raid as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate crossing for your professional development.

Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate. Notices to a household that will not open the door are a closed gate with a polite label. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a deportation score.

Food processing, dairy, agriculture, construction, service, restaurants, cleaning, childcare, home care, professional second generation, public employment.

### Work

Rural plants and metro kitchens can sit in the same extended family. A small-business owner and a waiver recipient may be the same household.

Worker centers and parishes may be the trusted channel in Greater Minnesota. Name the local one. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume CLUES reaches a dairy county. Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice.

### Staff

Latino staff exist inside DHS and counties. They are not unpaid interpreters, not the indigenous-language pool, and not “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan. Do not make a Latino colleague your unpaid tutor.

Remittance to kin in another country is obligation for many, not a disposable luxury. A budget that treats it as optional has already chosen a household type. Puerto Rican households may be sending money to the island after disaster — still not an immigration script.

Language including indigenous. Book qualified Spanish AND ask.

### Language

Confirm Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna when that is the home language. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

Who is in the room. Gender match in maternal and intimate care if they want it. Titles. Two surnames. SSN on the first screen: if you do not need it, do not demand it as theater. Mixed-status: do not collect status you do not need. Enforcement climate: skipped appointments are pattern.

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. If they name a healer or a parish, listen. Do not make either the case plan unless they asked. Mandated reporting still exists. Help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. You follow the law. You still see a family.

Rural access is a gate: distance, clinic hours, one interpreter contracted from the Cities who does not speak this language. Open the rural brief beside this page. A nuclear form that cannot see grandparents as the household is already a who.

### Adjacent doors

Not “Spanish” as indigenous. Mixtec, Zapotec, K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Garifuna are not dialects of Spanish. A Spanish interpreter is not those languages.

Puerto Rican is U.S. citizenship. Do not run an immigration script by default. Cuban, Dominican, Ecuadorian, Colombian, Salvadoran, Guatemalan, Honduran, Nicaraguan, Venezuelan, Mexican — name the origin. The Mexican default is a Minnesota fact and a Minnesota harm when it becomes the only file.

Not Somali. Not historic African American. Afro-Latino people exist — ask, do not mash them into the African American brief because both are Black, and do not bleach them into a mestizo Latino blob. Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Mexican cultural community.

### Counts

229,576; Twin Cities 61.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 38.9 percent; foreign-born 26.7 percent; language other than English (age 5+) 58.3 percent; English less than “very well” 23.7 percent; poverty 12.8 percent; median household income about $66,000. Mixtec, Zapotec may be in the home — Compass notes the language possibility; it is not a count of speakers. Do not invent that count.

Same Compass vintage, other origin profiles: Colombian 9,431; Cuban 9,406; Ecuadorian 18,271 (indigenous languages may be in the home); Guatemalan 17,172 (nearly half Greater Minnesota — K’iche’, Mam, other Mayan); Puerto Rican 21,802 (U.S. citizens); Salvadoran 17,571 (civil war and TPS history). Venezuelan, Honduran, Nicaraguan, Dominican and others live here — pattern now, date if you cite. Do not invent those counts on this page.

### What the count is not

Do not add these profiles into a fake “Latino Minnesota” total. Definitions overlap; people can appear in more than one story; the umbrella is not a people. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and across Hispanic-origin versus ancestry versus language. Date the number you cite.

A rate is not the person. Poverty 12.8 percent (Mexican, that vintage) is not the Guatemalan household in a plant town and not the Puerto Rican household in the Cities. Uninsured and delayed-care patterns: date MN figures when you have them. Do not invent a rate.

sections.heading: Begin here
paragraphs: Seven Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) nations and four Dakota nations are governments. Urban Native people live in this state too. This brief is a starting point for working with nations and families — consultation is government-to-government. Alaska Native households have their own brief. Start with this family and this nation.
The eleven Tribal Nations are governments. This page is a sovereignty door, not a culture sticker you apply to a family.
Not a community profile. Not “Native culture.” Not sweat lodge as a personality. Tribal Nations are governments. This page is not a hypothesis you apply to a family in place of consultation.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
paragraphs: 11 federally recognized nations in Minnesota. Seven Anishinaabe, four Dakota. Compass Native American ~162,216 is not this page. Urban Native is not off the list. Alaska Native is a different CI.
If the packet touches Native children, services, data, or land, consultation is G2G before the eList. OIP is a door. You do not apply a culture card in place of consultation.

This brief is about the eleven federally recognized Tribal Nations in Minnesota — seven Anishinaabe (Ojibwe) nations and four Dakota nations. They are governments. Consultation is government-to-government. A culture card is not that door. A land acknowledgment without a call is not that door.

### Who this is

The eleven nations, as named by the Minnesota Indian Affairs Council:

Anishinaabe reservations: Grand Portage (northeast corner); Bois Forte (extreme north); Red Lake (extreme north, west of Bois Forte); White Earth (northwest); Leech Lake (north central); Fond du Lac (northeast, west of Duluth); Mille Lacs (central, south and east of Brainerd).

Dakota communities: Shakopee Mdewakanton (south of the Twin Cities near Prior Lake); Prairie Island (near Red Wing); Lower Sioux (near Redwood Falls); Upper Sioux (near Granite Falls).

Ojibwe and Dakota are distinct languages, territories, legal histories, and governments. The Minnesota Chippewa Tribe is a government of six Anishinaabe reservations — Bois Forte, Fond du Lac, Grand Portage, Leech Lake, Mille Lacs, and White Earth. Red Lake is not in that union. Dakota nations are not in it. Filing all eleven as “Chippewa” closes the meeting before it starts.

Minnesota Compass’s Native American profile (ACS 2019–2023) counts about 162,216 people — Twin Cities 44.8 percent, Greater Minnesota 55.2 percent. Compass cannot split that count by nation. The number is not enrollment. It is not the eleven. It is not permission to skip the Office of Indian Policy. Date it if you cite it. It is not government-to-government.

Urban Native Minneapolis–St. Paul is part of this brief. People who live off-reservation for work, school, or kinship remain citizens of nations.

A community portrait here is not one socioeconomic slice. Native Minnesotans are attorneys, physicians, scientists, teachers, nurses, people who work for tribally run health and social programs, urban Indian-health clinicians, artists, language teachers, plant and casino workers, students, and elders. The same is true inside each nation. A casino does not make a people. Poverty on a Compass line does not make a people.

### Who this is not

Alaska Native people have their own brief. Other U.S. tribal citizens living in Minnesota are not automatically one of the eleven. Mendota Mdewakanton and other communities seeking recognition are not a twelfth nation on this page.

This is not a mash of “communities of color.” Rondo is African American history. Cedar-Riverside is Somali history. Phillips, Little Earth, and the eleven governments are this page.

### How to read this

Read it as an orientation. Name the nation. Always defer to this family. Always defer to the nation on who belongs to it.

The facts that follow are meant to help you meet people well — how kinship is held, what respect looks like, what a greeting carries, what a form may land on. History is here so the meeting is clearer, not so you deliver a lecture. Population size is not culture size. Eleven governments are not a small-count brochure.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
paragraphs: Anishinaabe and Dakota peoples — distinct languages, territories, histories. Older than the state. Older than the department.
History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not mash Ojibwe and Dakota as flavor.

Dakota and Anishinaabe peoples are older than Minnesota and older than this department. This land is Dakota homeland in creation stories. It is also a central place in Anishinaabe history — the westward movement along the Great Lakes, wild rice, and the northern forests.

### Anishinaabe

Anishinaabe (also written Ojibwe, Ojibwa, Chippewa in U.S. legal English) is a people across the Great Lakes — Minnesota, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ontario, and beyond. Ojibwemowin is the language. Bands in this state are nations.

### Dakota

Dakota (Dakhóta) is a people of this prairie and river country, related to Lakota and Nakota — not the same as “Sioux” borrowed from a nineteenth-century statute. Dakota language and Dakota nations in Minnesota survived exile. That sentence is literacy.

### What people brought

Nationhood, language, kinship, land relationship, ceremony, wild rice and water as more than commodities, and a record of dealing with the United States as governments. What they met: a territory and then a state that took children, land, and language, and then wrote English forms.

History is literacy for the meeting. It is not a speech you give the family. You do not narrate 1862 to a Dakota parent as icebreaker. You do know it. Ojibwe and Dakota are not flavors of one story.

sections.heading: Geography
paragraphs: Bois Forte, Fond du Lac, Grand Portage, Leech Lake, Mille Lacs, Red Lake, White Earth. Lower Sioux, Prairie Island, Shakopee Mdewakanton, Upper Sioux. Urban Minneapolis–St. Paul. Off-reservation.
Name the nation. Urban is not ‘off the list.’ Do not assume a reservation address.

Name the nation. Geography here is government, not scenery.

### Anishinaabe nations

Bois Forte Band of Chippewa (Zagaakwaandagowiniwag) — extreme northern Minnesota; Nett Lake and Vermilion.

Fond du Lac Band of Lake Superior Chippewa (Nagaajiwanaang) — west of Duluth; Cloquet. Urban Duluth households remain the nation.

Grand Portage Band of Lake Superior Chippewa (Gichi-Onigaming) — northeast corner, Lake Superior, a border.

Leech Lake Band of Ojibwe — north central; Cass Lake.

Mille Lacs Band of Ojibwe — central, south and east of Brainerd; Districts I–III as the nation names them.

Red Lake Nation — extreme north, west of Bois Forte; not in the Minnesota Chippewa Tribe union; a distinct land and legal history.

White Earth Nation — northwest; allotment and land restoration are living politics, not a museum.

### Dakota nations

Lower Sioux Indian Community (Cansa’yapi) — near Redwood Falls.

Prairie Island Indian Community — near Red Wing, next to a nuclear generating plant.

Shakopee Mdewakanton Sioux Community — south of the Twin Cities near Prior Lake. Economic position is real and is not the Dakota story copied onto the others.

Upper Sioux Community (Pezihutazizi Oyate) — near Granite Falls.

### Cities and off-reservation life

Urban Native Minneapolis–St. Paul — Phillips, Little Earth, and the metro as a whole. Off-reservation towns near each nation. People who live in Duluth, Bemidji, Cloquet, Onamia, Prior Lake, Redwood Falls, Granite Falls, Red Wing, and ordinary suburbs.

A reservation address is not the only address. Minneapolis is not the only address. Compass Native American: 55.2 percent Greater Minnesota, 44.8 percent Twin Cities (ACS 2019–2023). That split is the opposite of Hmong Minnesota (about 94 percent Twin Cities). Distance, broadband, and county lines are how the work actually runs. Nationhood is not a ZIP code.

A physician enrolled at White Earth who works in Minneapolis is still of that nation. A scientist at a tribal natural-resources office and a student at a tribal college are the same peoplehood as a household using a waiver. Community portrait means all of that.

sections.heading: Migration and Foundational Events
paragraphs: Treaties, broken treaties, removal, 1862, boarding schools, termination and restoration. People move for work, school, and kinship and remain citizens of nations.
Boarding school and removal are why mistrust is rational. Do not call that history ‘in the past.’

Treaties. Broken treaties. Removal. The U.S.–Dakota War of 1862. The largest mass execution in U.S. history at Mankato on 26 December 1862. Internment at Fort Snelling. Exile of Dakota people from Minnesota. Allotment and the Nelson Act of 1889. Boarding schools. Termination-era policy and restoration. The Indian Child Welfare Act of 1978. The Minnesota Indian Family Preservation Act. Haaland v. Brackeen (2023) did not repeal ICWA.

### 1862 and the boarding-school system

If the Great Migration is the foundational demographic event of modern Black America, 1862 and the boarding-school system are foundational events you cannot skip for Dakota and Anishinaabe Minnesota. They are not “in the past.” They are why a county petition can still sound like removal.

### Ordinary movement

People also move for ordinary reasons — work, school, love, health — and remain of their nations. Urban Native Minneapolis is not a leftover. AIM’s founding in Minneapolis in 1968 is Minnesota history.

Boarding school and removal are why mistrust is rational. That is structure. A powwow is public and also nation. It is not the Tuesday on which a county files a petition.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Kinship systems; ICWA/MIFPA placement preferences; othermothers and extended care.
Active efforts. Kin search is not flavor. A nuclear form is already a removal machine if it cannot see kin.

Kinship systems. Othermothers. Extended care. Who cares for the child may not match a nuclear English form.

### Who is family

Aunties, grandparents, clan and tiyospaye relationships, and people who are family without a blood-quantum worksheet — all of that is family. A form that only fits two legal parents in one household cannot see kin.

Ask who should be in the room. A scientist parent, a lawyer aunt, a grandmother who harvests rice, and someone who works for a tribally run program can be the same family. “Broken family” is what the English form says when the household is not nuclear.

### ICWA and MIFPA

The Indian Child Welfare Act and the Minnesota Indian Family Preservation Act exist because the state has a record of taking children. Placement preferences, inquiry (“is this child an Indian child?”), notice to the nation, and active efforts are law. Active efforts are documented work with the family’s people, culture, and values — not a box after a removal. Kin search is not optional courtesy.

### Who belongs

You do not decide who is Native. The nation does. Blood quantum is colonial technology. Enrollment versus community belonging is nation business. A lobby quiz is not inquiry.

sections.heading: Minnesota
paragraphs: Minnesota Indian Affairs Council; DHS Office of Indian Policy; Tribal-State Relations Training for many roles.
Take TSRT. Do not substitute a land acknowledgment. Nations are seats, not BCCs.

The Minnesota Indian Affairs Council exists to protect the sovereignty of the eleven and the well-being of American Indian citizens throughout the state — including urban. The DHS Office of Indian Policy is a door inside this department. Tribal-State Relations Training is required for many roles. Take it. A land acknowledgment is not a substitute.

### Governments, not a mailing list

Nations are seats, not a copy line. Notice to nations on the same day as an eList is not consultation. Empty follow-up cells on a tribal notice are a structural failure.

Minnesota-specific institutions — partners, not a list you copy once: each nation’s government; urban Indian organizations including Native American Community Clinic, Division of Indian Work, Ain Dah Yung, American Indian Family Center, MIGIZI; Little Earth; tribal colleges and language tables; urban Indian health. Pay. Report back. You are a guest.

### Staff

Staff of this department include citizens of these nations. They are not unpaid liaisons, unpaid interpreters, or “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan.

Rondo is African American literacy. Cedar-Riverside is Somali literacy. Phillips, Little Earth, and the eleven governments are this page.

sections.heading: Heart of the People
paragraphs: Sovereignty; land; kinship; language; holistic health — physical, mental, emotional, spiritual.
Nationhood is the first fact. Culture is not yours to display.

Sovereignty. Land. Kinship. Language. Holistic health — physical, mental, emotional, spiritual as one. Nationhood is the first fact. Culture is not yours to display.

### Peoplehood older than the United States

Du Bois’s double consciousness is African American intelligence. It is not a universal minority sentence to copy here. Dakota and Anishinaabe peoplehood is older than the United States. The tension here is not “how to be both Native and American without bleaching.” It is that the United States and this state made treaties, broke them, took children, and still write English forms. You work that fact. You do not perform it.

### Not a culture club

Eleven governments. Not a club. A Heritage Month frybread lunch is not the heart of anything.

Language revitalization is nationhood. Manoomin (wild rice) is food and law and season. Wacipi / powwow is public and also nation. Ceremony is not a training module. You are a guest even when the meeting is in a county building.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
paragraphs: Sovereignty; treaty; kinship; language revitalization; ceremony as nationhood not a module.
You work with these. You do not perform them. You do not decide who is Native. The nation does.

These concepts recur. They express differently by nation, family, and generation. They are hypotheses — not a script for the person in front of you.

### Sovereignty

Governments, not clubs. Treaties are living legal facts. A nation is not a stakeholder list.

### Treaty

The United States and Minnesota still sit on treaty ground. All seven Anishinaabe reservations in Minnesota were originally established by treaty and are considered separate and distinct nations by the United States government (Minnesota Indian Affairs Council). Dakota communities in this state are nations that survived exile.

### Kinship

Who is family may not fit the form. ICWA and MIFPA placement is the legal expression of that fact in child welfare.

### Language

Ojibwemowin and Dakota language revitalization. English is common. A word you learned in a training is not expertise. Language nests and tribal schools are nationhood, not an interpreter convenience.

### Land and water

Not a backdrop. Hunting, fishing, ricing, and treaty rights are law, not hobbies.

### Ceremony

Nationhood. The American Indian Religious Freedom Act. Not a team-building event. Not a lodge you book as department programming.

### Seven Grandfather Teachings

Wisdom, love, respect, bravery, honesty, humility, truth — these are Anishinaabe. They do not paste onto a Dakota household as a values poster. Dakota ethics and kinship have their own names. Ask.

### Blood quantum

Colonial technology. Enrollment is nation business.

### Two-spirit

Native LGBTQ people exist. Named variation. Not a side note and not a branding exercise.

### Urban Native

Not off the list.

A land acknowledgment is not consultation.

sections.heading: Religion and Healing
paragraphs: Traditional practice and Christianity both live here. AIRFA. Ceremony is not a team-building event.
If they name traditional healing, follow their lead and the nation’s. Do not book a lodge as DHS programming.

Traditional practice and Christianity both live here — often in the same family.

### Missions and ceremony

Catholic missions, Episcopal missions, boarding-school Christianity, and traditional ceremony are all Minnesota facts. The American Indian Religious Freedom Act (1978) is law. Ceremony is not a team-building event. Hmong txiv neeb is not a sweat lodge. Dakota lodge is not Anishinaabe lodge by default.

If they name traditional healing, follow their lead and the nation’s. A pastor, a priest, or a healer is the case plan when this family asked. Do not book a lodge as department programming. Do not photograph ceremony.

### Boarding-school harm

Spiritual harm from boarding schools is structure: language forbidden, ceremony punished, children taken. That harm sits in the same clinic as ordinary chronic disease. You can hold both. You do not interrogate a ceremony to complete a field.

A white convert to a lodge is not a citizen of a nation. A Dakota person who is Catholic is still Dakota. Mixing those facts is how the meeting goes wrong.

sections.heading: Greetings
paragraphs: Named variation by nation and family. Handshake is common in many rooms. Do not invent a protocol.
Follow this room. Do not force a hand. Do not use a word you learned as an icebreaker.

Follow this room. Handshake is common in many rooms. A protocol invented from a training slide is not a greeting. Do not force a hand. A word you learned is not an icebreaker.

### Elders and titles

Elders first. Listen longer than the form wants. Titles if they use them. Ask how to say a name.

You are a guest in nation space even when the meeting is in a county building. The Black nod is African American intelligence. As-salāmu ʿalaykum is Somali and Muslim intelligence. Importing another community’s greeting is a mash.

### Silence

Silence can be thought, not refusal. Directness is not rudeness. Filling every pause because Minnesota Nice is uncomfortable is not listening.

sections.heading: Naming
paragraphs: English names, nation names, and language names may all sit on one person. Enrollment names are nation business.
Ask how to say it. You do not decide who is Native. Do not treat a name as a blood-quantum quiz.

Ask how to say it. English names, nation names, and language names may all sit on one person. Enrollment names are nation business.

### Not a quiz

A name is not a blood-quantum quiz. Do not joke. Do not Anglicize. The form that only fits Mary Jones is a gate.

You do not decide who is Native. A scientist named in English and a language teacher named in Ojibwemowin can be siblings. Neither is more authentic as a case note.

Pronounce Bois Forte, Mille Lacs, Shakopee, Pezihutazizi. If you cannot, ask. Literacy includes the map.

sections.heading: Dates and Calendar
paragraphs: Nation events, treaty dates, 1862, boarding-school remembrance, powwow calendars some families name.
A calendar click is literacy. It is not consultation and not a day off the packet.

Treaty dates. 1862. 26 December — the Mankato executions; literacy, not a holiday you put on a flyer. Boarding-school remembrance. American Indian Month in Minnesota (May, as the state has marked it). Nation days and powwow calendars some families name. Ricing season. Hunting seasons as treaty practice.

### This family’s calendar

A calendar date is literacy. It is not consultation and not a day off the form. “Native holiday” does not belong on a case note. Ask this family and this nation.

Juneteenth is African American literacy. Eid is not this page. Another community’s calendar is not inclusion here.

sections.heading: Education
paragraphs: Boarding-school history is structure. Tribal schools, public schools, language nests. Attainment gaps — date MN when you cite.
Do not treat a degree as exceptional in a way that insults the rest. Language revitalization is nationhood.

Boarding-school history is structure in the school building too.

### Schools and colleges

Tribal schools, public schools, language nests, tribal colleges, University of Minnesota and Minnesota State students, attorneys with JDs, physicians, scientists, and teachers.

Bachelor’s or higher among Compass Native American adults 25 and older is 22.5 percent (ACS 2019–2023). High school graduate or higher 88.4 percent. Date it. A rate is not the person.

A degree is not exceptional in a way that insults the rest. Athletics is not the path. Language revitalization is not extra. English-only forms are a gate even when speech is strong.

### Teachers and scholars

Anton Treuer’s public Ojibwe-language work, tribal-college faculty, and classroom teachers in Onamia or Red Lake are the same educational story as a Ph.D. They are not a hierarchy of authenticity.

A parent who speaks Dakota or Ojibwe and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only IEP is the gate.

sections.heading: Etiquette
paragraphs: Listen longer than the form wants. Do not photograph ceremony. Hospitality is not consent to extract.
Guest. Keep medical and legal time. Do not record a lodge.

Listen. Do not photograph ceremony. Hospitality is not consent to extract. Keep medical and legal time.

### Guest

Do not record a lodge. Do not ask for a song as a closer. You are a guest. A design is not a logo for the department.

Food offered in a home is courtesy. You still keep the clock for court and clinic. Frybread is not a personality. Refusing everything as professionalism is not courtesy.

Nation offices are not a research site. Pay. Report back.

sections.heading: Communication
paragraphs: Ojibwe and Dakota language revitalization. English is common. Silence can be thought, not refusal.
Do not treat a word you learned as expertise. Book an interpreter if they ask. Directness is not rudeness.

Ojibwe and Dakota language revitalization. English is common.

### What Compass shows

Compass Native American (age 5+): 87.9 percent English only; 12.1 percent a language other than English; 3.2 percent speak English less than very well (ACS 2019–2023). Date it. Low limited-English-proficient numbers on a Compass line are not permission to skip the language an elder asks for.

Book an interpreter if they ask. A word you learned is not expertise. Do not correct English in the lobby.

### Silence and story

Silence can be thought, not refusal. Directness is not rudeness. Story and circular speech can be how an elder thinks in public. A short English yes may be exhaustion. Ask whether they agree. A smile is not consent.

sections.heading: Other Considerations
paragraphs: Blood quantum as colonial technology; enrollment vs community; two-spirit; data sovereignty.
You do not decide who is Native. The nation does. Do not out anyone. Follow law.

Blood quantum is colonial technology. Enrollment versus community is nation business. Two-spirit people exist. Data sovereignty is nation business.

### MMIW and child welfare

Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women is current structure, not a poster. The state has a record of taking children. That is why ICWA exists.

Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Mandated reporting still stands.

### Not one economy

Gaming revenue at one nation is not the Dakota story. Poverty on a Compass line is not the Anishinaabe story. Scientists, lawyers, doctors, teachers, and professionals in tribally run programs exist in the same nations as people on waivers. Community portrait means all of that. Dominant culture does not get to choose which slice is “the real Native.”

Haaland v. Brackeen (2023) upheld ICWA. That is current law. The Act is not optional because a commenter was uncomfortable.

sections.heading: Health
paragraphs: Worst health outcomes of any group in Minnesota — date the specific rate when you have the controlling source. Pattern now. IHS, tribal health, urban Indian health.
Believe reported pain. Those clinics are not interchangeable with a county clinic. Olmstead still applies. So does nationhood.

Pattern, dated: American Indian Minnesotans have among the worst health outcomes of any group in the state — date the specific rate when you have the controlling Minnesota Department of Health or tribal-epidemiology source. Do not invent a number here to sound complete.

### Compass

Compass Native American (ACS 2019–2023): 16.2 percent with a disability; 8.5 percent without health insurance; median household income about $58,000; 17.9 percent below poverty. Date it. A rate is not the person.

### Systems of care

Indian Health Service, tribal health, urban Indian health, and county clinics are not interchangeable. Olmstead and disability still apply. So does nationhood. Believe reported pain. Historical trauma and ordinary chronic disease sit in the same body. You can hold both.

A physician who is a citizen of White Earth and a patient at an urban Indian clinic are both this page. The clinic is not the whole portrait.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
paragraphs: Two-spirit and LGBTQ Native people exist. Harm in some churches and in some traditional rooms. Named variation.
Use the name and pronouns. Do not out someone to family or to a nation office as ‘culture.’

Two-spirit and LGBTQ Native people exist. Harm in some churches and in some traditional rooms. Named variation.

Use the name and pronouns. Outing someone to family or to a nation office is not culture. The people-page rule is the workplace rule.

Two-spirit is not a brand you put on a Heritage Month flyer. It is people.

sections.heading: Hair and Dress
paragraphs: Hair can be spiritual, personal, or neither. Do not touch. Do not police as unprofessional.
Do not touch. CROWN-adjacent harm still happens. Follow this person.

Hair can be spiritual, personal, or neither. Long hair, braids, a ribbon skirt, a jingle dress, a suit in a St. Paul hearing room — all of that is this people. Do not touch. Locs, braids, or long hair are not unprofessional.

CROWN-adjacent harm still happens. Follow this person. A ribbon skirt is not a costume you request.

A lawyer in a ribbon skirt and a scientist in a lab coat are not opposites. They may be the same person on different Tuesdays.

sections.heading: Music
paragraphs: Drum, song, powwow as public and as nation, church music, contemporary Minnesota work.
A playlist is not engagement. Guest. Not a content harvest.

Drum, song, powwow as public and as nation, church music, contemporary Minnesota work. A playlist is not engagement. You are a guest.

A colleague is not a soundtrack of their nation. Powwow is not the only music.

sections.heading: Sports
paragraphs: School sport, nation sport, hockey, basketball, softball. Not a personality.
Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

School sport, nation sport, hockey, basketball, softball. Over-representation in a sport is not a personality. The kid may not play. Sport is not the only excellence you can see.

A physician, a software engineer, a language teacher, and a varsity hockey player can be in the same family. The group is not the person.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: Oral literature; contemporary Native writers in this region; language texts. This is not a people without letters.
You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby. You do need to know the record exists.

Oral literature first. Contemporary Native writers in this region. Language texts. This is not a people without letters.

### Named writers

Louise Erdrich (Turtle Mountain Band of Chippewa, Minneapolis) is world literature and Minnesota literary life — not one of the eleven, not a mash, a reminder that Native letters are not a museum. Anton Treuer’s Ojibwe-language work is Minnesota public scholarship. Nation newspapers, language curricula, and testimony at the legislature are literature of government.

You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby. You do need to know the record exists. Population size is not culture size.

sections.heading: Art
paragraphs: Beadwork, quill, contemporary studio, wild rice as food and as nation, public art.
Guest. Pay. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  a design as a logo.

Beadwork, quill, contemporary studio, wild rice as food and as nation, public art. You are a guest. Pay. A design is not a logo for the department.

A festival is not consultation. An artist who sells work and a chemist at a tribal environmental office are both this portrait.

sections.heading: Civil Rights Memory
paragraphs: Treaties; 1862; boarding schools; termination and restoration; ICWA; 2020 and after. Not ‘in the past.’
A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not tell people the movement succeeded so the packet is fair now.

Treaties. 1862. Boarding schools. Allotment. Termination and restoration. AIM in Minneapolis, 1968. ICWA 1978. The Minnesota Indian Family Preservation Act. Haaland v. Brackeen 2023. Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women. Not “in the past.”

### The record

A DHS badge is not automatically help. The movement did not succeed so that the form is fair now. Empty follow-up cells on a tribal notice are a structural failure.

There is no U.S. Civil Rights Movement to copy onto this page as a template. The political literacy here is nation-to-nation, child welfare, land, language, and a state that still has to be made to keep its word.

sections.heading: Business and Work
paragraphs: 638; gaming as nation revenue not a mascot; tribal employment; urban professionals; trades.
A Heritage Month frybread lunch is not consultation. Native staff are not unpaid liaisons.

Self-determination contracting (Public Law 93-638). Gaming as nation revenue, not a mascot. Tribal employment. Urban professionals. Trades. Teachers. Health clinicians. Scientists in tribal natural-resources departments. Attorneys in tribal courts and in this department. Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Nation economies

A Heritage Month frybread lunch is not consultation. Notice goes to the nation as a government.

Shakopee Mdewakanton’s economic position is real and is not the Dakota story copied onto Upper Sioux or Lower Sioux. White Earth and Red Lake are not one economy. Name the nation. “Casino Indian” is not a type.

Native staff are not unpaid liaisons. Pay the work or do not ask for it.

sections.heading: Healthcare Encounters
paragraphs: Mistrust is historical and current. IHS / tribal / urban Indian / county are not one door.
Ask where they get care. Believe pain. Family and ceremony if they want them. Refer with competence.

Ask where they get care. Indian Health Service, tribal health, urban Indian health, and county clinics are not one door. Believe pain. Family and ceremony if they want them.

Refer with competence. Mandated reporting still exists. Staff are not unpaid cultural experts.

### Trust

Mistrust is historical and current. Help-seeking that becomes a child-welfare petition is a pattern families already know. Tuskegee is African American medical history — not this page. Do name this pattern: a county file that sounds like removal.

Gender match if they want it. Do not force a handshake. Inquiry under ICWA and MIFPA is not optional curiosity.

sections.heading: Diaspora and Adjacent
paragraphs: Alaska Native, other U.S. tribal citizens living in MN, First Nations from Canada — not the 11.
Open the Alaska Native CI for Alaska Native. Do not file them under the 11. Urban Native is not a leftover.

Alaska Native is a different brief. Other U.S. tribal citizens living in Minnesota are not automatically one of the eleven. First Nations from Canada are not the eleven. Urban Native is not a leftover.

### Not one Native module

Never one Native module. “Indigenous” is not a mash with Māori training slides. Open the Alaska Native brief for Alaska Native people. Open this for the eleven and for urban Native Minnesota that still belongs to a nation.

Historic African American, Somali, and Hmong are different cultural intelligences. Shared “people of color” language in a training is not shared nationhood.

sections.heading: Statistics
paragraphs: Compass Native American ~162,216 (ACS 2019–2023) is not enrollment and not G2G. Date any health or child-welfare rate. Counts disagree.
A rate is not the person. Disproportionality in child welfare is a gate, not a vibe.

Compass Native American (ACS 2019–2023), dated: about 162,216; Twin Cities 44.8 percent, Greater Minnesota 55.2 percent; 40.1 percent age 17 or younger; 7.0 percent 65+; 3.8 percent foreign-born.

### Language, education, income

Language (age 5+): 87.9 percent English only, 12.1 percent another language, 3.2 percent English less than very well. Education (25+): 88.4 percent high school or higher, 22.5 percent bachelor’s or higher. Median household income about $58,000; 17.9 percent below poverty; 54.4 percent owner-occupied; average household size 2.54; disability 16.2 percent; without health insurance 8.5 percent.

### What the count is not

Compass cannot disaggregate by tribe. Counts disagree with enrollment, with “American Indian alone,” and with “alone or in combination.” Date the number you cite. A rate is not the person.

Child-welfare disproportionality is a gate. Health outcomes — date the controlling Minnesota Department of Health or tribal-epidemiology source. Do not invent a statewide “worst” percentage if you cannot date it.

Population size is not culture size. 162,216 is not permission to write a brochure.

sections.heading: Resources
paragraphs: OIP; MIAC; each nation’s government; urban Indian organizations; TSRT; ICWA/MIFPA. CECLC is not a substitute for G2G.
Learn on your own time. Take TSRT. Do not make a Native colleague your unpaid tutor.

Each nation’s government. Minnesota Indian Affairs Council. DHS Office of Indian Policy. Tribal-State Relations Training. ICWA and MIFPA. Haaland v. Brackeen (2023). Urban Indian organizations named on this page. Compass Native American profile — administrative, not government-to-government. A community leadership council is not a substitute for government-to-government.

### Learn on your own time

Take Tribal-State Relations Training. A Native colleague is not an unpaid tutor. Pay partners. Report back.

The Office of Equal Opportunity and Access is a discrimination door, not this page. The African American brief is not this page. Alaska Native is not this page.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
paragraphs: ICWA/MIFPA; data sovereignty; Medicaid and tribal health; notice to nations on the same day as an eList is not consultation; English forms; child-welfare disproportionality.
G2G before the eList. Active efforts. Kin search. OIP. Take TSRT. Write a disposition on the packet. You are not a tribal liaison because you read this.

Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Child welfare: ICWA and MIFPA. Active efforts are documented work with the family’s people, culture, and values — not a box after a removal. Kin search is not flavor. If you work that system, the nation is a government, not a culture consult.

Health and disability: IHS, tribal health, urban Indian health, county. They are not interchangeable. Believe reported pain. Olmstead still applies. Ceremony is not DHS programming.

Notices and comment: notice to nations on the same day as an eList is not consultation. Empty follow-up cells are a structural failure. Pay. Report back.

If you skip consultation because you “understand Native culture now,” this failed and it may be unlawful.

sections.heading: Why this can be missed
paragraphs: A Heritage Month frybread lunch, a land acknowledgment, and an eList “tribal notice” on the same day as everyone else. Treating Nations as a culture club misses the point. They are governments. The worst health outcomes in the state are not a misunderstanding. They are the afterlife of treaties, removal, and boarding schools.

sections.heading: Eleven nations
paragraphs: Seven Anishinaabe (Ojibwe): Bois Forte, Fond du Lac, Grand Portage, Leech Lake, Mille Lacs, Red Lake, White Earth. Four Dakota: Lower Sioux, Prairie Island, Shakopee Mdewakanton, Upper Sioux. Urban Native people also live in the Twin Cities and are not “off the list.” Each nation is a government. There is no “the tribe.”

sections.heading: The historical why
paragraphs: Broken treaties, forced removal — including Dakota exile after 1862 — allotment, boarding schools whose purpose was cultural erasure, termination, and relocation. ICWA exists because states removed Native children at staggering rates. MIFPA is Minnesota’s law. Historical trauma is not a soft feeling. It is why a county badge can mean disappearance of a child.

sections.heading: Outcomes
paragraphs: American Indian Minnesotans have among the worst health, child-welfare, and criminal-legal outcomes in the state. That is structural racism plus sovereignty denied in practice. Traditional healing, including ceremony, is not a wellness add-on you paste onto a Western plan. Nations define it. DHS has committed to working with it. Co-create with the Nation. Do not import a program and call it traditional.

sections.heading: Holistic health and land
paragraphs: Physical, mental, emotional, and spiritual are one. Land, language, and kinship are not metaphors. Relatives include more than the nuclear file. Seven-generations thinking will collide with a ninety-day review. Name the collision. Do not steamroll it as noncompliance.

sections.heading: Government-to-government
paragraphs: Office of Indian Policy. Tribal-State Relations Training (TSRT) is required for many roles; it is not this page’s homemade test. ICWA and MIFPA active efforts. Consultation is a process with Tribal leadership, not a community-partner BCC. An August 6 eList is not consultation.

sections.heading: What this is not
paragraphs: Not a culture card next to Somali foodways. Not a sweat-lodge story for a team-building day. Not urban Native people used as a substitute for the Nation when the child is a citizen of that Nation.

Four Dakota nations: Lower Sioux, Prairie Island, Shakopee Mdewakanton, Upper Sioux. Source: Minnesota Indian Affairs Council / DHS Office of Indian Policy.
