community.title: Burmese Minnesota

chapters.body:
This brief is about Burmese Minnesota as a people-page and as a warning about an umbrella. CLAS fifteen interpreter cards say Burmese. Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) says Burmese 17,123. Both are operations and a U.S. administrative name. They are not a people.

### Who this is

Not Karen as a synonym. Not Chin as a synonym. Not Kachin, not Mon, not Rohingya, not “Asian.” Compass Burmese can include Bamar — the majority people of Myanmar, often called Burman — and may overlap or sit beside Chin, Kachin, Rohingya, Mon, Karen. Compass methodology: the Census recodes some people who write Karen into Burmese, with nothing left to show the original response. Ask the people. If the household is Karen, open Karen Minnesota and put S’gaw or Pwo on the line. If Chin, book Chin — Hakha, Falam, or the variety they name. If Rohingya, Rohingya or Bengali may be the language. Burmese is not the default.

### Who this is not

Compass, dated: Twin Cities 79.9 percent, Greater Minnesota 20.1 percent. Age 17 or younger 41.5 percent; 65+ 4.2 percent. Foreign-born 67.1 percent. Language other than English (age 5+) 89.6 percent. English less than “very well” 67.0 percent — a severe language gate. High school or higher among 25+ 32.8 percent; bachelor’s or higher 11.8 percent. Median household about $75,513. Poverty 29.6 percent. Owner-occupied 59.0 percent. Average household size 4.99. Disability 12.9 percent. Date Compass. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside the umbrella is the point. A Bamar Buddhist elder who reads Myanmar script, a Hakha Chin Christian plant worker in Worthington, a S’gaw Karen household that should have opened the Karen page, a Rohingya family who should not have been booked Burmese, a U.S.-born teenager who uses English with friends and still translates a 67-percent-LEP parent — share a country checkbox and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.
chapters.evidence: Burmese Minnesota: Compass ACS 2019–2023 17,123 is an administrative umbrella. Bamar, and possibly Chin, Kachin, Rohingya, Mon, Karen overlapping. Census recodes some Karen as Burmese. Not “Asian.” CLAS fifteen: Burmese.
chapters.practitioner: There is no single Burmese client. Defer to this family. If Karen, open Karen Minnesota and put S’gaw or Pwo on the line. If Chin, book Chin (Hakha, Falam, etc.). If Rohingya, Rohingya / Bengali may be the language — not Burmese by default.
chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Bamar peoplehood on the Irrawaddy is older than the British and older than the junta. Theravada Buddhism, Burmese as a tonal language with its own script, wet-rice agriculture, and a sequence of kingdoms organized a majority that is not the whole country. Chin, Kachin, Karen, Karenni, Mon, Rakhine, Rohingya, Shan, and others are peoples, not dialects. The country checkbox that says Burma or Myanmar is already a mash.

### History for the meeting

British colonial rule, independence in 1948, and decades of military government produced the file this desk meets. 1988. 2007. 2017 in Rakhine. 2021 coup — current structure. Camps in Thailand and Bangladesh are not a personality. They are years of interrupted school, interrupted care, and a kinship the form cannot see.

### What people brought

What people brought: language (maybe Burmese, maybe not), church or monastery or mosque, large household, farming and plant skill, a memory of being hunted by a state. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled Burmese for a household that is Chin or Karen.
chapters.evidence: Bamar majority in Myanmar; many other peoples. British colonial; independence 1948; military rule. Burmese (Myanmar language) is tonal with its own script. Not one people inside the country checkbox.
chapters.practitioner: History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a golden-pagoda souvenir.
chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
Homeland is Myanmar — Yangon, Mandalay, the Delta, the hills, Chin State, Kachin State, Kayin, Rakhine. Do not draw one pagoda on a case note. Camps in Thailand (Mae La and others) and in Bangladesh (Cox’s Bazar and others) are origin-of-arrival for many Minnesota families. Years. Not a layover.

### Homeland

The U.S. map is not only Minnesota: Indiana, New York, Texas, California, and others hold Burma-origin communities. Minnesota is a real resettlement and secondary-migration state, including Greater Minnesota.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Compass Burmese 79.9 percent Twin Cities, 20.1 percent Greater Minnesota. Name the town. Worthington, Albert Lea, Austin, Marshall, and Willmar are a Karen/Burmese pattern in public telling (MSP Magazine on Minnesota’s refugee history names those towns for Karen). Do not assume St. Paul. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Yangon. A Worthington household is not a Minneapolis default.
chapters.evidence: Myanmar; camps in Thailand and Bangladesh. Compass Burmese: 79.9% Twin Cities, 20.1% Greater Minnesota. Worthington, Albert Lea, Austin, Marshall, Willmar are a Karen/Burmese pattern. Do not assume St. Paul.
chapters.practitioner: Name the town. Rural is not an afterthought. Do not assume they have been to Yangon.
chapters.title: The Geography of the Burmese World

chapters.body:
If 1975 is Hmong Minnesota and 1991 is Somali Minnesota, military rule, the camps, and the later coups are the foundational events of Burma-origin Minnesota. They are not one event and not one people.

### Foundational events

MSP Magazine’s state refugee timeline: refugees from Burma arrive in Minnesota in 1993, most of them named as Karen in that telling. Later waves include Chin, Bamar, and others. 2017 Rohingya atrocities — mass killing, rape, and expulsion, named as genocide by the United States in 2022 — produced a specific flight. 2021 military coup is current structure: kin still there, remittance, silence, status anxiety here.

### Who you meet

Camps in Thailand and Bangladesh shaped literacy, time, and who counts as family. U.S. resettlement scattered people; secondary migration and church networks pulled some to Minnesota, including plant towns.

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children and a parent facing a 67 percent LEP gate. If you only know “refugee,” you will miss the 18-year-old and still fail the form for the elder. Do not ask a Rohingya survivor to narrate the village for your chart.
chapters.evidence: Military rule; 1988; 2007; 2017 Rohingya atrocities; 2021 coup as current structure. Camps. U.S. resettlement including Greater Minnesota. MSP Mag: Burma-origin refugees from 1993, most named as Karen in that telling.
chapters.practitioner: If you only know “refugee,” you will miss the U.S.-born child and still fail the 67% LEP gate for the parent. Do not ask a Rohingya survivor to narrate the village for your chart.
chapters.title: Military Rule, Camps, 2017, 2021 — Foundational Events

chapters.body:
Households are large. Compass average household size 4.99. Married couples with children under 18 are 46.5 percent of households. Elders, in-laws, camp-made kin, adult children. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox.

### Who is in the household

Camp years shape who is kin. A cousin who is not a cousin on the English form. A missing father. A household that formed in Mae La or Cox’s Bazar. Ask who is in the room. Do not reconstruct a family tree as icebreaker.

### Who speaks

Women’s labor — plant, care, second-generation school — sits next to a household in which an elder may still be named as head. Both can be true.

Do not skip mandated reporting and call it culture. Minnesota law still stands. A nuclear two-parent English form already has a who. It was built for a different household.

chapters.title: Family

chapters.body:
Minnesota holds a Burma-origin community large enough for Compass to profile it — 17,123 on the ACS 2019–2023 umbrella — and mixed enough that the profile is a gate if you treat it as one people. This department will meet these households on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment, in St. Paul and in Worthington.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities; Roseville as a Karen Organization of Minnesota address (a Karen door); Greater Minnesota plant towns — Worthington, Albert Lea, Austin, Marshall, Willmar among those named in public Karen/Burmese telling. Compass: about one in five outside the Twin Cities. Name the town. Do not assume St. Paul.

### Partners

Partners: Karen Organization of Minnesota is a Karen door — not automatically this page. Burmese, Chin, and Rohingya groups and the churches, monasteries, and mosques families name. Pay the partner this household names. CECLC is a department door, not the whole community.

Burmese or Karen staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A New Year visit is optional professional development. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.
chapters.evidence: Compass 17,123; 20.1% Greater Minnesota. Worthington and other towns. Karen Organization of Minnesota is a Karen door — not automatically this page. Churches, monasteries, mosques families name.
chapters.practitioner: Partners, not a harvest list. Pay the partner this household names. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  Burmese or Karen staff. Do not assume St. Paul. A New Year visit does not make you the expert.
chapters.title: Minnesota and Burmese History

chapters.body:
There is not one heart under this umbrella. Bamar Theravada life, Chin Christian hill life, Karen Baptist or Buddhist life, Rohingya Muslim life — these are peoples. The U.S. file that recodes Karen as Burmese is how a census becomes a closed door.

### In this state

In Minnesota it sits inside another fact: Asian in a checkbox that also holds Hmong, Chinese, Indian, and Korean histories they do not share; camp years; Greater Minnesota isolation for some; a language gate at 67 percent LEP.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Ask who is actually in the room.
chapters.evidence: Umbrella vs people. Bamar, Chin, Karen, Rohingya are not one heart. Asian in a U.S. checkbox that also holds Hmong and Chinese. Camp years. Greater MN isolation for some.
chapters.practitioner: Do not fold this household into Hmong or “Asian Pacific.” Do not copy the Karen page onto a Bamar household or the reverse.
chapters.title: Burmese Minnesota — the heart of a people

chapters.body:
Who is in the room. Bamar, Chin, Karen, Rohingya, Mon, Kachin. Ask. The country name is not the answer.

### Language

Burmese is tonal with Myanmar script. Hakha, Falam, S’gaw, Pwo, Rohingya/Bengali are not Burmese. 67 percent LEP is the gate. Literacy in any script is not guaranteed.

### Church, monastery, mosque

Information channel for some. Not the case plan unless they asked. Sunday and moon days are operations.

### Camp time

Interrupted school, interrupted care, kin the form cannot see. 67 percent less than high school among 25+ is structure.

### Large household

4.99. Ask who should hear.

### Face and quiet endurance

A smile can be misread as agreement. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

chapters.title: Core Concepts

chapters.body:
Theravada Buddhist majority among Bamar — monastery, moon days (Uposatha), Thingyan, offerings. A monk is not the case plan unless this family asked. Do not book a monastery as DHS programming.

### Streams

Christian majority among many Chin and Karen streams in Minnesota — Baptist and other Protestant, some Catholic. Church is often the information channel and the English class and the ride. Sunday is operations. Church is not “the community” and not automatically the Karen Organization.

### Practice

Muslim Rohingya. Mosque, Ramadan, halal. Do not copy Somali Islam blindly; do not assume Burmese is the language. Ask.

Do not assume pagoda. Do not assume Baptist. Illness meaning may sit next to blessing, vow, or monastery counsel. You can hold that next to a clinic. You do not mock it. You do not skip the waiver.
chapters.evidence: Theravada Buddhist majority among Bamar; Christian majority among many Chin and Karen streams; Muslim Rohingya. Ask. Sunday and moon days are operations.
chapters.practitioner: Church vs monastery is the information channel for some. Not the case plan unless they asked. Do not assume pagoda. Do not assume Baptist.
chapters.title: Religion and Healing

chapters.body:
Elders first. A slight bow or nod with an older person is safer than a hard handshake you assume is universal. Mingalaba is a common Burmese greeting. English hello is ordinary in many rooms and in the second generation. Chin and Karen greetings are not Burmese. Follow this room.

### Titles

Say the name. Ask how to say it. Do not force a hand. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. Do not import Somali right-hand rules or Hmong nyob zoo onto this page unless this person uses them.

### This room

Do not open with the junta. Do not open with “I have a Karen friend” if this household is not Karen.
chapters.evidence: Elders first. Mingalaba in Burmese. A slight bow or nod with elders. Handshake in many English rooms — ask.
chapters.practitioner: Do not force a handshake. Do not import Somali or Hmong greeting rules. Follow this room. Say the name.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
Myanmar Bamar naming often has no family surname as the database wants. Personal names may be one, two, or more syllables. Honorifics U (for a man) and Daw (for a woman) in some rooms — titles, not first names. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. That invented name becomes a gate.

### How to file

Chin and Karen naming differ — clan, baptismal, and English names exist in those streams. Rohingya naming may follow a different Muslim pattern. Ask how to file. Ask how to say it.

Do not “correct” a mother and child who do not share a last name as a fraud signal until you have a reason. The form that demands first-middle-last and a hyphen will invent a person.
chapters.evidence: Myanmar naming often has no family surname as the database wants. Honorifics (U, Daw) in some Bamar rooms. Chin and Karen naming differ. Ask.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to say it. Do not invent a last name because the screen requires one. Do not treat unmatched names as fraud by default.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
Thingyan — Burmese New Year, mid-April — for many Bamar Buddhist households. Water festival in the homeland; quieter in Minnesota. Literacy. Not automatically this Chin or Karen family’s day.

### Calendar

Buddhist moon days are operations for some. Sunday is operations for many Chin and Karen churches. Karen New Year is a Karen page — do not steal it as a Burmese holiday. Christmas and Easter for Christian streams. Lunar Islamic dates if this family is Rohingya or otherwise Muslim.

A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Asian holiday” on a case note. Ask which calendar this family uses.
chapters.evidence: Thingyan (Burmese New Year, April) for many Bamar. Buddhist moon days. Karen New Year is a Karen page. Christmas for many Chin and Karen. Lunar Islamic dates for Rohingya.
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Ask which calendar this family uses.
chapters.title: Dates of Significance

chapters.body:
Compass Burmese, age 25+: high school or higher 32.8 percent; bachelor’s or higher 11.8 percent; less than high school 67.2 percent. Date it. Camp years and interrupted schooling are structure, not a personality and not a refusal to value school.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Burmese, Hakha, or S’gaw and limited English is not illiterate. Literacy in Burmese script is not guaranteed even when Burmese is the spoken language. The English-only IEP is the gate. So is an interpreter in the wrong language.

Second-generation children are in English-dominant schools, including Greater Minnesota. The form still has to reach the parent. 41.5 percent of the Compass umbrella is 17 or younger. That is a school-and-waiver fact, not a vibe.
chapters.evidence: Compass: among 25+, high school or higher 32.8%; bachelor’s or higher 11.8%; less than high school 67.2%. Camp years and interrupted schooling are structure, not a personality.
chapters.practitioner: A parent who speaks fluent Burmese or Hakha and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only IEP is the gate. Literacy in Burmese script is not guaranteed.
chapters.title: Education

chapters.body:
Shoes off in many homes, monasteries, and some churches. Elders first. Head is high; feet are low — do not point feet at an altar, a monk, or a person if you are in a Buddhist household. Do not touch a child’s head as friendliness.

### In the home

Hospitality is a virtue. Accept a little food if offered. You still keep medical and legal time.

### Time

Quiet endurance can be misread as agreement. A smile is not consent to the plan. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

On-time for appointments. Plant shifts, multi-household logistics, and Greater Minnesota distance are real. Name the conflict. Do not punish a no-show you built in English only.
chapters.evidence: Shoes; elders; head and feet; monastery and church. Hospitality. Quiet endurance can be misread as agreement.
chapters.practitioner: Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.
chapters.title: Etiquette

chapters.body:
Burmese (Myanmar language) is tonal and written in its own script. Confirm that this is the language. Compass: among those 5 and older, 89.6 percent speak a language other than English; 67.0 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date it. That is a severe language gate.

### Language

A “Burmese interpreter” for a Hakha Chin household is a closed door. Same for Falam, S’gaw, Pwo, Rohingya, Bengali. Put the language on the request. Literacy of the spoken language is not literacy of the form. Many camp-schooled adults do not read the script you assumed.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent.

Do not make a Burmese, Chin, or Karen coworker the interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Burmese (Myanmar language) is tonal with its own script. Compass: 89.6% other language (5+); 67.0% LEP — a severe language gate. Hakha Chin, Falam, S’gaw, Pwo, Rohingya/Bengali are not Burmese.
chapters.practitioner: A “Burmese interpreter” for a Hakha Chin household is a closed door. Put the language on the line. Literacy of the form is a separate gate. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  staff.
chapters.title: Language and Communication

chapters.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Camp years and interrupted schooling: 67.2 percent less than high school among 25+ is structure. Do not write it as laziness or as “they don’t value education.”

Rohingya genocide is a fact. The United States determined in 2022 that the 2017 atrocities were genocide. Do not platform denial in a lobby. Do not book Burmese by default for a Rohingya household. LGBTQ people exist in every stream under this umbrella. Conservative church, monastery, and mosque climates can mean silence. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture.

Greater Minnesota isolation is real — plant town, few interpreters, English IEP, a notice that never left a St. Paul eList. Name the town. Do not file this household under Karen if they are not Karen. Do not file them under Hmong. Do not file them under Asian.

Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.
chapters.evidence: Camp years; 67% less than HS among 25+; Rohingya genocide is a fact; LGBTQ exist; Greater MN isolation; do not file under Karen or Hmong.
chapters.practitioner: Do not platform genocide denial. Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.
chapters.title: Other Considerations

chapters.body:
Compass Burmese: disability 12.9 percent; among under-65, 10.0 percent; uninsured 6.2 percent. Date it. Camp and interrupted-care histories — hepatitis, anemia, dental, immunization gaps — are patterns in refugee clinical literacy nationally. This page does not invent a Minnesota clinic rate. Date a local figure when a controlling source exists.

### Access

67 percent LEP is a health gate now. Literacy of the consent form is a health gate. A Burmese-script form for a person who does not read it is still a closed door.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Believe reported pain. Do not skip developmental screening. Do not mash this page with Hmong late autism identification or Somali ADDM. Those are other intelligences.

If they name a monk, a pastor, or a healer, listen. Do not make them the case plan unless they asked.
chapters.evidence: Compass disability 12.9%; uninsured 6.2%. Camp and interrupted-care histories — date a Minnesota clinical rate when you have it. LEP 67% is a health gate now.
chapters.practitioner: Literacy of the form is a health gate. Gender match in maternal care. Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. Do not mash with Hmong late-ID or Somali ADDM.
chapters.title: Health

chapters.body:
Queer and trans Burmese, Chin, Karen, and Rohingya Minnesotans exist. Conservative church, monastery, and mosque climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private home-language life.

### This person

You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility. Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies.

So does the duty not to treat a whole umbrella as a family-values exhibit.
chapters.evidence: Queer and trans Burmese, Chin, Karen, and Rohingya Minnesotans exist. Conservative church, monastery, and mosque climates can mean silence.
chapters.practitioner: Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture.
chapters.title: LGBTQ

chapters.body:
Longyi and thanaka among some Bamar — not a daily uniform in a Worthington plant. Karen and Chin traditional dress is public at New Year, not a clinic outfit. Muslim covering among some Rohingya. Second generation looks like Minnesota.

### Dress

paragraphs: Cambodian / Khmer Minnesota. Pronounce Khmer (kuh-MARE is common English; ask). Compass ACS 2019–2023: 11,984. Not Hmong. Not Vietnamese. Not Lao. Not a Census Asian mash. Date the number you cite.

This brief is about Cambodian / Khmer people as a people with a long state history on the Mekong and a Minnesota community built after the Khmer Rouge. Pronounce Khmer. A common English rendering is kuh-MARE. Then ask. If you say “Cambodian” as if it were interchangeable with Hmong or Vietnamese, you have already told the household you did not study.

### Who this is

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Hmong. It is not Vietnamese. It is not Lao. It is not Thai. It is not a generic Southeast Asian interpreter. Shared continent is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Cambodian cultural community near 11,984. About 73.8 percent Twin Cities, 26.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 27.7 percent age 17 or younger; 11.0 percent 65+. About 50.5 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 61.2 percent; English less than “very well” 29.4 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A survivor of 1975–1979 who came through a Thai camp, a Christian grandmother, a monk whose wat is the civic center, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota household the building forgot, a college student who uses English with friends and Khmer with an elder — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

### History for the meeting

French colonial rule, independence (1953), Sihanouk, Lon Nol, and then 1975 are the modern political sequence. 1975–1979 is the foundational political event of Cambodian Minnesota. It is not the origin of the people.

### What people brought

What people brought: language and script, Theravada Buddhism and ancestor practice, farming knowledge, kinship, and a memory of a state that ate its own. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled anything but Khmer.

Do not start with embroidery or Angkor Wat as icebreaker. History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family.

community.title: Cambodian Minnesota

chapters.body:
This brief is about Cambodian / Khmer people as a people with a long state history on the Mekong and a Minnesota community built after the Khmer Rouge. Pronounce Khmer. A common English rendering is kuh-MARE. Then ask. If you say “Cambodian” as if it were interchangeable with Hmong or Vietnamese, you have already told the household you did not study.

### Who this is

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Hmong. It is not Vietnamese. It is not Lao. It is not Thai. It is not a generic Southeast Asian interpreter. Shared continent is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Cambodian cultural community near 11,984. About 73.8 percent Twin Cities, 26.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 27.7 percent age 17 or younger; 11.0 percent 65+. About 50.5 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 61.2 percent; English less than “very well” 29.4 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A survivor of 1975–1979 who came through a Thai camp, a Christian grandmother, a monk whose wat is the civic center, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota household the building forgot, a college student who uses English with friends and Khmer with an elder — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Khmer peoplehood is older than the refugee file and older than the French protectorate. The Khmer Empire — Angkor as literacy for the desk, not a tourism sentence — is a state history with writing, irrigation, and monumental architecture. Khmer language and Khmer script are not oral-only. That matters when an English form meets an elder who reads Khmer, and when it meets an elder who does not.

### History for the meeting

French colonial rule, independence (1953), Sihanouk, Lon Nol, and then 1975 are the modern political sequence. 1975–1979 is the foundational political event of Cambodian Minnesota. It is not the origin of the people.

### What people brought

What people brought: language and script, Theravada Buddhism and ancestor practice, farming knowledge, kinship, and a memory of a state that ate its own. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled anything but Khmer.

Do not start with embroidery or Angkor Wat as icebreaker. History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family.

chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
Homeland is Cambodia — the Mekong, Tonle Sap, Phnom Penh, the provinces people name. Khmer people also live in the Mekong delta and in a global diaspora: California (Long Beach among the named U.S. hubs), Massachusetts, Minnesota, France, Australia. Thai border camps — Khao-I-Dang and others — are exile geography, not home.

### Homeland

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): 73.8 percent Twin Cities, 26.2 percent Greater Minnesota. Greater Minnesota is not an afterthought. Watt Munisotaram stands in Empire Township / Hampton, Dakota County — Twin Cities metro, a wat on farmland, not a downtown festival.

### Minnesota

Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Cambodia. Secondary migration built parts of this map.

chapters.title: The Geography of the Khmer World

chapters.body:
If the Secret War is the foundational event of Hmong Minnesota and 1991 of Somali Minnesota, the Khmer Rouge years 1975–1979 and the Killing Fields are the foundational event of Cambodian Minnesota.

### Foundational events

17 April 1975: Phnom Penh fell. The Khmer Rouge emptied cities, abolished money and schools, murdered intellectuals, monks, and anyone marked as enemy, and worked and starved the rest. 1975–1979 is not a personality. It is not an icebreaker. Do not ask a survivor to narrate killing for your professional development.

### Who you meet

Vietnamese invasion, 1979. Camps in Thailand. Resettlement to the United States in the late 1970s and 1980s through voluntary agencies and churches. Secondary migration. The desk in 2026 also meets their children — U.S.-born, English-dominant with peers, still translating for parents, still unable to get Khmer in the lobby.

U.S. policy later deported people with certain convictions, including people who have lived here since childhood. That is current structure. Do not collect status you do not need.

This brief is about Chinese Minnesota as a mosaic, not a country checkbox. People here name the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau, and Chinese communities that have lived for generations in Southeast Asia. Students, skilled professionals, restaurant and small-business households, and adoptees sit in the same Compass row and do not share a Tuesday.

### Who this is

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Chinese ancestry near 41,717. About 81.8 percent Twin Cities, 18.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 25.7 percent age 17 or younger; 8.3 percent 65 and older. Foreign-born about 57.5 percent. Among those 5 and older, language other than English about 62.5 percent; English less than “very well” about 29.2 percent. High school or higher (25+) about 86.0 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 62.4 percent. Median household income about $103,600 in 2022 dollars. Poverty 8.6 percent. The CLAS fifteen includes Cantonese. Cantonese is not Mandarin and not “Chinese” as a file. Taishanese, Hokkien, and Shanghainese exist in this country and may exist in this lobby. An interpreter labeled Chinese can still be a closed door. Book Cantonese for a Cantonese household. Book Mandarin for Mandarin. Ask.

### Who this is not

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Hmong. It is not Vietnamese. It is not Korean. It is not Japanese. Shared continent is not shared culture. Lunar New Year is not Hmong New Year and not Tết. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### How to read this

The diversity inside this Compass row is the point. A Cantonese-speaking elder, a Mandarin-speaking graduate student, a Taiwanese professional, a Hong Kong family that left after 1997 or after 2019, a Toisan restaurant household, a U.S.-born child, a person adopted from the PRC into a white Minnesota family — share a checkbox and do not share a language, a politics, or a church.

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

There is no single origin story that will fit the lobby. Civilizations on the Yellow and Yangtze rivers, many spoken languages, and successive states — imperial, republican, socialist, and the Republic of China on Taiwan after 1949 — are literacy for the meeting. They are not a lecture you give a parent who came in for a waiver.

### History for the meeting

Overseas Chinese communities are older than Minnesota. Nineteenth-century labor in the American West, merchant networks in Southeast Asia, and later student and professional migration are different founding events. The person in front of you may descend from one of those, or from none of them, or from more than one.

Writing is not one script in practice. Standard written Chinese can be shared across speakers who cannot understand each other’s speech. Traditional characters are ordinary in Taiwan and among many Hong Kong and diaspora readers; simplified characters are ordinary in the PRC. That is a materials problem, not trivia.

### What people brought

Language, family obligation, education as a mobility strategy and as pressure, foodways, ancestral rite or a secular refusal of it, a memory of states that claimed them. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled “Chinese.”

chapters.body:
This brief is about Chinese Minnesota as a mosaic, not a country checkbox. People here name the People’s Republic of China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Macau, and Chinese communities that have lived for generations in Southeast Asia. Students, skilled professionals, restaurant and small-business households, and adoptees sit in the same Compass row and do not share a Tuesday.

### Who this is

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Chinese ancestry near 41,717. About 81.8 percent Twin Cities, 18.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 25.7 percent age 17 or younger; 8.3 percent 65 and older. Foreign-born about 57.5 percent. Among those 5 and older, language other than English about 62.5 percent; English less than “very well” about 29.2 percent. High school or higher (25+) about 86.0 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 62.4 percent. Median household income about $103,600 in 2022 dollars. Poverty 8.6 percent. Owner-occupied about 69.5 percent. Average household size about 2.59. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The CLAS fifteen includes Cantonese. Cantonese is not Mandarin and not “Chinese” as a file. Taishanese, Hokkien, and Shanghainese exist in this country and may exist in this lobby. An interpreter labeled Chinese can still be a closed door. Book Cantonese for a Cantonese household. Book Mandarin for Mandarin. Ask.

### Who this is not

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Hmong. It is not Vietnamese. It is not Korean. It is not Japanese. Shared continent is not shared culture. Lunar New Year is not Hmong New Year and not Tết. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### How to read this

The diversity inside this Compass row is the point. A Cantonese-speaking elder, a Mandarin-speaking graduate student, a Taiwanese professional, a Hong Kong family that left after 1997 or after 2019, a Toisan restaurant household, a U.S.-born child, a person adopted from the PRC into a white Minnesota family — share a checkbox and do not share a language, a politics, or a church.

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
There is no single origin story that will fit the lobby. Civilizations on the Yellow and Yangtze rivers, many spoken languages, and successive states — imperial, republican, socialist, and the Republic of China on Taiwan after 1949 — are literacy for the meeting. They are not a lecture you give a parent who came in for a waiver.

### History for the meeting

Overseas Chinese communities are older than Minnesota. Nineteenth-century labor in the American West, merchant networks in Southeast Asia, and later student and professional migration are different founding events. The person in front of you may descend from one of those, or from none of them, or from more than one.

Writing is not one script in practice. Standard written Chinese can be shared across speakers who cannot understand each other’s speech. Traditional characters are ordinary in Taiwan and among many Hong Kong and diaspora readers; simplified characters are ordinary in the PRC. That is a materials problem, not trivia.

### What people brought

Language, family obligation, education as a mobility strategy and as pressure, foodways, ancestral rite or a secular refusal of it, a memory of states that claimed them. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled “Chinese.”

### Homeland

Chinese communities in Southeast Asia — Vietnam, Malaysia, Singapore, and others — carry other states’ histories. A Chinese Vietnamese household is not a Beijing file. Open Vietnamese Minnesota if that is the household they name. Open this if they name Chinese.

The U.S. Chinese map is California, New York, and also this Upper Midwest university-and-restaurant state. Compass: about 81.8 percent Twin Cities, 18.2 percent Greater Minnesota. Date Compass. Do not invent a dialect map.

### Minnesota

Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume they have been to Beijing, Taipei, or Hong Kong. A Greater Minnesota restaurant household is still this people. A university apartment is still this people. An adoptee raised in a western Minnesota town is still this people.

chapters.title: The Geography of the Chinese World

chapters.body:
Chinese Minnesota is stacked. There is no single 1975. Labor on the American West, the Chinese Exclusion Act, the 1949 split, Hart-Celler, students, Hong Kong, and PRC-born adoptees are different doors into the same Compass row.

### Foundational events

May 6, 1882: the Chinese Exclusion Act. Scott Act (1888) and Geary Act (1892) tightened it. Magnuson Act repealed Exclusion in 1943 and set a tiny quota. Hart-Celler (October 1965) opened family and skilled immigration. That is U.S. literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family.

1949: the People’s Republic of China on the mainland; the Republic of China on Taiwan. Households that name either are not a mash you referee. Students and skilled workers from the 1980s sit next to restaurant and small-business streams that are older. Hong Kong 1997 and the 2019–20 exits are later doors. PRC-born adoptees into Minnesota families are this state’s history, not a side note.

### Who you meet

COVID-era anti-Asian climate is current structure. Stop Asian Hate gathered at the Minnesota State Capitol on March 28, 2021. Date that. Do not invent this person’s story. Do not collect status you do not need.

If you only know “international student,” you will miss the Cantonese elder and the adoptee who does not want a cultural volunteer at the bedside.

Family-name-first. Obligation to elders is a hypothesis, not a waiver design. Compass: average household size about 2.59. Smaller than some neighboring spines. Still not always a nuclear English form.

### Who is in the household

Who cares for a disabled adult or a child may be a son, a daughter-in-law, a sibling — not the legally recognized caregiver on the checkbox. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Adoptee households exist: white Minnesota parents and a Chinese-born adult child. Kin search may point to the PRC, to a closed file, or to no one. Do not assume Chinese relatives in the metro. Do not assume the adoptive family is the barrier or the solution. Ask this person.

### Who speaks

community.title: Colombian Minnesota

chapters.body:
This brief is about Colombian people as a people with a country — Andean, Caribbean, Pacific, llanos, Amazon — and a Minnesota community the building will mash into Mexican if you let it. This is not Mexican. It is not Ecuadorian as a synonym. It is not one Spanish. Paisa, costeño, bogotano, vallecaucano are not an accent test you run in the lobby. Afro-Colombian and indigenous peoples exist inside the republic. Ask this household. Do not invent a Minnesota indigenous-language speaker count.

### Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one Latino blob, one “Spanish interpreter,” a cartel joke as icebreaker, and an English form because Compass bachelor’s attainment looks high.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Colombian ancestry near 9,431. About 70.1 percent Twin Cities, about 29.9 percent Greater Minnesota — not an afterthought. About 25.6 percent age 17 or younger; about 4.4 percent 65+. About 41.5 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 40.0 percent; English less than “very well” 16.3 percent. High school or higher 95.1 percent; bachelor’s or higher 52.1 percent. Poverty 7.1 percent. Uninsured 11.4 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Medellín professional, a Caribbean-coast household, an Afro-Colombian student, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota family, a person who left because of conflict and will not name it in the lobby, a second-generation kid who uses English with friends and Spanish with an elder — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Colombia is not one people inside one flag. Andean interior, Caribbean coast, Pacific, llanos, Amazon. Afro-Colombian nations and communities. Indigenous nations — Wayuu, Nasa, Embera, and others — inside the republic. Mestizo majority narratives do not erase those histories. Shared Spanish is not shared culture.

### History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, African enslavement, indigenous survival, a republic, and a half-century of armed conflict produced the streams you will meet. “Hispanic” on a U.S. form is an ethnicity checkbox. People in this page check white, Black, American Indian, other, two or more.

### What people brought

What people brought: regional Spanish, kinship, parish and later evangelical church, professional and trade skill, and a living memory of a state and of a war that is not one war. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one Latino module, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, a Mexican default, and a drug-war headline someone thought was icebreaker.

History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with coffee, a telenovela, or a cartel sentence.

chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
Homeland is not one city. Bogotá is not Medellín. Cali is not Barranquilla. The Pacific is not the Caribbean. Regional Spanish, food, and some kinship patterns shift. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee paisa versus costeño in a waiver meeting. Listen.

### Homeland

In the United States, Florida, New York, and New Jersey hold large Colombian communities. Minnesota is not Miami. Do not import a Doral picture onto a Ramsey County lobby.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities 70.1 percent; Greater Minnesota 29.9 percent — not an afterthought. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Colombia.

chapters.body:
Colombian Minnesota is not an IRCA file and not a 1975 poster. Professional and family streams; internal displacement as a named Colombian fact (desplazados); later asylum and, for some, Temporary Protected Status as a possible U.S. path — pattern now, not a Minnesota count. Do not invent a TPS number. Do not collect status you do not need.

### Foundational events

Armed conflict — guerrilla, paramilitary, state, 2016 peace, later violence in some regions — is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not every household. The U.S. drug war sat on top of that stack and still sits in a lobby joke. You do not make the joke.

### Who you meet

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children, mixed-status households, a professional who does not need an interpreter and whose elder does, and a person who will not put a relative’s name on a form. Compass foreign-born 41.5 percent (ACS 2019–2023) — dated, not a personality.

If you only know “immigrant” or only know “cartel,” you will miss them.

chapters.title: Minnesota and Colombian History

chapters.body:
To be Colombian in Minnesota is to be placed in a U.S. checkbox that holds Mexican as the default and a news cycle that holds a cartel as the icebreaker. There is a peoplehood here the mash deletes: regional Spanish, Afro-Colombian and indigenous histories, professional and working-class lives, conflict memory for some and a history class for others.

### In this state

Mexican Minnesota is the largest Latino origin in this state. That fact becomes a harm when the building treats Mexican Spanish as the Latino default. A costeño household, a paisa household, and an Afro-Colombian household are not variants of Mexico.

In the U.S. racial order, Hispanic is ethnicity, not race. Colorism inside this page is real. Afro-Colombian people exist — ask, do not mash them into historic African American, and do not bleach them into a mestizo story. Drug-war stigma is a named harm. You do not write it as ethnicity.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to this family.

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, indigenous, English, or both. Ask.

chapters.body:
This brief is about Cuban people as a people with a country and a Minnesota community the building will mash into Mexican — or into Puerto Rican — if you let it. This is not Mexican. It is not interchangeable with Puerto Rican. Puerto Rican is U.S. citizenship under the Jones Act (1917). Cuban is not that file. 1959, Mariel (1980), 1994 balseros, and later streams are not one exile story. Spanish is Caribbean Spanish, not Mexican.

### Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one Latino blob, one “Spanish interpreter,” a 1959 speech you give a U.S.-born twenty-year-old, and collecting status because you learned the word Mariel.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Cuban ancestry near 9,406. About 67.3 percent Twin Cities, about 32.7 percent Greater Minnesota — not an afterthought. About 34.1 percent age 17 or younger; about 8.9 percent 65+. About 21.9 percent foreign-born — which means a large share was born here. Language other than English (age 5+) 39.3 percent; English less than “very well” 11.4 percent. Poverty 10.5 percent. Owner 45.0 percent. Disability 21.5 percent. Date the number you use. Do not invent a cause. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A 1960s exile elder, a Mariel arrival, a 1994 balsero, a later-stream parent, a U.S.-born nurse, an Afro-Cuban student, a Greater Minnesota household, a person who left 1959 politics and still shows up at a parish — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to this family.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
paragraphs: Not Mexican; Spanish is not one Spanish; indigenous language as a possible home language; two surnames; familismo as hypothesis; Costa/Sierra/Oriente; enforcement climate.
You work with these as hypotheses you still test. Confirm the language. Do not make a priest the case plan unless this family asked.

Not Mexican. The first grammar. If you open a Mexican default because the name is Spanish, you do not have a household yet.

### Spanish is not one Spanish

Andean register (usted) is not coastal, and neither is Mexican. Book qualified Spanish AND ask.

### Indigenous language as a possible home language

Kichwa, Shuar, others. Compass notes the possibility. It is not a speaker count. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Name the language on the request.

### Two surnames

Dropping the second invents a person.

### Familismo as hypothesis

Ask who should be in the room. Not a license to skip mandated reporting.

### Enforcement climate

Mixed-status. Do not collect status you do not need.

sections.heading: Religion
paragraphs: Catholic majority in many streams; evangelical and Pentecostal large in some; indigenous practice. Parish may be the trusted channel.
Do not make a priest or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Do not treat indigenous practice as folklore. Hispanic Heritage Month is not consultation.

Catholic majority in many streams — not all. The parish may be the trusted channel for information, mutual aid, and a room people will enter when they will not enter yours. Evangelical and Pentecostal churches are large in some rooms. Indigenous practice lives here and is not a souvenir.

### Streams

Do not make a priest, a pastor, or a healer the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one parish and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic, or indigenous practice as witchcraft.

### Practice

Holy Week, fiestas families name, and funeral obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

sections.heading: Greetings
paragraphs: Handshake common. Titles — Señor, Señora, Don, Doña — until invited. Elders first. Usted is respect in many Andean Spanish rooms.
Follow this room. Do not force a first name on an elder because the form printed it. Do not import Somali or Mexican-default greeting rules as if they were Ecuador.

Handshake is common in many rooms. A slight nod with an elder is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth. Follow this room. Do not initiate a cheek kiss because a training slide said Latinos are tactile.

### Titles

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it. Usted versus tú is respect in many Andean Spanish rooms; a qualified interpreter matches register. You do not correct it.

### This room

Elders first. Greet the people in the room, not only the English speaker.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. Cross-gender touch: follow this room.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
paragraphs: Two surnames: apellido paterno + apellido materno. U.S. databases that keep one invent a person. Indigenous given names in some families. Ask.
Ask. Pronounce. Do not drop the second surname as clutter. Unmatched last names in a household are not fraud by default.

Two surnames is the default in much of Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

### How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, indigenous, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.

A parent who speaks fluent Spanish, or fluent Kichwa, and limited English is not illiterate. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. Oral Spanish is not print Spanish. Mixtec is a Mexican door; Kichwa is this one. A Spanish IEP is still a closed door if Spanish is not the home language.

chapters.body:
This brief is about Ecuadorian people as a people with a country — Costa, Sierra, Amazon/Oriente, Galápagos — and a Minnesota community the building will mash into Mexican if you let it. This is not Mexican. It is not Colombian as a synonym. It is not one Spanish. Indigenous languages may be in the home: Kichwa, Shuar, others. Compass notes the possibility; it is not a count of speakers. Do not invent that count. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door.

### Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one Latino blob, one “Spanish interpreter,” an SSN field on the first screen, and an English IEP written for a household the building never studied.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Ecuadorian ancestry near 18,271. About 94.0 percent Twin Cities, about 6.0 percent Greater Minnesota. About 42.7 percent age 17 or younger; about 2.1 percent 65+. About 49.8 percent foreign-born. Language other than English (age 5+) 76.4 percent; English less than “very well” 44.6 percent. Poverty 20.2 percent. Uninsured 21.6 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Kichwa-speaking mother who does not use Spanish as a home language, an Afro-Ecuadorian student, a coastal Spanish speaker, a Sierra household that uses usted, a U.S.-born child in an English-dominant school, a professional second generation, a mixed-status kitchen table — share a Census checkbox and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Ecuador is not one people inside one flag. Costa, Sierra, Amazon/Oriente, Galápagos. Kichwa (Runa Shimi) and other indigenous nations live inside the republic. Shuar and other Amazonian peoples. Afro-Ecuadorian streams in Esmeraldas and the Valle del Chota. Mestizo majority narratives do not erase those histories. Shared Spanish is not shared culture.

### History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, indigenous survival, African enslavement on the coast, a republic, and later dollarization and emigration produced the streams you will meet. “Hispanic” on a U.S. form is an ethnicity checkbox. People in this page check white, Black, American Indian, other, two or more. The form that treats Hispanic as a race has already mashed.

### What people brought

What people brought: Spanish varieties and indigenous languages, kinship, parish and later evangelical church, work knowledge, and a living memory of a state and of a crisis that moved people. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one Latino module, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, and a Mexican default.

History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with food, a hat, or a Heritage Month sentence.

chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
Homeland is not one climate. Quito and the Sierra are not Guayaquil. The Amazon is not the coast. Galápagos is a name some families hold and most Minnesota desks will never need. Regional Spanish and indigenous languages do not travel as a blob. Do not referee Quito versus Guayaquil in a waiver meeting. Listen if they name a place.

### Homeland

In the United States, New York and New Jersey hold large Ecuadorian communities. Minnesota is not Queens. Do not import a Roosevelt Avenue picture onto a Hennepin County lobby.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities is the Compass split — 94.0 percent. Greater Minnesota is 6.0 percent, not zero. Do not copy a Worthington plant-town default from Mexican Minnesota onto this page, and do not assume Minneapolis is every household. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Ecuador.

chapters.title: The Geography of Ecuador and Ecuadorian Minnesota

chapters.body:
If IRCA is a foundational settlement fact of Mexican Minnesota, Ecuadorian Minnesota is not that file. Labor and family streams; the 1999–2000 banking crisis (feriado bancario) as a named emigration wave toward Spain and the United States; later family reunification and work; secondary migration from other states.

### Foundational events

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born children translating for parents, mixed-status households, a Kichwa household that has been here for years and still cannot get the language in the lobby, and a professional who does not need an interpreter and whose elder does. Compass foreign-born 49.8 percent (ACS 2019–2023) — dated, not a personality.

### Who you meet

Enforcement is current structure. When raids or a visible ICE climate spike, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. The desk that asks “are you legal?” on visit one has already chosen a who.

If you only know “immigrant” or only know “Latino,” you will miss them.

### Who is in the household

Mixed-status is structure: a U.S.-citizen child, a parent without status, a sibling with another path. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names, a grandmother as caregiver, or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason.

### Who speaks

Familismo is a hypothesis, not a rule: obligation to kin can mean fierce showing-up and can mean a woman who never signs for herself. Both can be true. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family. Do not skip the report and call it respeto. Do not use a child as interpreter.

chapters.body:
To be Ecuadorian in Minnesota is to be placed in a U.S. checkbox that holds Mexican as the default. There is a peoplehood here the mash deletes: Costa, Sierra, Oriente; Kichwa and other indigenous nations; Afro-Ecuadorian histories; U.S.-born lives. Spanish is not the people.

### In this state

Mexican Minnesota is the largest Latino origin in this state. That fact becomes a harm when the building treats Mexican Spanish, Mexican parish, and Mexican food as the Latino default. An Andean household, a Kichwa household, and an Afro-Ecuadorian household are not variants of Mexico.

In the U.S. racial order, Hispanic is ethnicity, not race. Colorism inside this page is real. Indigenous erasure under “they all speak Spanish” is real. Afro-Ecuadorian people exist — ask, do not mash them into historic African American, and do not bleach them into a mestizo story.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to this family.

Elders first. Greet the people in the room, not only the English speaker.

### How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, indigenous, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.
