chapters.title: Religion

chapters.body:
Elders first. Mano — taking an elder’s hand to the forehead — is ordinary in some rooms. A handshake is ordinary in many professional rooms and in much of the second generation. Follow this room. Do not force a mano you saw in a video. Do not force a hug.

### Titles

Po and opo mark respect in Tagalog. You do not need to perform them. You need to book an interpreter who can. English “hello” plus the name is ordinary. Say the name.

### This room

Do not import Chinese, Japanese, Hmong, or Somali greeting rules onto this page.

Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default.
chapters.evidence: Elders first. Mano in some rooms (hand to forehead). Handshake in many professional rooms. Po / opo as respect in Tagalog.
chapters.practitioner: Follow this room. Do not force a mano you saw in a video. Do not force a hug. Do not import Chinese or Hmong greeting rules. Say the name.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
Spanish surnames are Filipino history: Santos, Cruz, Reyes, Garcia, Ramos, de la Cruz, Mendoza. They are not a Latino file. Do not run a Mexican or Puerto Rican script because the last name looks Spanish. Do not mash with the Latino CI. Open that CI when the household is that household.

### How to file

Multiple given names and a mother’s family name in Philippine records can collide with a U.S. form that wants one first, one last. The same person can appear as Maria Santos, Maria Cruz Santos, and Maria C. Santos. That is a system failure, not a fraud signal until you have a reason.

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Nicknames are ordinary. Do not treat unmatched names as fraud. Women may or may not take a husband’s name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match.
chapters.evidence: Spanish surnames — Santos, Cruz, Reyes, Garcia, Ramos — are Filipino history, not a Latino file. Multiple given names. U.S. forms flatten.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not treat a Spanish surname as Mexican. Do not treat unmatched names as fraud.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
Christmas and Holy Week are large in many Catholic rooms. Travel, food, elders, closed shops. Schedule around them when you can. They are not a day off the work. A calendar click is not community engagement.

### Calendar

12 June — Philippine Independence Day (from Spain, declared 1898; the date many Filipino Americans mark). 4 July 1946 is the U.S. recognition date. Literacy. Not a party on a case note. People Power / EDSA, February 1986 — literacy, not a speech.

Parish fiestas and hometown associations will not be on your state calendar. Ask. Do not put “Asian holiday” on a case note. Do not mash with Chinese New Year, Hmong New Year, or Tết.
chapters.evidence: Christmas and Holy Week in many Catholic rooms. Independence Day 12 June. People Power / EDSA 1986 is literacy. Fiestas are household and parish, not “Asian holiday.”
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Asian holiday” on a case note.
chapters.title: Dates of Significance

chapters.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023), among Filipino Minnesotans 25 and older: about 92.3 percent high school or higher; about 53.8 percent bachelor’s or higher. English only about 59.6 percent among those 5 and older. LEP about 8.4 percent. Foreign-born about 38.4 percent. Date Compass.

### School and language

English is official in the Philippines. That sentence will be used to skip the interpreter. 8.4 percent LEP is not zero. An English IEP still closes the door for the parent who reads Tagalog and limited English. That parent is not illiterate.

A nursing degree is labor history in this community. It is not this teenager. It is not proof the waiver household needs no interpreter. Education pressure in some streams is a hypothesis. It is not an excuse to skip mental-health screening.
chapters.evidence: Compass (25+): HS+ 92.3%; bachelor+ 53.8%. English only 59.6%. LEP 8.4%. Foreign-born 38.4%. English official in the Philippines is not a skip.
chapters.practitioner: Do not skip the interpreter because attainment is high or because English is official there. A lola who reads Tagalog and limited English is not illiterate.
chapters.title: Education

chapters.body:
Elders first. Hospitality. Accept a little food if offered. Shoes off in some homes. Follow this room. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Hiya — shame, propriety, the cost of a public no — is a hypothesis in some rooms. A yes that is courtesy is not a signature. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

### Time

Do not photograph a home altar or a wall of overseas family. Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter.

Courtesy-yes then no-show happens when the plan was never agreed. Ask again, plainly, without humiliation.

Tagalog / Filipino is not the only language. Cebuano (Bisaya), Ilocano, and others live in this Compass row. Book THIS language. An interpreter labeled Asian, or Tagalog for a Cebuano elder, can still be a closed door. Still book a qualified interpreter.

### Language

Compass: language other than English about 40.4 percent; LEP about 8.4 percent (age 5+). Date it. English official in the Philippines is not a skip. New arrivals and elders are inside that 8.4 percent. English-dominant second generation is inside the 59.6 percent English-only and still on this page.

A short English yes may be exhaustion, courtesy, or hiya. Do not take a smile as consent. Do not make a Filipino coworker the interpreter. Do not make a a nurse coworker the interpreter as the culture.

chapters.title: Language and Communication

chapters.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Model-minority is a weapon. English official, 53.8 percent bachelor’s, and a nursing pipeline will be used to skip 8.4 percent LEP, 7.3 percent poverty, disability, and the lola who does not read the IEP. That skip is the policy.

U.S. colonial amnesia is a building problem. 1898 and occupation are literacy. They are not a speech. They are a reason a government badge is not automatically help.

Remittance labor is work, not a personality. Martial-law memory still sits in some rooms. You do not icebreak with it. You do not put it on a case note as color.

LGBTQ Filipino Minnesotans exist. Undocumented and visa-overstay households exist. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

chapters.practitioner: Do not collect status you do not need. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Do not out anyone. Do not skip screening because they are a nurse.
chapters.title: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice

chapters.body:
Believe reported pain. Do not invent “Asian stoicism.” Do not fold this into a generic Asian slide. Nursing as a community labor pattern does not mean this person is fine.

### Access

Do not invent a Minnesota diabetes, heart, or suicide rate. Date the CDC page you cite if you cite one. Do not skip screening because the person is a nurse or English-dominant.

Mental-health stigma is real in some families. Naming a counselor is not the same as a family accepting one. A smile is not a PHQ-9. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it.

Hilot, herbs, and parish prayer often sit beside biomedicine. Ask. Co-create. Do not mock. Do not skip a child-protection duty when the facts are the facts. A Filipino nurse on staff is not the interpreter and not the culture unit.
chapters.evidence: Nursing pipeline is labor, not a personality. Believe reported pain. Do not invent “Asian stoicism.” Mental-health stigma in some streams. Do not invent a Minnesota rate.
chapters.practitioner: Book the language. Do not skip screening. Gender match may be requested. Ask what they use. A coworker who is a nurse is not the interpreter.
chapters.title: Health

chapters.body:
Queer and trans Filipino Minnesotans exist. Conservative parish climates can mean silence or exile. Bakla and trans people are not a joke, not entertainment, and not a file you invent from a TV clip. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder or a priest as cultural humility.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a family-values exhibit.

Do not assume a Catholic household is not affirming. Do not assume a secular household is. Ask this person.
chapters.evidence: Queer and trans Filipino Minnesotans exist. Conservative parish climates can mean silence. Bakla and trans people are not a joke and not a file you invent.

chapters.title: LGBTQ

chapters.body:
Barong tagalog and terno are public at weddings, independence stages, and some parish events. They are not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

Hair and head: follow this person. Do not touch.

Do not mash barong with a qipao, an áo dài, or a kimono on the unit’s Heritage Month table. Spanish-colonial dress history is not a Latino mash and not a China mash.

chapters.practitioner: Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch. Do not mash with a qipao or an áo dài on an “Asian” table.
chapters.title: Hair, Dress, and Body

chapters.body:
Parish music is ordinary in Catholic streams. Karaoke is social life in some rooms. Kundiman, pop, and none. Not one soundtrack.

### Variation

A playlist is not engagement. Karaoke is not consultation. Do not ask a staff person or a client to perform.

A funeral is not staff entertainment. Fiesta stages are public life. They are not a case plan.

chapters.title: Music

Basketball is public culture for some Filipino households. It is not the case plan and not this teenager. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Do not assume the kid plays.

### Not the whole person

Sport clubs are not language access. An elder in the stands who needs Tagalog still needs Tagalog. 8.4 percent LEP is not a skip because the child plays varsity.

A Saturday tournament does not replace an interpreter on Monday.

chapters.title: Sports

Tagalog / Filipino, English, a Spanish colonial archive, and regional languages. This is not a people without letters. You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby.

### Literacy in the lobby

Literacy in Tagalog is not guaranteed for every generation. A Tagalog notice can still be a closed door. An English notice can still be a closed door. Ask which language they read.

Do not put a proverb on a brochure and call it language access.

Parish fiesta, weaving, diaspora visual work, and the public culture of groceries and independence stages. Foodway is not consultation.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. A grocery visit is not a case plan. A museum visit is optional professional development. It is not consultation.

Heritage Month that mashes this with Hmong paj ntaub or a Chinese lion dance has already mashed the adjacent peoples.

chapters.body:
Spanish colonial rule, the 1898 U.S. war and occupation, WWII, independence, Marcos martial law, U.S. bases, and a labor-export nursing pipeline — that is the political file. A DHS badge is not automatically help.

### The badge

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
paragraphs: Guatemalan Minnesota. Compass ACS 2019–2023: 17,172; Greater MN 46.5% — nearly half. K’iche’, Mam, other Mayan languages. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Not Mexican. Not the Latino umbrella. Date the number you cite.
There is no single Guatemalan client. Defer to this family. Do not open a Mexican or Latino-umbrella case with this page. Ask language. Pronounce the name.

This brief is about Guatemalan Minnesota as a people — guatemalteco, guatemalteca — and as Maya nations inside a republic, not as a Mexican variant and not as the Latino / Hispanic umbrella. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Kaqchikel and other Mayan languages are in this state. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. This is not Mexican. It is not Salvadoran. It is not Puerto Rican. Shared Spanish is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is

Open the Latino umbrella only as adjacent. That page is the mash and the CLAS Spanish line. This page is Guatemalan. If you leave this door and file the household under “Latino” or under Mexican because that is the Minnesota default, you have left this door.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Guatemalan cultural community at 17,172. Twin Cities 53.5 percent; Greater Minnesota 46.5 percent — nearly half. About 47.3 percent age 17 or younger. Compass suppresses 65+ in this vintage — do not invent it. Foreign-born 46.7 percent. Language other than English (age 5+) 58.8 percent; English less than “very well” 33.7 percent. Date the number you use. Compass does not count K’iche’ or Mam speakers. Do not invent that count. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A K’iche’-speaking mother in a plant town who does not use Spanish as a home language, a Mam dairy worker, a ladino Spanish-speaking professional in the Cities, a U.S.-born child in an English school, an evangelical grandmother, a person who left the highlands in the 1980s and still will not open the door to a badge — share a passport word and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
paragraphs: Guatemala holds Maya nations — K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Kaqchikel and others — inside a Spanish-language republic. Colonization, ladino state, indigenous survival. Not a Mexican origin story.
History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a textile tourism sentence.

Guatemalan peoplehood is not a Mexican origin story with different mountains. Maya nations — K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Kaqchikel, and others — are older than the Spanish colony and older than the republic. The republic is Spanish-language, ladino-dominated, and has both claimed and hunted those nations. Minnesota’s community includes Maya households and ladino Spanish-speaking households. Ask. Do not lecture a Willmar family about taxonomy they did not ask for.

### History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, independence with the other Central American republics (15 September 1821), a nineteenth- and twentieth-century plantation state, and the civil war that followed — that is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a huipil, a volcano postcard, or a Heritage Month sentence.

### What people brought

Writing in Spanish is the state’s public literacy. Mayan languages are languages, not dialects of Spanish. Some people read Spanish. Some do not. Some U.S.-born adults do not read Spanish either. Oral skill is not print. Some Maya literacy is oral and in a language the building has never put on an interpreter line.

What people brought: language (Spanish varieties and Mayan languages), kinship, costumbre and later evangelical church, farm skill, a memory of a state that used them and of villages that were emptied. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Latino” checkbox, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, and a plant town that had not studied Mam.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Guatemalan World
paragraphs: Highlands, coast, Petén; Maya geographies that do not match the republic’s map. U.S. Guatemalan America includes California and the Upper Midwest plant belt. Compass: 53.5% Twin Cities, 46.5% Greater Minnesota.
A Worthington, Willmar, or dairy-county household is not a Minneapolis default. Do not assume they have been to Guatemala. Greater Minnesota is not an afterthought.

Homeland is not one flag on a classroom map. Highlands, coast, Petén; K’iche’ country, Mam country, Q’eqchi’ country — geographies that do not match the republic’s departments as the person in the lobby may name them. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee Quetzaltenango versus San Marcos in a waiver meeting. Listen.

### Homeland

The U.S. Guatemalan map includes California and also the Upper Midwest plant and dairy belt that a Minneapolis default still treats as leftover. Compass: 53.5 percent Twin Cities, 46.5 percent Greater Minnesota. Nearly half. Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea, and dairy counties are names you should be able to hold without turning them into a tour.

### Minnesota

Metro pockets exist. They are not the whole. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Guatemala. A Greater Minnesota household is still this people. Open rural literacy beside this page when place is the gate.

sections.heading: War, Maya Flight, and Plant Towns — Foundational Event
paragraphs: Civil war 1960–1996; 1980s scorched earth against Maya communities; later gang and state violence; plant and dairy labor in Greater Minnesota. Not IRCA-Mexican as the file.
If you only know “immigrant,” you will miss the U.S.-born child and the Mam speaker who has been in a plant town for years and still cannot get Mam in the lobby.

If IRCA-era settlement is a foundational stack for Mexican Minnesota, the Guatemalan civil war (1960–1996) and the 1980s scorched-earth campaigns against Maya communities are the foundational political event of much of Guatemalan Minnesota. That is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not an icebreaker. Do not ask a person to narrate massacre for your professional development.

### Foundational events

Later streams carry gang and state violence, family reunification, and ordinary work migration into food processing and dairy. Plant and dairy towns in southern and western Minnesota built households that a Twin Cities default will miss. Nearly half of Guatemalan Minnesota is Greater Minnesota. That is not a metro leftover.

### Who you meet

The desk in 2026 does not only meet a 1980s arrival. It meets U.S.-born children translating for parents, mixed-status households, and a Mam speaker who has been in a plant town for years and still cannot get Mam in the lobby. If you only know “immigrant,” you will miss them. If you only know “Mexican labor,” you will mash them.

Enforcement is current structure. When raids or rumored raids spike, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

### Who is in the household

Mixed-status is structure. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names, a grandmother as caregiver, or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

### Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English — or the only Spanish. That child is not the qualified interpreter. If the home language is K’iche’ or Mam, a Spanish-speaking child is still a closed door. CLAS still stands. Using a child as the go-between is a harm: it reverses respeto, it leaks adult business, and it is not language access.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

### Places

Places, not a blob: plant and dairy towns in southern and western Minnesota; Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea; metro pockets. Markets are public life. They are not consultation. A food visit does not make you the expert.

### Partners

Partners: rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. CLUES is a Twin Cities door; it does not automatically reach a dairy county. Churches are often the actual safe channel. CECLC is a department door, not the whole community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Guatemalan staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A fiesta visit is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Guatemalteco / Maya — the heart of a people
paragraphs: Guatemalteco, and Maya peoplehood inside a republic. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ are peoples, not Spanish accents. Latino in a U.S. checkbox that defaults Mexican.
Do not fold this household into one Latino blob or into Mexican. Do not copy a Mexican Guadalupe sentence onto this page. Open the Latino umbrella only as adjacent.

To be Guatemalan in Minnesota is to be filed under a U.S. checkbox that defaults Mexican, and often to be a Maya person inside a republic the building has never studied. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ are peoples. Face, kin, costumbre, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### In this state

The Mexican default in this state is a count fact on another page. It is a harm on this one when staff copy Guadalupe, norteño, and “Mexican Spanish” onto a Maya household.

In the United States another fact sits on the same desk: Hispanic is ethnicity, not race. Maya people are indigenous. Colorism and ladino hierarchy are real. Do not bleach this household into a mestizo Latino story.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

Catholic, evangelical, and Pentecostal streams are all large in Guatemalan Minnesota. Maya costumbre lives in some homes and is not a souvenir. The parish or the iglesia may be the trusted channel for information, mutual aid, and a room people will enter when they will not enter yours. Our Lady of Guadalupe is Mexican Catholic literacy — do not install it as the default on this page. Ask.

### Streams

Do not make a priest, a pastor, or a traditional practitioner the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one church and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic, or Maya practice as witchcraft.

### Practice

Holy Week, funerals, and fiesta obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it. Do not photograph an altar or traje as a souvenir.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.

sections.heading: Greetings
paragraphs: Elders first. Handshake common in many rooms. Titles — Señor, Señora, Don, Doña — until invited. Usted in many Spanish rooms.
Follow this room. Do not force a first name on an elder. Do not import Somali or African American greeting rules. Say the name.

Elders first. A handshake is common in many rooms. A slight nod with an older person is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth. Follow this room.

### Titles

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it. Usted versus tú is respect in Spanish; a qualified interpreter matches register. In a Maya-language room, the interpreter matches that register. You do not correct it.

### This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
paragraphs: Two surnames: apellido paterno + apellido materno. Given names may be Spanish, Maya, English, or both. U.S. databases that keep one invent a person.
Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not drop the second surname. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.

Two surnames is the default in much of Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

### How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Given names may be Spanish, Maya, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask. Do not anglicize as a convenience.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.

paragraphs: 15 September (Central American independence). Holy Week. Maya calendar dates in some rooms — ask, do not invent as universal. Not Cinco de Mayo. Not Guadalupe as the default.
A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.

15 September — independence with the other Central American republics. Literacy for the desk. Not Mexican 16 September. Not Cinco de Mayo. Do not put a restaurant calendar on a case note.

### Calendar

Holy Week is large in many Catholic streams. Funerals and fiesta days will not be on your state calendar. Ask. Maya calendar dates (Cholq’ij and related observances) live in some rooms — ask this family; do not invent them as universal and do not put “Maya holiday” on a file as color.

Hispanic Heritage Month is the umbrella calendar. It is not this people’s day and not consultation. A calendar click is literacy for scheduling. It is not community engagement and not a day off the work. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.

sections.heading: Education
paragraphs: Compass: ~60.8% high school or higher (25+); ~15.5% bachelor’s or higher. Foreign-born 46.7%. A Spanish IEP is not K’iche’. English IEP is still a gate.
A parent who speaks fluent Mam and limited English — or limited Spanish — is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Guatemalan Minnesotans 25 and older, about 60.8 percent high school or higher; about 15.5 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 46.7 percent of the community is foreign-born. A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent K’iche’ or Mam and limited English — or limited Spanish — is not illiterate. A Spanish IEP is not a Maya-language IEP. The English-only form is the gate. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus poverty plus enforcement fear plus a school that never learned the second surname. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.

sections.heading: Etiquette
paragraphs: Elders first. Hospitality. Titles. Traje and altars in some homes. Do not photograph ritual objects.
Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Do not use a child as the go-between. Do not ask an elder to model traje for Heritage Month.

Elders first. Titles. Accept a little food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not walk into a living room and photograph an altar or traje. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain “your culture” as entertainment, or to model a huipil for Heritage Month. Shoes: follow the household.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Plant shifts and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter — Spanish if that is the language, K’iche’ or Mam if that is the language.

community.title: Guatemalan Minnesota

chapters.body:
This brief is about Guatemalan Minnesota as a people — guatemalteco, guatemalteca — and as Maya nations inside a republic, not as a Mexican variant and not as the Latino / Hispanic umbrella. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Kaqchikel and other Mayan languages are in this state. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. This is not Mexican. It is not Salvadoran. It is not Puerto Rican. Shared Spanish is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is

Open the Latino umbrella only as adjacent. That page is the mash and the CLAS Spanish line. This page is Guatemalan. If you leave this door and file the household under “Latino” or under Mexican because that is the Minnesota default, you have left this door.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts the Guatemalan cultural community at 17,172. Twin Cities 53.5 percent; Greater Minnesota 46.5 percent — nearly half. About 47.3 percent age 17 or younger. Compass suppresses 65+ in this vintage — do not invent it. Foreign-born 46.7 percent. Language other than English (age 5+) 58.8 percent; English less than “very well” 33.7 percent. Date the number you use. Compass does not count K’iche’ or Mam speakers. Do not invent that count. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A K’iche’-speaking mother in a plant town who does not use Spanish as a home language, a Mam dairy worker, a ladino Spanish-speaking professional in the Cities, a U.S.-born child in an English school, an evangelical grandmother, a person who left the highlands in the 1980s and still will not open the door to a badge — share a passport word and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Guatemalan peoplehood is not a Mexican origin story with different mountains. Maya nations — K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, Kaqchikel, and others — are older than the Spanish colony and older than the republic. The republic is Spanish-language, ladino-dominated, and has both claimed and hunted those nations. Minnesota’s community includes Maya households and ladino Spanish-speaking households. Ask. Do not lecture a Willmar family about taxonomy they did not ask for.

### History for the meeting

Spanish colonial rule, Catholic mission, independence with the other Central American republics (15 September 1821), a nineteenth- and twentieth-century plantation state, and the civil war that followed — that is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a huipil, a volcano postcard, or a Heritage Month sentence.

### What people brought

Writing in Spanish is the state’s public literacy. Mayan languages are languages, not dialects of Spanish. Some people read Spanish. Some do not. Some U.S.-born adults do not read Spanish either. Oral skill is not print. Some Maya literacy is oral and in a language the building has never put on an interpreter line.

What people brought: language (Spanish varieties and Mayan languages), kinship, costumbre and later evangelical church, farm skill, a memory of a state that used them and of villages that were emptied. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Latino” checkbox, often one interpreter labeled Spanish, and a plant town that had not studied Mam.

chapters.practitioner: History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a textile tourism sentence.
chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
Homeland is not one flag on a classroom map. Highlands, coast, Petén; K’iche’ country, Mam country, Q’eqchi’ country — geographies that do not match the republic’s departments as the person in the lobby may name them. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee Quetzaltenango versus San Marcos in a waiver meeting. Listen.

### Homeland

The U.S. Guatemalan map includes California and also the Upper Midwest plant and dairy belt that a Minneapolis default still treats as leftover. Compass: 53.5 percent Twin Cities, 46.5 percent Greater Minnesota. Nearly half. Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea, and dairy counties are names you should be able to hold without turning them into a tour.

### Minnesota

Metro pockets exist. They are not the whole. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Guatemala. A Greater Minnesota household is still this people. Open rural literacy beside this page when place is the gate.

chapters.title: The Geography of the Guatemalan World

chapters.body:
If IRCA-era settlement is a foundational stack for Mexican Minnesota, the Guatemalan civil war (1960–1996) and the 1980s scorched-earth campaigns against Maya communities are the foundational political event of much of Guatemalan Minnesota. That is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not an icebreaker. Do not ask a person to narrate massacre for your professional development.

### Foundational events

Later streams carry gang and state violence, family reunification, and ordinary work migration into food processing and dairy. Plant and dairy towns in southern and western Minnesota built households that a Twin Cities default will miss. Nearly half of Guatemalan Minnesota is Greater Minnesota. That is not a metro leftover.

### Who you meet

The desk in 2026 does not only meet a 1980s arrival. It meets U.S.-born children translating for parents, mixed-status households, and a Mam speaker who has been in a plant town for years and still cannot get Mam in the lobby. If you only know “immigrant,” you will miss them. If you only know “Mexican labor,” you will mash them.

Enforcement is current structure. When raids or rumored raids spike, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Family is often larger than a nuclear English form. Compass: average household size about 3.51. Elders, in-laws, adult children, padrinos, and cousins who are household in practice sit in the same week. Who cares for the child may not match the waiver checkbox. Ask who should be in the room.

### Who is in the household

Mixed-status is structure. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat unmatched last names, a grandmother as caregiver, or a missing SSN as fraud until you have a reason. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

### Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English — or the only Spanish. That child is not the qualified interpreter. If the home language is K’iche’ or Mam, a Spanish-speaking child is still a closed door. CLAS still stands. Using a child as the go-between is a harm: it reverses respeto, it leaks adult business, and it is not language access.

Minnesota law still stands. Domestic violence is not culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Minnesota holds a Guatemalan community large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment — and nearly half of it is Greater Minnesota. Compass: 17,172 (ACS 2019–2023); 46.5 percent Greater Minnesota. Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote.

### Places

Places, not a blob: plant and dairy towns in southern and western Minnesota; Worthington, Willmar, Austin, Albert Lea; metro pockets. Markets are public life. They are not consultation. A food visit does not make you the expert.

### Partners

Partners: rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. CLUES is a Twin Cities door; it does not automatically reach a dairy county. Churches are often the actual safe channel. CECLC is a department door, not the whole community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Guatemalan staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. A fiesta visit is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

chapters.title: Minnesota and Guatemalan History

chapters.body:
To be Guatemalan in Minnesota is to be filed under a U.S. checkbox that defaults Mexican, and often to be a Maya person inside a republic the building has never studied. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ are peoples. Face, kin, costumbre, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### In this state

The Mexican default in this state is a count fact on another page. It is a harm on this one when staff copy Guadalupe, norteño, and “Mexican Spanish” onto a Maya household.

In the United States another fact sits on the same desk: Hispanic is ethnicity, not race. Maya people are indigenous. Colorism and ladino hierarchy are real. Do not bleach this household into a mestizo Latino story.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

### Costumbre

### War memory

Foundational for much of this Minnesota community. Not a personality for the person in the lobby. Not an icebreaker.

### Familismo and two surnames

Hypotheses you still test. The database that keeps one surname invents a person.

### Plant-town settlement

Greater Minnesota 46.5 percent. Work and school as a family project in a county the St. Paul meeting will not reach.

chapters.title: Core Concepts

chapters.body:
Catholic, evangelical, and Pentecostal streams are all large in Guatemalan Minnesota. Maya costumbre lives in some homes and is not a souvenir. The parish or the iglesia may be the trusted channel for information, mutual aid, and a room people will enter when they will not enter yours. Our Lady of Guadalupe is Mexican Catholic literacy — do not install it as the default on this page. Ask.

### Streams

Do not make a priest, a pastor, or a traditional practitioner the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one church and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic, or Maya practice as witchcraft.

### Practice

Holy Week, funerals, and fiesta obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it. Do not photograph an altar or traje as a souvenir.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.
chapters.evidence: Catholic, evangelical and Pentecostal large, Maya costumbre in some homes. Parish or iglesia may be the trusted channel. Not Guadalupe as the default — that is Mexican literacy.
chapters.practitioner: Do not make clergy the case plan unless this family asked. Do not treat Maya practice as folklore or as witchcraft. Ask.
chapters.title: Religion

chapters.body:
Elders first. A handshake is common in many rooms. A slight nod with an older person is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth. Follow this room.

### Titles

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it. Usted versus tú is respect in Spanish; a qualified interpreter matches register. In a Maya-language room, the interpreter matches that register. You do not correct it.

### This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.
chapters.evidence: Elders first. Handshake common in many rooms. Titles — Señor, Señora, Don, Doña — until invited. Usted in many Spanish rooms.
chapters.practitioner: Follow this room. Do not force a first name on an elder. Do not import Somali or African American greeting rules. Say the name.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

### How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Given names may be Spanish, Maya, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask. Do not anglicize as a convenience.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.
chapters.evidence: Two surnames: apellido paterno + apellido materno. Given names may be Spanish, Maya, English, or both. U.S. databases that keep one invent a person.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not drop the second surname. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
15 September — independence with the other Central American republics. Literacy for the desk. Not Mexican 16 September. Not Cinco de Mayo. Do not put a restaurant calendar on a case note.

### Calendar

Holy Week is large in many Catholic streams. Funerals and fiesta days will not be on your state calendar. Ask. Maya calendar dates (Cholq’ij and related observances) live in some rooms — ask this family; do not invent them as universal and do not put “Maya holiday” on a file as color.

Hispanic Heritage Month is the umbrella calendar. It is not this people’s day and not consultation. A calendar click is literacy for scheduling. It is not community engagement and not a day off the work. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.
chapters.evidence: 15 September (Central American independence). Holy Week. Maya calendar dates in some rooms — ask, do not invent as universal. Not Cinco de Mayo. Not Guadalupe as the default.
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.
chapters.title: Dates of Significance

chapters.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Guatemalan Minnesotans 25 and older, about 60.8 percent high school or higher; about 15.5 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 46.7 percent of the community is foreign-born. A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent K’iche’ or Mam and limited English — or limited Spanish — is not illiterate. A Spanish IEP is not a Maya-language IEP. The English-only form is the gate. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus poverty plus enforcement fear plus a school that never learned the second surname. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Compass: ~60.8% high school or higher (25+); ~15.5% bachelor’s or higher. Foreign-born 46.7%. A Spanish IEP is not K’iche’. English IEP is still a gate.
chapters.practitioner: A parent who speaks fluent Mam and limited English — or limited Spanish — is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Do not use a child as interpreter.
chapters.title: Education

chapters.body:
Elders first. Titles. Accept a little food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not walk into a living room and photograph an altar or traje. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain “your culture” as entertainment, or to model a huipil for Heritage Month. Shoes: follow the household.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Plant shifts and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter — Spanish if that is the language, K’iche’ or Mam if that is the language.
chapters.evidence: Elders first. Hospitality. Titles. Traje and altars in some homes. Do not photograph ritual objects.
chapters.practitioner: Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Do not use a child as the go-between. Do not ask an elder to model traje for Heritage Month.
chapters.title: Etiquette

chapters.body:
This is the CLAS gate that the Mexican default will miss. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ and other Mayan languages are in this state. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Name the language on the request. A scarce interpreter is a gate, not an excuse to proceed in English only without recording the failure. Compass does not count Mayan speakers. Do not invent that count.

### Language

Guatemalan Spanish is not Mexican Spanish and not one interpreter accent test. Book a qualified Spanish interpreter AND ask this household. Register matters: usted, not a buddy tú, until the room says otherwise.

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 58.8 percent speak a language other than English; about 33.7 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed: oral skill is not print.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan. Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Guatemalan coworker the interpreter.
chapters.evidence: K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’, other Mayan languages. Guatemalan Spanish is not Mexican Spanish. Compass: ~58.8% language other than English (5+); ~33.7% LEP. Compass does not count Mayan speakers.
chapters.practitioner: Book qualified Spanish AND ask. If K’iche’ or Mam is the home language, a Spanish interpreter is a closed door. Do not use a child. Do not take a smile as consent.
chapters.title: Language and Communication

chapters.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

ICE and enforcement climate is structure. Mixed-status households skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate.

Maya erasure under “they all speak Spanish” is a named harm. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Colorism and ladino hierarchy are real. The Mexican default in this state will talk over this household if you let the umbrella page do this page’s job.

Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. You still see a family.

LGBTQ Guatemalan Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it familismo. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.
chapters.evidence: ICE/enforcement climate; mixed status; Maya erasure under they-all-speak-Spanish; colorism; Mexican default as a Minnesota harm; LGBTQ people exist; domestic violence is not culture.
chapters.practitioner: Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Do not collect status you do not need.
chapters.title: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice

chapters.body:
Believe reported pain. Do not invent stoicism. War and flight trauma sit in some rooms. They are not a personality. They are not a reason to skip screening. They are a reason a government badge is not automatically help. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic immigrant-mistrust slide.

### Access

Uninsured and delayed-care patterns sit here. Date Minnesota figures when you have them. Do not invent a rate. Compass poverty (ACS 2019–2023) is 13.6 percent — a poverty figure, not an uninsured rate. Disability 4.9 percent — date it. Do not invent a 65+ rate; Compass suppresses it in this vintage.

Fear of the lobby is a health access fact. A badge, a form that asks for SSN, a child called to interpret a diagnosis, an interpreter who does not speak this Spanish or this Mam — these are clinical events. When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic. That is not noncompliance.

Traditional healing and parish prayer can sit next to a fierce wish for biomedicine. If they name a healer, listen. Do not make the healer the case plan unless they asked. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Do not use a child as interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Believe reported pain. War trauma in some rooms is not a personality. Uninsured and delayed-care patterns — date MN figures when you have them; do not invent a rate. Fear of the lobby is a health access fact.
chapters.practitioner: Do not skip screening. Gender match if they want it. If they name a healer, listen. Do not use a child as interpreter. Peers who share language.
chapters.title: Health

chapters.body:
Queer and trans Guatemalan Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, parish, and evangelical climates can mean silence or exile. Maya queer people exist. Some people live a public English life and a private K’iche’ or Spanish life. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a family-values exhibit. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.

Face and parish climate do not get a veto over this person. Always defer to the person in front of you.
chapters.evidence: Queer and trans Guatemalan Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, parish, and evangelical climates can mean silence. Maya queer people exist.
chapters.practitioner: Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture.
chapters.title: LGBTQ

chapters.body:
Traje and huipil are public at fiesta and ceremony in some rooms. They are not a daily uniform and not yours to request for a Heritage Month photo. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

Colorism is real. Ladino default beauty is a hierarchy. Name it if it is in the room. Do not rank indigeneity off clothing. Do not touch.

Plant and dairy work may mean stained hands. That is labor. It is not a joke and not a race trait. Quinceañera dress, baptism white, evangelical modesty — celebration and devotion, not a case note.
chapters.evidence: Traje and huipil are public at fiesta and ceremony, not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Colorism is real.
chapters.practitioner: Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch. Do not rank indigeneity off clothing.
chapters.title: Hair, Dress, and Body

chapters.body:
Marimba, church music, later pop. Named variation, not a playlist. A Mexican mariachi default in this waiting room is the mash in speakers.

### Variation

A festival stage is not engagement. A playlist is not language access. Church music is not staff entertainment.

Knowing that music is public life will not write the waiver. It will stop you from treating one Heritage Month speaker as the community.
chapters.evidence: Marimba, church music, later pop. Not mariachi as the default. Named variation, not a playlist.
chapters.practitioner: A playlist is not engagement. A Mexican default playlist in this waiting room is the mash.
chapters.title: Music

chapters.body:
Fútbol is common public sport. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

### Not the whole person

Leagues and pickup games are social infrastructure in plant towns. They are not language access and not a case plan. Greater Minnesota teams are still this people.

A Saturday tournament does not replace a Mam interpreter on Monday.
chapters.evidence: Fútbol is common public sport. Ordinary school sport in the second generation.
chapters.practitioner: Do not assume the kid plays. Sport clubs are not language access.
chapters.title: Sports

chapters.body:
Maya oral literature is older than the Spanish file and is not “no letters.” Spanish-language letters exist. That fact does not mean the person in the lobby can read your form — in English or in Spanish. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed.

### Literacy in the lobby

Rigoberta Menchú is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family and not a quote for a case note. You do not need to quote a testimonio in the lobby. You need the language this person hears.

Print Spanish from Mexico or a machine translation is not automatically this household’s Spanish, and Spanish is not K’iche’. CLAS is qualified language, not Google and not a child.
chapters.evidence: Maya oral literature is older than the Spanish file. Spanish letters exist. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed.
chapters.practitioner: You do not need to quote Menchú. You need the language this person hears. History is literacy for the desk, not a speech.
chapters.title: Literature

chapters.body:
Traje, huipil, and weaving are art and memory, not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table. Plant-town public life is not a West Side mural tour copied over from Mexican Minnesota.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. Do not photograph traje or an altar because it is pretty. A textile is not a case plan. A market visit is not consultation.

Heritage Month that mashes this with mariachi or a Mexican ofrenda has already mashed the adjacent peoples.
chapters.evidence: Traje, huipil, weaving as art and memory. Not a mascot. Plant-town public life is not a mural tour.
chapters.practitioner: Guest, not researcher. Do not photograph traje as a souvenir. A textile is not a case plan.
chapters.title: Art

chapters.body:
The civil war (1960–1996) and the 1980s campaigns against Maya communities are the political event. Historical-record bodies named genocide; you do not need to litigate that in a waiver meeting. You need to know why a badge is not automatically help. Later: ordinary policing, and deportation of people with records. That is current structure.

### The badge

Do not use the war as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate dying, crossing, or a village emptying for your professional development. Intra-community ladino and Maya difference is real. You do not referee it on a case note as color.

When enforcement spikes, people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a deportation score.
chapters.evidence: Civil war 1960–1996; 1980s Maya genocide as historical-record literacy; later enforcement. A DHS badge is not automatically help.
chapters.practitioner: Do not use the war as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate massacre for your professional development. Do not collect status you do not need.
chapters.title: War, the State, and Deportation Climate

chapters.body:
Food processing, dairy, agriculture, construction, service, professional second generation, public employment. Rural plants can sit next to a metro cousin. A small-business owner and a waiver recipient may be the same household.

### Work

Worker centers and parishes may be the trusted channel in Greater Minnesota. Name the local one. Do not assume Minneapolis. Do not assume CLUES reaches a dairy county. Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice.

### Staff

Guatemalan staff exist inside DHS and counties. They are not unpaid interpreters, not the K’iche’ or Mam pool, and not “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan. Do not make a Guatemalan colleague your unpaid tutor.

Remittance to kin in Guatemala is obligation for many, not a disposable luxury. A budget that treats it as optional has already chosen a household type.
chapters.evidence: Food processing, dairy, agriculture, service, professional second generation. Worker centers and parishes in Greater Minnesota. Guatemalan staff in government.
chapters.practitioner: Guatemalan employees are not unpaid interpreters and not the Maya-language pool. Name the local worker center — do not assume Minneapolis.
chapters.title: Work, Markets, and Government

chapters.body:
Language including Mayan. Book qualified Spanish AND ask. Confirm K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ when that is the home language. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Do not use a child as interpreter. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### Language

Who is in the room. Gender match in maternal and intimate care if they want it. Titles. Two surnames. SSN on the first screen: if you do not need it, do not demand it as theater. Mixed-status: do not collect status you do not need. Enforcement climate: skipped appointments are pattern.

### The meeting

Believe reported pain. Do not skip screening. If they name a healer or a church, listen. Do not make either the case plan unless they asked. Mandated reporting still exists. Rural access is a gate: distance, clinic hours, one interpreter contracted from the Cities who does not speak this language. Greater Minnesota 46.5 percent is not an afterthought.
chapters.evidence: K’iche’/Mam; Spanish variety; two surnames; child as interpreter; SSN on first screen; mixed-status; enforcement climate; rural access.
chapters.practitioner: Book qualified Spanish AND ask. Confirm the Mayan language. Do not use a child. Believe reported pain. Do not collect status you do not need.
chapters.title: Health-care and Human-service Encounters

chapters.body:
Not Mexican. Not Salvadoran. Not Puerto Rican. Not the Latino / Hispanic umbrella. Open that CI as adjacent — CLAS Spanish, the mash, the other origins as a list. This page is Guatemalan. Do not file this household under “Latino” or under Mexican and call it done.

### Adjacent doors

Not K’iche’, Mam, or Q’eqchi’ as dialects of Spanish. Those are languages and peoples. A Spanish interpreter is not those languages. Not Honduran. Not Nicaraguan. Not Ecuadorian. Name the origin.

Not Somali. Not historic African American. Afro-Guatemalan and Garifuna people exist in the wider Central American map — ask, do not mash, and do not invent a Minnesota count Compass does not have. Never one Latino module.
chapters.evidence: Not Mexican. Not Salvadoran. Not Puerto Rican. Not the Latino umbrella. Not K’iche’ as a Spanish dialect. Open the Latino CI only as adjacent.
chapters.practitioner: Never one Latino module. Open this for Guatemalan. Ask this household.
chapters.title: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash

chapters.body:
Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Guatemalan cultural community: 17,172; Twin Cities 53.5 percent; Greater Minnesota 46.5 percent (nearly half); age 17 or younger 47.3 percent; 65+ suppressed — do not invent it; foreign-born 46.7 percent; language other than English (age 5+) 58.8 percent; English less than “very well” 33.7 percent; high school or higher (25+) 60.8 percent; bachelor’s or higher 15.5 percent; median household income about $55,927; poverty 13.6 percent; owner-occupied 47.1 percent; average household size 3.51; disability 4.9 percent.

### Counts

K’iche’, Mam, other Mayan languages may be in the home. Compass does not count speakers. Do not invent that count. Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions. Date the number you cite.

### What the count is not

A young age structure is not a personality. Language and child-as-interpreter are gates. Greater Minnesota 46.5 percent is not an afterthought. A rate is not the person.
chapters.evidence: Compass ACS 2019–2023: 17,172; 53.5% metro; 46.5% Greater MN; 47.3% 17 or younger; 65+ suppressed; foreign-born 46.7%; LEP 33.7%; poverty 13.6%; owner 47.1%. No K’iche’ speaker count. Date them. Do not invent a rate.
chapters.practitioner: A rate is not the person. Greater MN nearly half is not an afterthought. Language is the gate.
chapters.title: Counts, Dated

chapters.body:
Minnesota Compass Guatemalan profile (ACS 2019–2023) — https://www.mncompass.org/topics/demographics/cultural-communities/guatemalan. Date the retrieval. Rural parish and worker centers — name the local one; do not assume Minneapolis. The parish in a dairy county may be the actual door. CLUES — https://clues.org/ — Twin Cities services, not automatic reach into Greater Minnesota.

### Public doors

CECLC is a department door, not the whole community. Open the Latino umbrella CI as adjacent, not as this page. Open Mexican, Salvadoran, Puerto Rican when that is the household. Open a K’iche’ or Mam interpreter request when Spanish is the wrong door.

### Learn on your own time

Learn on your own time. Do not make a Guatemalan colleague your unpaid tutor. Do not BCC a metro org and call it consultation for a plant town. Pay partners. Report back. Hispanic Heritage Month is not the work.
chapters.evidence: Compass Guatemalan profile ACS 2019–2023. Rural parish and worker centers. CLUES is metro — not automatic reach. CECLC is a door, not the community. Open Latino umbrella only as adjacent.
chapters.practitioner: Learn on your own time. Do not make a Guatemalan colleague your unpaid tutor. Pay partners. Name the local one.
chapters.title: Doors and Sources

chapters.body:
Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: CLAS Spanish is not one Spanish. K’iche’, Mam, Q’eqchi’ and other Mayan languages are in this state. A Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door. Still book a qualified interpreter. Name the language. Do not use a child. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: two surnames. The database that keeps one invents a person. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.

Hour caps, exception processes, SSN on the first screen, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral. Mixed-status households will bounce if the first field feels like enforcement. Do not collect status you do not need.

Child welfare and disability: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score. Domestic violence is not culture. You follow law.

Enforcement climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 46.5 percent — a St. Paul meeting is not the whole channel.

Workforce: Guatemalan staff are not the interpreter pool, not the Maya-language pool, and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  them.

Latino mash: opening Mexican, or the umbrella, because the checkbox says Hispanic is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned that a Spanish interpreter can still be a closed door.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
paragraphs: Indian (Asian Indian) Minnesota. Not Native American. Not the Eleven Tribal Nations. Compass ACS 2019–2023: 51,909. Hindi, Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Malayalam, English, others. Census Asian mixes this with Chinese, Hmong, Vietnamese. Date the number you cite.
There is no single Indian client. Defer to this family. Do not open a Tribal Nation or a Native American case with this page. Book THIS language. Pronounce the name.

This brief is about Indian (Asian Indian) Minnesota as a people of India and of a global diaspora — many languages, many religions, many states — and as a Minnesota community Compass counts near 51,909 (ACS 2019–2023). This is not Native American. This is not the Eleven Tribal Nations. The U.S. word “Indian” is already a mash. If the household is a Tribal Nation, open that CI. If Asian Indian, this page. Do not guess from the word.

### Who this is

### History for the meeting

A line that still sits in some Minnesota rooms as family memory and in others as a history class. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not an icebreaker. Not Pakistani. Not Bangladeshi. Not Sri Lankan as a synonym. Not Nepali. Not Chinese. Not Hmong. Not Vietnamese. Not Korean. Not “Asian American” as the file. Some households are mixed. Some people name South Asian. Ask this household. Do not file them under Hindi by default.

Never one Asian module. Never one “Indian” interpreter. Never a Tribal consultation checklist on this desk because the checkbox said Indian.

community.title: Indian (Asian Indian) Minnesota

chapters.body:
This brief is about Indian (Asian Indian) Minnesota as a people of India and of a global diaspora — many languages, many religions, many states — and as a Minnesota community Compass counts near 51,909 (ACS 2019–2023). This is not Native American. This is not the Eleven Tribal Nations. The U.S. word “Indian” is already a mash. If the household is a Tribal Nation, open that CI. If Asian Indian, this page. Do not guess from the word.

### Who this is

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Chinese. It is not Hmong. It is not Pakistani as a synonym. It is not one Hindi. Shared continent is not shared culture. Diwali is not Chinese New Year as a file and not Hmong New Year. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 51,909; Twin Cities 89.7 percent; Greater Minnesota 10.3 percent; age 17 or younger 27.8 percent; 65+ about 3.9 percent; foreign-born 66.1 percent; among those 5 and older, English only about 29.8 percent, language other than English about 70.2 percent, English less than “very well” about 12.3 percent; high school or higher (25+) about 95.9 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 80.3 percent; median household income about $124,931 in 2022 dollars; poverty 5.4 percent; owner-occupied 58.1 percent; average household size about 2.55; individuals living alone about 27.2 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Telugu-speaking H-1B household in Eden Prairie, a Gujarati shop family, a Malayalam Christian nurse, a Punjabi Sikh elder who needs an interpreter, a Tamil grandmother who does not read the English IEP, a U.S.-born college student, a Muslim family that will not share a Tuesday with a Hindutva uncle, a person who left India and still shows up at Diwali — share a Compass row and do not share a language, a religion, or a politics.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

chapters.practitioner: There is no single Indian client. Defer to this family. Do not open a Tribal Nation or a Native American case with this page. Book THIS language. Pronounce the name.
chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Indian peoplehood is older than the British Raj, older than 1947, and older than the H-1B file. Named kingdoms, a modern republic, many languages with their own scripts, and religions that are not interchangeable — Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Christian, Jain, Buddhist, none — are literacy for the desk. They are not a lecture you give a parent who came in for a waiver.

### History for the meeting

1947 Partition of British India into India and Pakistan is the modern political break. Millions moved. Mass violence. A line that still sits in some Minnesota rooms as family memory and in others as a history class. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not an icebreaker. Bangladesh 1971 is a neighboring story. Do not mash.

### What people brought

Writing is not one script. Devanagari, Tamil, Telugu, Gujarati, Malayalam, Gurmukhi, Bengali, Kannada, Arabic-based Urdu, English. Many elders read a script that is not Hindi. Some do not read any of them. Second generation may not read the language of home at all. A notice in the wrong script is a closed door.

What people brought: a language that may not be Hindi, a religion that may not be Hindu, family obligation, education as mobility and as pressure, foodways that are not one curry, a memory of a state and of a village. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, a U.S. word already used for Native nations, and often one interpreter labeled “Indian” or “Hindi.”
chapters.evidence: Indian peoplehood older than 1947 and older than the H-1B file. Many languages, many religions, named kingdoms and a modern republic. Partition 1947 is literacy, not a speech.
chapters.practitioner: History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a curry tourism sentence.
chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
India is not one region. North, south, east, west, and the states people name — Kerala, Gujarat, Andhra, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, Punjab, Maharashtra, Bengal, Karnataka, and others — shift language, food, and sometimes the script on the notice. Do not referee Delhi versus Chennai in a waiver meeting. Listen if they name a place.

### Homeland

The diaspora is global: California, New Jersey, Texas, New York, the Gulf, East Africa, the United Kingdom, Canada, and Minnesota. Eden Prairie is not this map. Secondary migration, university, and employer transfer built part of what you will meet here.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities suburbs — Eden Prairie, Plymouth, Eagan, Maple Grove among the named concentrations — Minneapolis, and a real Greater Minnesota 10.3 percent. Do not assume the professional corridor is the whole. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to India. Do not mash this geography with Native nations, reservations, or urban Indian organizations. Those are another CI.
chapters.evidence: India — north, south, east, west, and the states people name. Diaspora in California, New Jersey, Texas, Minnesota, the Gulf, East Africa, the UK. Compass: 89.7% Twin Cities, 10.3% Greater Minnesota.
chapters.practitioner: Do not assume Eden Prairie. Do not assume they have been to India. Greater Minnesota share is real. Do not mash with Native American geography.
chapters.title: The Geography of the Indian World

chapters.body:
Hart-Celler (1965) opened skilled and family immigration that rebuilt Asian Indian America after earlier exclusion. Later decades brought students, physicians, engineers, and H-1B / L-1 employer streams that are large in this state. That is a stream, not a virtue ranking, and not the whole community.

### Foundational events

Earlier U.S. streams — Punjabi farm and railroad labor on the West Coast, a small pre-1965 professional presence — are literacy. Minnesota’s visible community is largely post-1965 and post-1990s tech and health. India Association of Minnesota dates to 1973. Family reunification brought parents. Those parents are often the LEP elders inside a 12.3 percent that a room that treats everyone the same will round to zero.

### Who you meet

1947 is the political event of the subcontinent. It is not this person’s personality. Visa status, H-1B dependency, and green-card wait times change who opens the door. That is current structure. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

If you only know “IT,” you will miss the restaurant household, the student, the U.S.-born child, and the grandmother who still cannot get Telugu in the lobby.
chapters.evidence: Hart-Celler 1965; later H-1B, L-1, family reunification, students, and earlier railroad and farm streams elsewhere in the U.S. 1947 Partition is the political break of the subcontinent. Minnesota’s large professional stream is a stream, not the whole.
chapters.practitioner: If you only know “IT,” you will miss the LEP elder, the restaurant household, the student, and the U.S.-born child still translating for a grandmother.
chapters.title: 1965, H-1B, and Earlier Streams — Foundational Events

chapters.body:
Filial obligation is a hypothesis, not a personality. Elders often speak first. Adult children may be in the same week as a waiver meeting, a shift, and a school conference. Compass: average household size about 2.55. About 27.2 percent live alone. Joint family and nuclear English form both live here. Ask who should be in the room.

### Who is in the household

Who cares for a disabled adult or a child may be a son, a daughter-in-law, a sibling, not the legally recognized caregiver on the checkbox. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

### Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English. That child is not the qualified interpreter. Using a child as the go-between is a closed door and a harm. Book the interpreter. Ask who should be in the room.

Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. In-law duty and who holds the child’s medical decision may not match the English form. Ask.
chapters.evidence: Filial obligation as hypothesis; elders; joint and nuclear both. Compass average household size about 2.55; 27.2% live alone. Who speaks may be a child — that is a gate.
chapters.practitioner: Ask who should be in the room. Do not use a child as interpreter. A nuclear English form already has a who. Do not dump care onto a daughter-in-law and call it culture.
chapters.title: Family

chapters.body:
Minnesota holds an Asian Indian community large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, student households, and employment. Compass: about 51,909 (ACS 2019–2023). Twin Cities 89.7 percent. Greater Minnesota 10.3 percent is not an afterthought. Do not write this people as an Eden Prairie anecdote.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Eden Prairie, Plymouth, Eagan, Maple Grove, Minneapolis, university areas, and Greater Minnesota towns with work and housing. Groceries, temples, gurdwaras, masjids, and restaurants are public life. They are not consultation. A food-court visit does not make you the expert.

### Partners

Partners: India Association of Minnesota, founded 1973; temples, gurdwaras, masjids, and churches this household names. CECLC is a department door — not the whole community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Indian staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. Diwali is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.
chapters.evidence: Twin Cities suburbs including Eden Prairie, Plymouth, Eagan, Maple Grove; Minneapolis; Greater Minnesota 10.3%. India Association of Minnesota (est. 1973). Temples, gurdwaras, masjids, churches families name.
chapters.practitioner: Partners, not a harvest list. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  Indian staff. Guest at Diwali if invited. A grocery visit does not make you the expert.
chapters.title: Minnesota and Indian History

chapters.body:
To be Indian in Minnesota is often to be asked whether you speak Hindi, whether you are Hindu, and whether you are “from India,” as if those were one room — and to be filed under a U.S. word, “Indian,” that this country already uses for Native nations this household is not, and under an Asian checkbox that also holds Chinese, Hmong, and Korean histories they do not share.

### In this state

Hindi is not the language. Hindu is not the religion. Patel is not the name. Face, family reputation, and not shaming the name travel into some waiver meetings. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

Model-minority is a weapon in this building. 80.3 percent bachelor’s and a median near $124,931 will be used to skip 12.3 percent LEP, 5.4 percent poverty, disability, caste harm, and the elder who does not read the IEP. That skip is the policy.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.
chapters.evidence: Not one language. Not one religion. Asian in a U.S. checkbox that also holds Chinese, Hmong, and Native American histories they do not share — and a U.S. word, “Indian,” that is already a mash.
chapters.practitioner: Do not fold this household into “Asian Pacific.” Do not open the Eleven Nations CI for this family. Do not copy a Pakistani or a Chinese sentence onto this page.
chapters.title: Not one language, not one religion — the heart of a people

chapters.body:
Language is the first grammar. Hindi is not the default. Telugu, Tamil, Gujarati, Malayalam, Punjabi, Urdu, Kannada, Bengali, Marathi, English. Book THIS language.

### Religion is not Hindu by default

Hindu, Muslim, Sikh, Christian, Jain, none. Do not make clergy the case plan unless they asked.

### Name

Regional surnames, South Indian patronymics, Singh / Kaur. Ask. Do not correct.

### Model-minority

A weapon that hides LEP elders, 5.4 percent poverty, disability, and youth who are not thriving.

### Caste

A named harm in some rooms. Not an icebreaker. Not a field you collect because you are curious.

### Face and education pressure

Hypotheses. Not this teenager.
