chapters.title: Core Concepts

chapters.body:
Catholic and a large evangelical / Pentecostal stream both live in Salvadoran Minnesota. The parish or the iglesia may be the trusted channel for information, mutual aid, and a room people will enter when they will not enter yours. Romero is literacy for the desk — 24 March 1980 — not a piety ranking you assign in the lobby. Our Lady of Guadalupe is Mexican Catholic literacy. Do not install it as the default on this page. Ask.

### Streams

Do not make a priest or a pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Do not BCC one church and call it consultation. Do not treat evangelical growth as the evolved version of Catholic.

### Practice

Holy Week, funerals, and fiesta obligation can collide with your calendar. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it. Do not photograph an altar.

Help that looks like a report is not help. Religious framing of disability, mental health, or gender can sit next to a fierce wish for services. You can hold both.
chapters.evidence: Catholic and a large evangelical / Pentecostal stream. Romero is literacy for the desk, not a piety ranking. Parish or iglesia may be the trusted channel.
chapters.practitioner: Do not make clergy the case plan unless this family asked. Do not install Guadalupe as the default — that is Mexican literacy. Ask.
chapters.title: Religion

chapters.body:
Elders first. A handshake is common in many rooms. A slight nod with an older person is safer than a hard first-name hello you assume is warmth. Follow this room.

### Titles

Titles until invited: Señor, Señora, Don, Doña. Use the last name you were given — and remember there may be two. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it. Usted is respect with strangers and elders; voseo is ordinary among familiars. A qualified interpreter matches register. You do not correct it.

### This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.
chapters.evidence: Elders first. Handshake common. Titles — Señor, Señora, Don, Doña — until invited. Usted in many rooms; voseo among familiars.
chapters.practitioner: Follow this room. Do not force a first name on an elder. Do not import Somali or African American greeting rules. Say the name.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
Two surnames is the default in much of Salvadoran Spanish-language naming: apellido paterno then apellido materno. A U.S. database that keeps one surname invents a person. That invented name then follows them through MHCP, child welfare, and school. It is a gate.

### How to file

Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Pronounce it. Do not drop accents as a joke. Given names may be Spanish, English, or both. Some people use a middle given name as the call-name. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s surname in U.S. records. Children may carry two surnames that do not match a parent’s U.S. “last name” field. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

Do not treat unmatched last names in a household as a fraud flag by default. Do not invent a hyphen and then punish the person when the hyphen moves.
chapters.evidence: Two surnames: apellido paterno + apellido materno. U.S. databases that keep one invent a person. Given names may be Spanish, English, or both.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not drop the second surname. Unmatched last names are not fraud by default.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
15 September — independence with the other Central American republics. Literacy for the desk. Not Mexican 16 September. Not Cinco de Mayo. Do not put a restaurant calendar on a case note.

### Calendar

24 March — Romero. Literacy. Not an icebreaker. Not a day you ask a survivor to speak to staff for professional development. 16 January 1992 — Peace Accords. Holy Week. Funerals and fiesta days will not be on your state calendar. Ask.

Hispanic Heritage Month is the umbrella calendar. It is not this people’s day and not consultation. A calendar click is literacy for scheduling. It is not community engagement and not a day off the work. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.
chapters.evidence: 15 September (independence). 24 March Romero. 16 January 1992 Peace Accords. Holy Week. Not Cinco de Mayo. Not Guadalupe as the default.
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Latino holiday” on a case note.
chapters.title: Dates of Significance

chapters.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Salvadoran Minnesotans 25 and older, about 62.1 percent high school or higher; about 17.0 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 43.9 percent of the community is foreign-born. Among those 5 and older, 79.1 percent speak a language other than English; 39.0 percent speak English less than “very well.” That is a language gate, not a culture clash. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Salvadoran Spanish and limited English is not illiterate. Some elders read Spanish. Some do not. The English-only form is the gate. A Mexican-Spanish notice is not automatically this household’s Spanish. Do not use a child as interpreter.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus enforcement fear plus a school that never learned the second surname. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Compass: ~62.1% high school or higher (25+); ~17.0% bachelor’s or higher. Foreign-born 43.9%. LOTE 79.1%; LEP 39.0%. English IEP is still a gate.
chapters.practitioner: A parent who speaks fluent Salvadoran Spanish and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Do not use a child as interpreter.
chapters.title: Education

chapters.body:
Elders first. Titles. Accept a little food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not walk into a living room and photograph an altar. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain the war as entertainment. Shoes: follow the household.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Shifts and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use. Do not write a “Latino time” joke in a case note.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Elders first. Hospitality. Titles. Food. Do not photograph an altar.
chapters.practitioner: Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Do not use a child as the go-between. Relationship before the packet is not delay.
chapters.title: Etiquette

chapters.body:
Spanish is not one Spanish. Salvadoran Spanish is not Mexican Spanish. Voseo is ordinary. Book a qualified Spanish interpreter AND ask this household. A Mexican interpreter from one region can still be a closed door. Register matters: usted with elders and strangers; vos among familiars. The interpreter matches the room. You do not correct it.

### Language

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 79.1 percent speak a language other than English; about 39.0 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. This is a large language gate. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed: oral skill is not print. Compass does not split an indigenous-language count on this Salvadoran profile. Do not invent one, and do not copy Mixtec or K’iche’ onto this page unless this household names it.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Salvadoran coworker the interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Salvadoran Spanish is not Mexican Spanish. Voseo is ordinary. Compass: ~79.1% language other than English (5+); ~39.0% LEP. Compass does not split indigenous-language speakers on this profile — do not invent one.
chapters.practitioner: Book qualified Spanish AND ask. A Mexican interpreter can still be a closed door. Do not use a child. Do not take a smile as consent.
chapters.title: Language and Communication

chapters.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

ICE, TPS, and enforcement climate are structure. Mixed-status households skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved or when TPS is a clock. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need. SSN on the first screen is a gate.

The Mexican default in this state will talk over this household if you let the umbrella page do this page’s job. Spanish is not one Spanish.

Gang discourse in U.S. media — including MS-13 as a story that began among Salvadoran refugee youth in Los Angeles — is HISTORY and a named harm in enforcement. A last name is not a gang file. Do not score a Minnesota child on a cousin’s decade or a cable-news segment. Follow law. Still see a family.

Machismo is a named harm, not a joke and not “that’s culture.” Domestic violence is not culture. You follow mandated reporting. LGBTQ Salvadoran Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.
chapters.evidence: ICE/TPS/enforcement climate; mixed status; Mexican default; gang discourse as HISTORY not a last-name score; machismo as named harm; LGBTQ people exist; domestic violence is not culture.
chapters.practitioner: Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not score a child on a last name.
chapters.title: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice

chapters.body:
Believe reported pain. Do not invent stoicism. War trauma sits in some rooms. It is not a personality. It is not a reason to skip screening. It is a reason a government badge is not automatically help. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic immigrant-mistrust slide.

### Access

Uninsured and delayed-care patterns sit here. Date Minnesota figures when you have them. Do not invent a rate. Compass poverty (ACS 2019–2023) is 5.9 percent — a poverty figure, not an uninsured rate, and not proof the gates closed. Disability 3.4 percent — date it. Do not invent a 65+ rate; Compass suppresses it in this vintage.

Fear of the lobby is a health access fact. A badge, a form that asks for SSN, a child called to interpret a diagnosis, an interpreter who does not speak this Spanish — these are clinical events. When TPS is threatened or enforcement spikes, people skip clinic. That is not noncompliance.

Parish prayer and biomedicine can both be in the household. If they name a healer or a pastor, listen. Do not make either the case plan unless they asked. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Do not use a child as interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Believe reported pain. War trauma in some rooms is not a personality. Uninsured and delayed-care patterns — date MN figures when you have them; do not invent a rate. Fear of the lobby is a health access fact.
chapters.practitioner: Do not skip screening. Gender match if they want it. Do not use a child as interpreter. Peers who share language.
chapters.title: Health

chapters.body:
Queer and trans Salvadoran Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, parish, and evangelical climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private Spanish life. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a family-values exhibit. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.

Face and parish climate do not get a veto over this person. Always defer to the person in front of you.
chapters.evidence: Queer and trans Salvadoran Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, parish, and evangelical climates can mean silence.
chapters.practitioner: Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture.
chapters.title: LGBTQ

chapters.body:
There is no Salvadoran uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Fiesta dress is public at celebration, not a daily costume, and not yours to request for Heritage Month. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

Do not touch. Do not rank piety off clothing. Colorism is real inside Central American streams. Name it if it is in the room. Do not rank.

Quinceañera dress, baptism white, evangelical modesty — celebration and devotion, not a case note. Service and plant work may mean stained hands. That is labor. It is not a joke.
chapters.evidence: Not one look. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Fiesta dress is not a daily uniform.
chapters.practitioner: Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch.
chapters.title: Hair, Dress, and Body

chapters.body:
Cumbia, church music, later pop. Named variation, not a playlist. A Mexican mariachi default in this waiting room is the mash in speakers.

### Variation

A festival stage is not engagement. A playlist is not language access. Church music is not staff entertainment.

Romero commemorations are public life in some rooms. They are not consultation and not a case plan.
chapters.evidence: Cumbia, church music, later pop. Not mariachi as the default. Named variation, not a playlist.
chapters.practitioner: A playlist is not engagement. A Mexican default playlist in this waiting room is the mash.
chapters.title: Music

chapters.body:
Fútbol is common public sport. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

### Not the whole person

Leagues and pickup games are social infrastructure. They are not language access and not a case plan. Greater Minnesota teams are still this people.

A Saturday tournament does not replace an interpreter on Monday.
chapters.evidence: Fútbol is common public sport. Ordinary school sport in the second generation.
chapters.practitioner: Do not assume the kid plays. Sport clubs are not language access.
chapters.title: Sports

chapters.body:
Spanish-language letters exist. Roque Dalton is literacy for the desk, not a quote for a case note. That fact does not mean the person in the lobby can read your form — in English or in Spanish. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. Oral Spanish is not print Spanish.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do not need to quote a poet in the lobby. You need the language this person reads — or hears. Print Spanish from Mexico or a machine translation is not automatically this household’s Spanish.

CLAS is qualified language, not Google and not a child.
chapters.evidence: Spanish-language letters exist. Literacy in any language is not guaranteed. Oral Spanish is not print Spanish.
chapters.practitioner: You do not need to quote Dalton. You need the language this person reads.
chapters.title: Literature

chapters.body:
Public culture of markets, church, and fiesta. Pupusas are foodway, not consultation. Guest, not researcher. A food visit is not a case plan. Do not photograph an altar.

### Guest

Heritage Month that mashes this with mariachi or a Guatemalan huipil has already mashed the adjacent peoples.

chapters.body:
This brief is about Thai people as a people of Thailand — the lowland state history, Theravada wats, a language related to Lao and not interchangeable with it — and as a Minnesota community Compass counts near 6,738 (ACS 2019–2023). This is not Hmong. This is not Lao. Camps in Thailand — Ban Vinai, Mae La, and others — held Hmong and Karen families after wars this people did not fight as those files. Do not file a Thai household under that war. If the household is Hmong, open Hmong Minnesota. If Lao, open Lao Minnesota. If Thai, book Thai.

### Who this is

This is not a Census “Asian” mash. It is not Khmer. It is not Vietnamese. Shared continent is not shared culture. Songkran is not Hmong New Year and not Tết. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 6,738; Twin Cities 60.8 percent; Greater Minnesota 39.2 percent; age 17 or younger 37.5 percent; 65+ about 4.9 percent; foreign-born 37.4 percent; among those 5 and older, English only about 33.3 percent, language other than English about 66.7 percent, English less than “very well” about 30.6 percent; high school or higher (25+) about 86.4 percent; bachelor’s or higher about 29.5 percent; median household income about $72,888 in 2022 dollars; poverty 17.8 percent; owner-occupied 46.4 percent; average household size about 3.15; individuals living alone about 18.6 percent. Female about 59.7 percent. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A wat household in the Twin Cities, a Greater Minnesota restaurant family, an Isan speaker, a Bangkok-origin professional, a U.S.-born child translating for a parent, a marriage-stream household far from a Thai-speaking neighbor — share a Compass row and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Thai peoplehood is older than the name Thailand (1939), older than 1932, and older than the restaurant file. Siam; kingdoms; a modern nation that marks itself as never colonized by a European power — that national narrative is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. It is not a virtue ranking against neighbors who were colonized.

### History for the meeting

Thai language is related to Lao. Related is not interchangeable. A Lao interpreter is not the default. Isan (northeastern Thai) is a neighboring variety some families will name. Ask. Do not guess. Do not mash Hmong into this origin because camps sat on Thai soil.

### What people brought

What people brought: language, Theravada practice or not, family obligation, foodways, a memory of a state that was not a camp. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, a restaurant cliché, and often a worker who has already filed them under Hmong because the building only studied the war.

Writing is Thai script. Related to Lao — not interchangeable. Many elders read Thai. Some do not. Second generation may not read it at all. A notice in Lao, or in English only, can still be a closed door. Ask.

### Titles

Elders first. English “hello” plus the name is ordinary. Say the name. Ask how to say it. Nicknames are ordinary in Thai address; the form-name may not be the name they use.

### This room

Do not import Hmong, Lao, Somali, or Black greeting rules onto this page.

Physical contact: ask the room. Do not touch the head. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default.
chapters.evidence: Wai (palms) in some rooms; handshake in many second-generation and professional rooms. Elders first. Thai greeting; English hello.
chapters.practitioner: Follow this room. Do not force a wai you saw in a video. Do not force a hug. Do not import Hmong, Lao, or Somali greeting rules. Say the name.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
Given names are used in address. Family names sit last in modern Thai practice — the Surname Act of 1913 is literacy for the desk, not a lecture. Family names can be long. Nicknames are ordinary and may be the only name a teacher or a nurse hears. Ask which name they use day to day. Ask how to file. Ask how to say it.

### How to file

U.S. forms flatten a long given name, invent a first-last pair, and then fail to match a nickname. That is a system failure, not a fraud signal until you have a reason.

Do not assume a Hmong clan name. Do not mash with Lao naming. Women may or may not take a husband’s family name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match.

The form that guesses will invent a person, and that invented name follows them through MHCP, school, and child welfare.
chapters.evidence: Given name used in address; family name last (Surname Act 1913 is literacy). Nicknames are ordinary. Long given names. U.S. forms flatten.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to say it and how to file it. Ask which name they use day to day. Do not treat a nickname as fraud. Do not assume a Hmong clan name.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
Songkran — Thai New Year — in April. Water, elders, wat, travel. Related mid-April new year to Lao Pi Mai, different people. Do not mash. Do not put “Asian holiday” on a case note. Schedule around it when you can. A calendar click is not community engagement.

### Calendar

Loy Krathong. Buddhist holy days (including Visakha). Thai Mother’s Day and Father’s Day in sending-country public life may matter in some rooms. Household dates will not be on your state calendar. Ask.

Do not mash Songkran with Hmong New Year, Tết, Chinese Lunar New Year, or Diwali. 1975 is a neighboring people’s date. It is not a Thai holiday and not an icebreaker for this family.
chapters.evidence: Songkran (Thai New Year, April). Loy Krathong. Buddhist holy days. Mother’s Day / Father’s Day in Thai public life. Not Hmong New Year. Not Pi Mai as a mash.
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Asian holiday” on a case note.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Thai and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only IEP is the gate. The child is not the interpreter. Book Thai, not Lao, not Hmong.

Greater Minnesota 39.2 percent means some children sit in districts that have never booked Thai. Under-identification in schools is a pattern to watch, not a rate to invent. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.

### In the home

Accept a little food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time. Do not photograph an altar. Do not touch ritual objects.

Courtesy-yes then no-show happens when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in Thai if that is the language they use.

### Language

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 66.7 percent speak a language other than English; about 30.6 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. This is a language gate, not a rounding error. Compare it with Korean or Filipino LEP on Compass if you need the building to see it. Do not invent a rate.

The camp mash is a closed door. Camps in Thailand are a Hmong and Karen story. Filing a Thai family under Ban Vinai or Mae La is how a building that only studied 1975 erases this people. Do not do it.

Restaurant labor is work, not a personality and not a joke. Hours, pay, and a Greater Minnesota town with one Thai family are labor facts. Do not write “Thai food” as ethnicity.

Poverty 17.8 percent is not zero. LEP 30.6 percent is a gate. Owner-occupied 46.4 percent is not a model-minority brochure. Female 59.7 percent is not a mail-order cliché. Do not invent that personality.

Never-colonized as a national narrative, 1932, Cold War U.S. presence, and a United States that met Thai people as students, spouses, workers, and neighbors — that is this political file. A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not collect immigration status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance. Do not use a restaurant, a marriage, or a camp as a personality.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
paragraphs: Ukrainian Minnesota. Historic and recent. Compass ACS 2019–2023 near 22,570. Not the Russian language door as a people. Census white can skip the interpreter. Date the number you cite.

There is no single Ukrainian client. Defer to this family. Do not open Russian Minnesota as a synonym. Book Ukrainian if that is the language; Russian only if this household asks for Russian. Pronounce the name.

This brief is about Ukrainian people — українці — as a people with a country, a language, and a Minnesota community that is historic and recent. This is not the Russian language door. It is not “Russian-speaking” as a people. Shared empire and a shared alphabet family are not shared culture. Do not open /ci/russian as a synonym. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian.

### Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one “former Soviet” interpreter, an English form because the person looks white, and a 2022 speech you give a third-generation parish household.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Ukrainian ancestry near 22,570. About 72.8 percent Twin Cities, about 27.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 31.1 percent age 17 or younger; about 13.5 percent 65+. About 30.3 percent foreign-born — which means a large share was born here and a large first generation was not. Date the number you use. The 2019–2023 five-year estimate includes early 2022 and does not hold the whole post-invasion stream. Do not invent a 2026 total. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Greek Catholic elder whose family has been in Minnesota since a mid-century parish, a 1990s professional, a 2014 arrival, a 2022 mother on humanitarian parole, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota household, a person who uses Ukrainian with an elder and English with friends, a household that uses Russian at the table and still names itself Ukrainian — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
paragraphs: Ukrainian peoplehood is older than 1991 and older than 2022. Kyivan Rusʼ memory; Cossack states; empire; Soviet; independent Ukraine. Named literature and a modern nation, not a camp origin myth.
History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a nesting-doll or borscht tourism sentence.

Ukrainian peoplehood is older than the Soviet Union, older than 1991, and older than 24 February 2022. A country on the Black Sea and the steppe; a language; a literature; churches that are not Moscow as a default. Kyivan Rusʼ memory, Cossack polities, partitions under empire, Holodomor, and a modern nation. Minnesota’s community is Ukrainian. Ask how this family names itself. Do not lecture a St. Paul family about taxonomy they did not ask for.

### History for the meeting

Writing in Ukrainian Cyrillic is the ordinary public literacy of the language. It is not Russian with a different flag. Many elders read it. Some do not. Second generation may not read Ukrainian at all. Some households use Russian as a home language because of Soviet schooling — that is a Tuesday fact, not a reason to file this people under the Russian door.

### What people brought

What people brought: language, parish, kinship, farming and professional skill, a memory of famine and of a state that denied the name. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, a racial order that may file them as white and skip the interpreter, and often one interpreter labeled “Russian.”

History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a nesting-doll, a borscht, or a 2022 tourism sentence.

sections.heading: The Geography of the Ukrainian World
paragraphs: Ukraine — west, center, east, south, Crimea as occupied geography some families name. Diaspora in Canada, the U.S., Europe. Compass: 72.8% Twin Cities, 27.2% Greater Minnesota.
Do not assume Northeast Minneapolis. Do not assume they have been to Ukraine. Greater Minnesota share is real. Do not referee Kyiv versus Donetsk in a waiver meeting.

Ukraine is west, center, east, south — language, church, and some vocabulary shift. Galicia and the Greek Catholic west are not Donetsk. Crimea is occupied geography some families name. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee Kyiv versus Lviv versus the east in a waiver meeting. Listen.

### Homeland

The diaspora is global: Canada (large historic community), the United States, Poland, Germany, and elsewhere. Toronto is not this map. Chicago and the Rust Belt sit on a different U.S. map. Secondary migration and parish networks built part of what you will meet here.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities — including some inner-ring suburbs and named parishes — and a real Greater Minnesota share. Compass: 72.8 percent Twin Cities, 27.2 percent Greater Minnesota. Do not assume Northeast Minneapolis is the whole. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Ukraine.

sections.heading: Historic Streams and 2022 — Foundational Events, Not One Flight
paragraphs: Late-imperial and early-20th-century streams; post-WWII displaced persons; 1991 independence; 2014 Crimea and Donbas; 24 February 2022 full-scale invasion and Uniting for Ukraine parole. Historic and recent. Different Tuesdays.
If you only know “2022 refugee,” you will miss the third-generation parish household and still cannot get Ukrainian for a grandmother who arrived last year.

If 1975 is the foundational event of Vietnamese Minnesota, Ukrainian Minnesota does not get one year. It gets a stack, and you will misread the room if you pick the wrong one.

### Foundational events

Late-imperial and early-twentieth-century labor and farm streams. Post-WWII displaced persons. 1991 independence and the 1990s movement. 2014 — Crimea annexed, war in the Donbas — moved some families before the full-scale invasion. 24 February 2022 is current structure for some households: Uniting for Ukraine humanitarian parole, relatives under fire, a child who has never seen a Minnesota winter. It is a trap if you treat every Ukrainian as last year’s arrival. It is also a trap if you pretend the war is not in the room when they name it.

### Who you meet

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born adults who do not need an interpreter, elders who need Ukrainian, mixed families, and people who will not accept a Russian-language flyer that looks like Moscow. Compass foreign-born 30.3 percent (ACS 2019–2023) is the dated share in that vintage — not the whole post-2022 stream.

2022 is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not ask a person to narrate Bucha, Mariupol, or a crossing for your professional development.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Nuclear and multi-generation both live here. Patronymic names the father in the person. Compass average household size about 2.46. Who speaks may be a child — that is a gate.
Ask who should be in the room. Do not use a child as interpreter. A nuclear English form already has a who. Do not drop the patronymic.

Family is not one size. Some households look nuclear on an English form and still carry obligation to a parent who does not drive and does not read the form. Some are three generations in one week. Some are a 2022 mother and children whose spouse is still in Ukraine. Compass: average household size about 2.46. Smaller than some neighboring spines. Still not always a nuclear English form.

### Who is in the household

The patronymic — a name built from the father — is how a person is fully named in Ukrainian. A form that keeps only first and last has already dropped a who. Ask how to file. Ask who should be in the room.

### Who speaks

Adult children may speak for an elder in English. That is a hypothesis, not permission to skip the interpreter or to use a child. CLAS still stands. A sixteen-year-old in the lobby is not the qualified interpreter.

Women’s labor and professional second generation sit next to older gender patterns in some rooms. Both can be true. Minnesota law still stands on violence, neglect, and who may consent. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it culture.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Ukrainian History
paragraphs: Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota 27.2%. Ukrainian Catholic and Orthodox parishes families name. Civic groups this family names. No single “Russian community center” as this people. CECLC is a door.
Partners, not a harvest list. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  Ukrainian staff. Guest at a liturgy if invited. A festival visit does not make you the expert.

Minnesota holds a Ukrainian community large enough for a Compass profile and large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment — historic parish households and recent arrivals in the same week. Compass: about 22,570 (ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is 27.2 percent. Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities; inner-ring suburbs; Greater Minnesota towns. Do not write “the Ukrainian neighborhood” onto a map you do not have. Pattern now.

### Partners

Partners: Ukrainian Catholic parishes some families name; Ukrainian Orthodox parishes some families name; civic groups this family names; no single “Russian community center” as this people. CECLC is a department door — not the community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Do not extract Ukrainian staff as the interpreter or as “the community.” A liturgy is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Українці — not a Russian-speaking file
paragraphs: Українці. Peoplehood with a country, a language, and a war that is current for some and a history class for others. White in a U.S. racial order that may skip CI. Not a Russian-speaking file.
Do not fold this household into “Eastern European” or into the Russian CLAS door. Do not copy a Russian, Polish, or “white Minnesota” sentence onto this page.

To be Ukrainian in Minnesota is to be a people with a country and a language, filed under white in a building that may skip the interpreter and skip the page. Face, parish, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### In this state

2022 sits in the room for some and is a news cycle for others. Historic parish families, 1990s arrivals, 2014, U.S.-born children, and last year’s parole household do not share one Tuesday. You do not referee. You do not put a war slogan on a case note as color.

In the United States another fact sits on the same desk: many Ukrainian Minnesotans are read as white. The building’s unmarked default will skip Ukrainian, skip the patronymic, and call that fairness. That skip is the gate. White appearance is not English proficiency and not the absence of a people.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
paragraphs: Ukrainian not Russian as a synonym; language of the home asked, not assumed; patronymic as personhood; parish as a channel not the community; historic versus 2022; white appearance is not English.
You work with these. You do not perform them. Do not make a priest the case plan unless this family asked. Book Ukrainian if that is the language.

Ukrainian, not Russian as a synonym. The first grammar. If you open the Russian door because the face is white and the name looks Slavic, you do not have a household yet.

### Language of the home, asked

Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. After 2022, a Russian interpreter can be a political door. Confirm.

### Patronymic

Given name, father’s name as a middle element, family name. Dropping it invents a person. Filing it wrong invents a person. Ask.

### Parish as a channel, not the community

Ukrainian Greek Catholic, Orthodox, evangelical, none. Do not make a priest the case plan unless this family asked.

### Historic versus 2022

A third-generation English-dominant household and a parole arrival are not one file. You do not interrogate loyalty. You do the form.

### White appearance is not English

The skip is the gate.

sections.heading: Religion
paragraphs: Ukrainian Orthodox, Ukrainian Greek Catholic, Roman Catholic, evangelical, Jewish in some families, none. Streams do not share a sanctuary. Ask.
Do not make a priest or pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Do not assume Moscow-patriarchate politics. Do not assume no church.

Ask. Ukrainian Orthodox and Ukrainian Greek Catholic (Byzantine rite, in communion with Rome) are the two large historic public streams. Roman Catholic, evangelical Protestant, Jewish in some families, and none all live here. Do not assume Moscow. Do not assume no church.

### Streams

The parish is a center of liturgy, memorial, and sometimes mutual aid. It is not the community. Do not BCC one priest and call it consultation. Icons in a home are not a case plan and not a museum.

### Practice

Intra-church politics after 2018 — autocephaly, Moscow patriarchate — are real in some rooms. You do not referee them on a case note.

Do not rank piety. A person who left the church is still this people-page if that is the household in front of you.

sections.heading: Greetings
paragraphs: Handshake common in many rooms. Titles. Given name plus patronymic is respectful address in Ukrainian. Добрий день. Follow this room.
Do not force a hug. Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod. Say the name. Ask how to address an elder.

Handshake is common in many rooms — men, and often women in professional space. Follow this room. Some older parish settings will change the rule. You nod if a hand is not offered. You do not make a scene in the lobby.

### Titles

Titles matter. Given name plus patronymic is the respectful Ukrainian address for an adult you do not know well. English Mr./Ms. plus family name is a decent substitute if you cannot produce the patronymic. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it.

### This room

Добрий день is a common formal hello. English “hello” is ordinary, especially with the second generation. Say the name. Ask how to say it.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Physical contact: follow this person. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
paragraphs: Given name + patronymic + family name. -enko, -uk, -chuk, -skyi endings. Gendered family-name endings in some records. Databases that drop the patronymic invent a person. Kyiv not a correction you perform on the form.
Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not invent a middle name because the screen wants one. Do not “correct” toward a Russian spelling. The invented name becomes a gate.

A common Ukrainian pattern is given name, patronymic, family name. The patronymic is not a middle name you may drop for convenience. Databases that drop it invent a person. That invented person then fails a match in MHCP, child welfare, and school.

### How to file

Family names may take a gendered ending. -enko, -uk, -chuk, -skyi / -ska are patterns, not a joke. The form that flags the difference as fraud has already chosen a household type. Ask how to file. Ask how this person wants the English record to read.

Do not “correct” a name toward a Russian textbook. Kyiv, Kharkiv, Lviv are place-literacy for the desk. On the form, write what they tell you. Pronounce it. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s family name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match. That is not fraud until you have a reason. Three people in one household may not share a “last name” the way a Swedish Minnesota form expects.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
paragraphs: Orthodox Nativity and Pascha for some; Ukrainian Greek Catholic calendar for some; Independence Day 24 August; Holodomor remembrance; 24 February 2022 as current structure for some, not a holiday.
A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put a Ukraine-war slogan on a case note.

Orthodox Nativity and Pascha follow the Julian calendar for many Orthodox households — often later than Western Christmas and Easter. Some Ukrainian churches have moved Nativity to 25 December. Ask. They are not a day off the work. They are literacy.

### Calendar

Independence Day — 24 August. Holodomor Remembrance — fourth Saturday of November in many Ukrainian rooms. Literacy, not a file. Vyshyvanka Day exists in some public life. A calendar click is not community engagement.

24 February 2022 is current structure for some families. It is not a holiday and not a personality. Do not put a war slogan, a flag lecture, or “Fall of Saigon party” energy on a case note.

Do not put “Eastern European holiday” on a case note.

sections.heading: Education
paragraphs: Compass: ~93.9% high school or higher (25+); ~53.7% bachelor’s or higher. Foreign-born 30.3%. High attainment is not “no language gate.” English IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.
A parent who reads Ukrainian and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Do not skip the interpreter because the person looks white or professional.

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Ukrainian Minnesotans 25 and older, about 93.9 percent high school or higher; about 53.7 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 30.3 percent of the community is foreign-born. High attainment is not “no language gate.” A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Ukrainian and limited English is not illiterate. Many elders read Ukrainian Cyrillic. Some do not. Recent arrivals may hold credentials this country has not recognized. The English-only form is the gate.

Do not skip the interpreter because the adult in the lobby is white, employed, or accent-light. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.

sections.heading: Etiquette
paragraphs: Shoes in some homes. Hospitality. Formality with elders. Icons in some living rooms. Flowers and food as ordinary courtesy in some rooms.
Accept a little tea. Keep medical and legal time. Do not photograph icons or a home altar. Follow this household.

Elders first. Shoes off in some homes. Accept a little tea or food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not walk into a living room and photograph an icon corner or a family photograph wall. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain the war as entertainment.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. Courtesy-yes then no-show happens when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
paragraphs: Ukrainian is not Russian. Cyrillic literacy for many elders; some recent arrivals; some U.S.-born do not read it. Compass: ~30.8% language other than English (5+); ~13.2% LEP. Some households use Russian — ask. After 2022 a Russian interpreter can be a political door.

Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. Still book a qualified interpreter. Do not use a child. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  staff. Do not take a smile as consent.

Ukrainian is not Russian. It is not Belarusian. It is not “former Soviet.” An interpreter labeled Russian who is the wrong language for this household is a closed door — and after 2022, a political door. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. CLAS: still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the dialect.

### Language

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 30.8 percent speak a language other than English; about 13.2 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Many elders read Ukrainian in Cyrillic. Some U.S.-born adults do not. A notice in Russian is not a Ukrainian notice.

White appearance is not English. Do not take a light accent as “no interpreter needed” without asking. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Ukrainian coworker the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice
paragraphs: War trauma in some 2022 rooms is not a personality. Intra-community language politics. Alcohol and family violence exist and are not “the culture.” LGBTQ people exist. Status fear for some recent arrivals. White skip of CI.
Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Do not collect status you do not need.

Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

War trauma is real in some 2022 rooms: cities, roads, loss, a spouse still there. It is not a personality. It is not a reason to skip screening. It is a reason a government badge is not automatically help. Do not invent a Minnesota PTSD rate.

Intra-community language politics still split some rooms — Ukrainian only, Russian at the table, mixed families. You do not referee. You book the language this household asks for.

Alcohol harm and family violence exist in some households. They are not “the culture.” They are not a Slavic joke. You follow the law. You still see a family. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Immigration status fear is real for some recent arrivals, including parole that can expire. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

LGBTQ Ukrainian Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
paragraphs: Compass uninsured 4.5% (ACS 2019–2023) — date it; it is not the 2022 arrival. Do not invent a PTSD rate. Trauma in some streams. Mental-health stigma. Believe reported pain. Do not invent Slavic stoicism.
Book the language they name. Offer gender match. Do not skip screening. Do not ask a person to narrate Bucha for your professional development.

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 4.5 percent without health insurance among those for whom status is determined. Date it. That vintage is not the whole 2022 stream. Do not invent a PTSD rate to fill this chapter. Trauma sits in some rooms. It is not every household.

### Access

Believe reported pain. Do not invent a Slavic or “European stoicism” slide. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic refugee module.

Mental-health stigma exists in some families. Naming a counselor is not the same as a family accepting one. A smile is not a PHQ-9. War does not make screening optional. It does not make every person a case study.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Book the language they name even if the person is white. Confirm Ukrainian, not a “former Soviet” default.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
paragraphs: Queer and trans Ukrainian Minnesotans exist. Conservative parish climates can mean silence. The war does not erase this person. Minnesota Human Rights Act still applies.
Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture. Do not treat a war as a veto over this person.

Queer and trans Ukrainian Minnesotans exist. Conservative Orthodox, Greek Catholic, and some family climates can mean silence or exile. The war does not erase this person and does not get a veto over the name they use.

### This person

Staff duty is the same as on the other spines: use the name they use; do not out them to an elder as cultural humility; Minnesota Human Rights Act still applies.

Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
paragraphs: Vyshyvanka is public at festivals and some church days, not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Head covering in some parish rooms.
Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch. Do not mash with a matryoshka Heritage Month table.

Vyshyvanka is public at festivals, Independence Day tables, and some church days. It is not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

Head covering happens in some parish rooms. It is not a security threat and not a consent problem. Do not touch. Do not comment on gold, a cross, or embroidery as a case note.

Winter dress is Minnesota. It is not ethnography. Heritage Month tables that mash this with a matryoshka have already failed the adjacent-peoples chapter.

sections.heading: Music
paragraphs: Church chant, kobzar and folk, pop, wartime song in some rooms. Named variation. Not a Russian mix.
A playlist is not engagement. A liturgy or a funeral is not staff entertainment. Do not put the wrong anthem on a speaker.

Church chant is liturgy, not a playlist. Kobzar and folk forms, popular song, and wartime music exist in some rooms. Named variation, not a “Slavic mix.”

### Variation

A playlist is not engagement. A funeral or a liturgy is not staff entertainment. Knowing that 2022 can sit inside a song will stop you from putting the wrong flag on a speaker.

Festival stages are public life. They are not consultation and not a case plan.

sections.heading: Sports
paragraphs: Soccer, and ordinary school sport in the second generation. Not a people-trait.
Do not assume the kid plays. Sport clubs are not language access.

Soccer shows up in public Ukrainian Minnesota life. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

### Not the whole person

Sport clubs are social infrastructure for some. They are not language access and not a case plan. A club flyer in English is still a closed door for the parent who needs Ukrainian on the line.

Greater Minnesota and Twin Cities both play.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: A vast written literature in Ukrainian. Shevchenko is literacy, not a lobby quote. Cyrillic for many elders. U.S.-born may not read it. This is not a people without letters.
You do not need to quote Кобзар. You need the language this person reads. Ukrainian is not Russian literature with a different flag.

Ukrainian is a major written language with a long literature. Shevchenko is literacy for the desk, not a prompt to quote Кобзар in the lobby. This is not a people without letters. It is not Russian literature with a different flag.

### Literacy in the lobby

Cyrillic literacy for many elders is the actual operations fact. A notice that exists only in English, or only in Russian, is a closed door. U.S.-born adults may not read Cyrillic and may still be the person who has to explain the form.

You do not need a novel. You need the language this person reads.

sections.heading: Art
paragraphs: Pysanky, vyshyvanka, icons, diaspora visual work. Not matryoshka. Not a nesting-doll exhibit.
Guest, not researcher. An icon is not a case plan. A festival is not consultation.

Pysanky, vyshyvanka embroidery, icons, and diaspora visual work. Not matryoshka. Not a nesting-doll exhibit. Not a Russian folk-costume mash.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. An icon is not a case plan. A festival is not consultation. Do not photograph a sanctuary as professional development without being asked.

Heritage Month tables that mash a vyshyvanka, a menorah, and a matryoshka into one “Eastern European” booth have already mashed what this brief asks you to keep apart.

sections.heading: War, the State, and the Russian-Door Trap
paragraphs: Holodomor; Soviet state; 1991; 2014; 24 February 2022; Uniting for Ukraine parole and later enforcement climate for some. A DHS badge is not automatically help.
Do not use 2022 as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate a war. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not assume every Ukrainian is last year’s arrival.

Holodomor, Soviet surveillance, 1991, 2014, 24 February 2022, Uniting for Ukraine parole, and later enforcement climate for some arrivals — that is the political stack. A DHS badge is not automatically help. For some people, a government form is a thing you survive. That is not “paranoia.” It is pattern.

### The badge

The war is current structure for some households: family under fire, mixed marriages, parole that can expire, people who left and people who have been here for three generations. It is a trap if you assume every Ukrainian is a 2022 refugee. It is also a trap if you punish someone for not performing the politics you prefer.

Do not use 2022 as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate a war for your professional development. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not open the Russian language door as this people.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
paragraphs: Professional, trade, small business, public employment. High Compass attainment is not this kitchen table. Ukrainian staff inside the department are not unpaid interpreters and not “the community.”
Identity is not a staffing plan. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  staff. Relationship may precede a signature. The notice still has to exist in the language they read.

Professional work, trades, small business, public employment, and under-recognized credentials all live here. A small-business owner and a waiver recipient may be the same extended family. Compass median household income about $95,000 is an average, not this kitchen table.

### Work

Ukrainian staff exist inside DHS and counties. They are not unpaid interpreters and not “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Staff

Relationship and hospitality may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision. The notice still has to exist in the language they read.

An English eList comment period is not how this community was reached.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
paragraphs: Language: Ukrainian unless they ask for Russian. Patronymic. Assuming English because white. Who is in the room. Child as interpreter. War climate for some. Enforcement for some recent arrivals.
Confirm the language. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Ask how to file the name. Ask who should hear. Believe reported pain. Mandated reporting still exists.

Language. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. Patronymic. Who is in the room. Assuming English because the person is white. A child pushed forward as English. War climate for some. Enforcement climate for some recent arrivals.

### Language

Confirm the language. Still book a qualified interpreter. Offer gender match. Ask who should hear. Ask how to file the name. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

Believe reported pain. Do not invent stoicism. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a risk score. Do not collect status you do not need.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
paragraphs: Not the Russian language door as a people (open /ci/russian for a Russian-language request). Not Belarusian mash. Not Polish as a synonym. Not “white = no CI.” Not one former-Soviet interpreter.
Open this for a Ukrainian household. Open Russian Minnesota only as a language door if they ask for Russian. Ask this household.

Not the Russian language door as a people. Open /ci/russian for a Russian-language request. A Ukrainian family that uses Russian still gets to name their people. Ask. A Russian interpreter can still be the wrong door.

### Adjacent doors

Not Belarusian mash. Not Polish as a synonym. Not a “former Soviet” interpreter. Not Somali. Not the African American CI. Not “white = no cultural intelligence.” Historic German- and Scandinavian-Minnesota unmarked culture is the European American door, not this one.

Some households are mixed. Ask this household. Never one East-European module. Never one Slavic interpreter.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
paragraphs: Compass ACS 2019–2023: ~22,570; 72.8% metro; 27.2% Greater MN; 31.1% 17 or younger; 65+ 13.5%; foreign-born 30.3%; LOTE 30.8%; LEP 13.2%; HS+ 93.9%; bachelor+ 53.7%; poverty 8.2%; owner 66.4%; avg HH 2.46. Date them. Do not invent a post-2022 total.
A rate is not the person. Language and child-as-interpreter are gates. White appearance is not English.

Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Ukrainian cultural community: about 22,570; Twin Cities 72.8%; Greater Minnesota 27.2%; age 17 or younger 31.1%; 65+ 13.5%; foreign-born 30.3%; language other than English (age 5+) 30.8%; English less than “very well” 13.2%; English only 69.2%; high school or higher (25+) 93.9%; bachelor’s or higher 53.7%; median household income about $95,000 (2022 dollars, averaged); poverty 8.2%; owner-occupied 66.4%; average household size 2.46; uninsured 4.5%.

### Counts

Date Compass. The 2019–2023 five-year estimate includes early 2022 and does not hold the whole post-invasion stream. Do not invent a 2026 community total. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions (ancestry vs. birthplace vs. language). Date the number you cite.

### What the count is not

A young age structure is not a personality. An owner rate is not proof the gates closed. Language and child-as-interpreter are gates. White appearance is not English. A rate is not the person.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
paragraphs: Compass Ukrainian profile ACS 2019–2023. Ukrainian Catholic and Orthodox parishes families name. Civic groups this family names. CECLC is a door, not the community. Adjacent: Russian CLAS five — not this people-page.
Learn on your own time. Do not make a Ukrainian colleague your unpaid tutor. Pay partners. Book Ukrainian if that is the language.

Minnesota Compass Ukrainian profile (ACS 2019–2023). Ukrainian Catholic and Orthodox parishes families name. Civic groups this family names. CECLC is a door, not the whole community.

### Public doors

Adjacent, not this page: DHS Equal Opportunity and Access LEP resources — Russian on the five. That list is not this people. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian.

### Learn on your own time

Learn on your own time. Do not make a Ukrainian colleague your unpaid tutor. Do not BCC a parish and call it consultation. Pay partners. Report back. Guest at a liturgy if invited — it is not consultation.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
paragraphs: Ukrainian vs Russian on the interpreter line; patronymics on nuclear forms; assuming English because the person is white; 2022/parole climate for some; English eList; harvesting Ukrainian staff; Greater Minnesota 27.2%; Russian door as a people-mash.

Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. Book a qualified interpreter even if the person is white. Ask how to file the name. Toolkit disposition on the packet. If the household cannot run the exception in English, the cap is the policy. Statute may still stand. Name who the packet was built for.

Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: Ukrainian is not Russian. An interpreter labeled “former Soviet” is a closed door. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. Still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the dialect. Cyrillic is not optional decoration on a notice that actually has to be read. Do not use a child.

Names: given name, patronymic, family name. The database that drops the patronymic or “corrects” toward a Russian spelling invents a person.

Assuming English because the person is white is a CLAS failure wearing Minnesota Nice.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Enforcement and parole climate: some recent arrivals skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 27.2 percent — a St. Paul meeting is not the whole channel.

Workforce: Ukrainian staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  them.

Russian mash: opening /ci/russian because the checkbox or the face looks “Slavic” is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that treated a white face as no CI and a language list as a people.

sections.heading: Minnesota context
paragraphs: Minnesota Compass: 22,570 people — ACS 2019–2023 (Minnesota Compass cultural communities). Date it. Counts disagree across vintages. Source: https://www.mncompass.org/topics/demographics/cultural-communities/ukrainian

sections.heading: Ways to connect
paragraphs: Local organizations — named in the deepening — Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum.

sections.heading: In the work
paragraphs: DHS: Open the cultural intelligence. Toolkit on the work in front of you. Language access.
