community.title: Ukrainian Minnesota

chapters.body:
This brief is about Ukrainian people — українці — as a people with a country, a language, and a Minnesota community that is historic and recent. This is not the Russian language door. It is not “Russian-speaking” as a people. Shared empire and a shared alphabet family are not shared culture. Do not open /ci/russian as a synonym. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian.

### Who this is

A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby. Paternalism is one “former Soviet” interpreter, an English form because the person looks white, and a 2022 speech you give a third-generation parish household.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Ukrainian ancestry near 22,570. About 72.8 percent Twin Cities, about 27.2 percent Greater Minnesota. About 31.1 percent age 17 or younger; about 13.5 percent 65+. About 30.3 percent foreign-born — which means a large share was born here and a large first generation was not. Date the number you use. The 2019–2023 five-year estimate includes early 2022 and does not hold the whole post-invasion stream. Do not invent a 2026 total. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A Greek Catholic elder whose family has been in Minnesota since a mid-century parish, a 1990s professional, a 2014 arrival, a 2022 mother on humanitarian parole, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota household, a person who uses Ukrainian with an elder and English with friends, a household that uses Russian at the table and still names itself Ukrainian — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.
chapters.evidence: Ukrainian Minnesota. Historic and recent. Compass ACS 2019–2023 near 22,570. Not the Russian language door as a people. Census white can skip the interpreter. Date the number you cite.
chapters.practitioner: There is no single Ukrainian client. Defer to this family. Do not open Russian Minnesota as a synonym. Book Ukrainian if that is the language; Russian only if this household asks for Russian. Pronounce the name.
chapters.title: A Note on This Guide

chapters.body:
Ukrainian peoplehood is older than the Soviet Union, older than 1991, and older than 24 February 2022. A country on the Black Sea and the steppe; a language; a literature; churches that are not Moscow as a default. Kyivan Rusʼ memory, Cossack polities, partitions under empire, Holodomor, and a modern nation. Minnesota’s community is Ukrainian. Ask how this family names itself. Do not lecture a St. Paul family about taxonomy they did not ask for.

### History for the meeting

Writing in Ukrainian Cyrillic is the ordinary public literacy of the language. It is not Russian with a different flag. Many elders read it. Some do not. Second generation may not read Ukrainian at all. Some households use Russian as a home language because of Soviet schooling — that is a Tuesday fact, not a reason to file this people under the Russian door.

### What people brought

What people brought: language, parish, kinship, farming and professional skill, a memory of famine and of a state that denied the name. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, a racial order that may file them as white and skip the interpreter, and often one interpreter labeled “Russian.”

History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a nesting-doll, a borscht, or a 2022 tourism sentence.
chapters.evidence: Ukrainian peoplehood is older than 1991 and older than 2022. Kyivan Rusʼ memory; Cossack states; empire; Soviet; independent Ukraine. Named literature and a modern nation, not a camp origin myth.
chapters.practitioner: History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a nesting-doll or borscht tourism sentence.
chapters.title: Origins and the Founding of a People

chapters.body:
Ukraine is west, center, east, south — language, church, and some vocabulary shift. Galicia and the Greek Catholic west are not Donetsk. Crimea is occupied geography some families name. Confirm the place if they name it. Do not referee Kyiv versus Lviv versus the east in a waiver meeting. Listen.

### Homeland

The diaspora is global: Canada (large historic community), the United States, Poland, Germany, and elsewhere. Toronto is not this map. Chicago and the Rust Belt sit on a different U.S. map. Secondary migration and parish networks built part of what you will meet here.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities — including some inner-ring suburbs and named parishes — and a real Greater Minnesota share. Compass: 72.8 percent Twin Cities, 27.2 percent Greater Minnesota. Do not assume Northeast Minneapolis is the whole. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Ukraine.
chapters.evidence: Ukraine — west, center, east, south, Crimea as occupied geography some families name. Diaspora in Canada, the U.S., Europe. Compass: 72.8% Twin Cities, 27.2% Greater Minnesota.
chapters.practitioner: Do not assume Northeast Minneapolis. Do not assume they have been to Ukraine. Greater Minnesota share is real. Do not referee Kyiv versus Donetsk in a waiver meeting.
chapters.title: The Geography of the Ukrainian World

chapters.body:
If 1975 is the foundational event of Vietnamese Minnesota, Ukrainian Minnesota does not get one year. It gets a stack, and you will misread the room if you pick the wrong one.

### Foundational events

Late-imperial and early-twentieth-century labor and farm streams. Post-WWII displaced persons. 1991 independence and the 1990s movement. 2014 — Crimea annexed, war in the Donbas — moved some families before the full-scale invasion. 24 February 2022 is current structure for some households: Uniting for Ukraine humanitarian parole, relatives under fire, a child who has never seen a Minnesota winter. It is a trap if you treat every Ukrainian as last year’s arrival. It is also a trap if you pretend the war is not in the room when they name it.

### Who you meet

The desk in 2026 meets U.S.-born adults who do not need an interpreter, elders who need Ukrainian, mixed families, and people who will not accept a Russian-language flyer that looks like Moscow. Compass foreign-born 30.3 percent (ACS 2019–2023) is the dated share in that vintage — not the whole post-2022 stream.

2022 is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not ask a person to narrate Bucha, Mariupol, or a crossing for your professional development.
chapters.evidence: Late-imperial and early-20th-century streams; post-WWII displaced persons; 1991 independence; 2014 Crimea and Donbas; 24 February 2022 full-scale invasion and Uniting for Ukraine parole. Historic and recent. Different Tuesdays.
chapters.practitioner: If you only know “2022 refugee,” you will miss the third-generation parish household and still cannot get Ukrainian for a grandmother who arrived last year.
chapters.title: Historic Streams and 2022 — Foundational Events, Not One Flight

chapters.body:
Family is not one size. Some households look nuclear on an English form and still carry obligation to a parent who does not drive and does not read the form. Some are three generations in one week. Some are a 2022 mother and children whose spouse is still in Ukraine. Compass: average household size about 2.46. Smaller than some neighboring spines. Still not always a nuclear English form.

### Who is in the household

The patronymic — a name built from the father — is how a person is fully named in Ukrainian. A form that keeps only first and last has already dropped a who. Ask how to file. Ask who should be in the room.

### Who speaks

Adult children may speak for an elder in English. That is a hypothesis, not permission to skip the interpreter or to use a child. CLAS still stands. A sixteen-year-old in the lobby is not the qualified interpreter.

Women’s labor and professional second generation sit next to older gender patterns in some rooms. Both can be true. Minnesota law still stands on violence, neglect, and who may consent. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it culture.
chapters.evidence: Nuclear and multi-generation both live here. Patronymic names the father in the person. Compass average household size about 2.46. Who speaks may be a child — that is a gate.
chapters.practitioner: Ask who should be in the room. Do not use a child as interpreter. A nuclear English form already has a who. Do not drop the patronymic.
chapters.title: Family

chapters.body:
Minnesota holds a Ukrainian community large enough for a Compass profile and large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment — historic parish households and recent arrivals in the same week. Compass: about 22,570 (ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is 27.2 percent. Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote.

### Places

Places, not a blob: Twin Cities; inner-ring suburbs; Greater Minnesota towns. Do not write “the Ukrainian neighborhood” onto a map you do not have. Pattern now.

### Partners

Partners: Ukrainian Catholic parishes some families name; Ukrainian Orthodox parishes some families name; civic groups this family names; no single “Russian community center” as this people. CECLC is a department door — not the community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Do not extract Ukrainian staff as the interpreter or as “the community.” A liturgy is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.
chapters.evidence: Twin Cities and Greater Minnesota 27.2%. Ukrainian Catholic and Orthodox parishes families name. Civic groups this family names. No single “Russian community center” as this people. CECLC is a door.
chapters.practitioner: Partners, not a harvest list. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  Ukrainian staff. Guest at a liturgy if invited. A festival visit does not make you the expert.
chapters.title: Minnesota and Ukrainian History

chapters.body:
To be Ukrainian in Minnesota is to be a people with a country and a language, filed under white in a building that may skip the interpreter and skip the page. Face, parish, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### In this state

2022 sits in the room for some and is a news cycle for others. Historic parish families, 1990s arrivals, 2014, U.S.-born children, and last year’s parole household do not share one Tuesday. You do not referee. You do not put a war slogan on a case note as color.

In the United States another fact sits on the same desk: many Ukrainian Minnesotans are read as white. The building’s unmarked default will skip Ukrainian, skip the patronymic, and call that fairness. That skip is the gate. White appearance is not English proficiency and not the absence of a people.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.
chapters.evidence: Українці. Peoplehood with a country, a language, and a war that is current for some and a history class for others. White in a U.S. racial order that may skip CI. Not a Russian-speaking file.
chapters.practitioner: Do not fold this household into “Eastern European” or into the Russian CLAS door. Do not copy a Russian, Polish, or “white Minnesota” sentence onto this page.
chapters.title: Українці — not a Russian-speaking file

chapters.body:
Ukrainian, not Russian as a synonym. The first grammar. If you open the Russian door because the face is white and the name looks Slavic, you do not have a household yet.

### Language of the home, asked

Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. After 2022, a Russian interpreter can be a political door. Confirm.

### Patronymic

Given name, father’s name as a middle element, family name. Dropping it invents a person. Filing it wrong invents a person. Ask.

### Parish as a channel, not the community

Ukrainian Greek Catholic, Orthodox, evangelical, none. Do not make a priest the case plan unless this family asked.

### Historic versus 2022

A third-generation English-dominant household and a parole arrival are not one file. You do not interrogate loyalty. You do the form.

### White appearance is not English

The skip is the gate.
chapters.evidence: Ukrainian not Russian as a synonym; language of the home asked, not assumed; patronymic as personhood; parish as a channel not the community; historic versus 2022; white appearance is not English.
chapters.practitioner: You work with these. You do not perform them. Do not make a priest the case plan unless this family asked. Book Ukrainian if that is the language.
chapters.title: Core Concepts

chapters.body:
Ask. Ukrainian Orthodox and Ukrainian Greek Catholic (Byzantine rite, in communion with Rome) are the two large historic public streams. Roman Catholic, evangelical Protestant, Jewish in some families, and none all live here. Do not assume Moscow. Do not assume no church.

### Streams

The parish is a center of liturgy, memorial, and sometimes mutual aid. It is not the community. Do not BCC one priest and call it consultation. Icons in a home are not a case plan and not a museum.

### Practice

Intra-church politics after 2018 — autocephaly, Moscow patriarchate — are real in some rooms. You do not referee them on a case note.

Do not rank piety. A person who left the church is still this people-page if that is the household in front of you.
chapters.evidence: Ukrainian Orthodox, Ukrainian Greek Catholic, Roman Catholic, evangelical, Jewish in some families, none. Streams do not share a sanctuary. Ask.
chapters.practitioner: Do not make a priest or pastor the case plan unless this family asked. Do not assume Moscow-patriarchate politics. Do not assume no church.
chapters.title: Religion

chapters.body:
Handshake is common in many rooms — men, and often women in professional space. Follow this room. Some older parish settings will change the rule. You nod if a hand is not offered. You do not make a scene in the lobby.

### Titles

Titles matter. Given name plus patronymic is the respectful Ukrainian address for an adult you do not know well. English Mr./Ms. plus family name is a decent substitute if you cannot produce the patronymic. Do not use a first name with an elder because the form printed it.

### This room

Добрий день is a common formal hello. English “hello” is ordinary, especially with the second generation. Say the name. Ask how to say it.

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars. Physical contact: follow this person. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.
chapters.evidence: Handshake common in many rooms. Titles. Given name plus patronymic is respectful address in Ukrainian. Добрий день. Follow this room.
chapters.practitioner: Do not force a hug. Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod. Say the name. Ask how to address an elder.
chapters.title: Greetings

chapters.body:
A common Ukrainian pattern is given name, patronymic, family name. The patronymic is not a middle name you may drop for convenience. Databases that drop it invent a person. That invented person then fails a match in MHCP, child welfare, and school.

### How to file

Family names may take a gendered ending. -enko, -uk, -chuk, -skyi / -ska are patterns, not a joke. The form that flags the difference as fraud has already chosen a household type. Ask how to file. Ask how this person wants the English record to read.

Do not “correct” a name toward a Russian textbook. Kyiv, Kharkiv, Lviv are place-literacy for the desk. On the form, write what they tell you. Pronounce it. Ask.

Women may or may not take a husband’s family name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match. That is not fraud until you have a reason. Three people in one household may not share a “last name” the way a Swedish Minnesota form expects.
chapters.evidence: Given name + patronymic + family name. -enko, -uk, -chuk, -skyi endings. Gendered family-name endings in some records. Databases that drop the patronymic invent a person. Kyiv not a correction you perform on the form.
chapters.practitioner: Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not invent a middle name because the screen wants one. Do not “correct” toward a Russian spelling. The invented name becomes a gate.
chapters.title: Naming Conventions

chapters.body:
Orthodox Nativity and Pascha follow the Julian calendar for many Orthodox households — often later than Western Christmas and Easter. Some Ukrainian churches have moved Nativity to 25 December. Ask. They are not a day off the work. They are literacy.

### Calendar

Independence Day — 24 August. Holodomor Remembrance — fourth Saturday of November in many Ukrainian rooms. Literacy, not a file. Vyshyvanka Day exists in some public life. A calendar click is not community engagement.

24 February 2022 is current structure for some families. It is not a holiday and not a personality. Do not put a war slogan, a flag lecture, or “Fall of Saigon party” energy on a case note.

Do not put “Eastern European holiday” on a case note.
chapters.evidence: Orthodox Nativity and Pascha for some; Ukrainian Greek Catholic calendar for some; Independence Day 24 August; Holodomor remembrance; 24 February 2022 as current structure for some, not a holiday.
chapters.practitioner: A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put a Ukraine-war slogan on a case note.
chapters.title: Dates of Significance

chapters.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Ukrainian Minnesotans 25 and older, about 93.9 percent high school or higher; about 53.7 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 30.3 percent of the community is foreign-born. High attainment is not “no language gate.” A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Ukrainian and limited English is not illiterate. Many elders read Ukrainian Cyrillic. Some do not. Recent arrivals may hold credentials this country has not recognized. The English-only form is the gate.

Do not skip the interpreter because the adult in the lobby is white, employed, or accent-light. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Compass: ~93.9% high school or higher (25+); ~53.7% bachelor’s or higher. Foreign-born 30.3%. High attainment is not “no language gate.” English IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.
chapters.practitioner: A parent who reads Ukrainian and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Do not skip the interpreter because the person looks white or professional.
chapters.title: Education

chapters.body:
Elders first. Shoes off in some homes. Accept a little tea or food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not walk into a living room and photograph an icon corner or a family photograph wall. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain the war as entertainment.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. Courtesy-yes then no-show happens when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Shoes in some homes. Hospitality. Formality with elders. Icons in some living rooms. Flowers and food as ordinary courtesy in some rooms.
chapters.practitioner: Accept a little tea. Keep medical and legal time. Do not photograph icons or a home altar. Follow this household.
chapters.title: Etiquette

chapters.body:
Ukrainian is not Russian. It is not Belarusian. It is not “former Soviet.” An interpreter labeled Russian who is the wrong language for this household is a closed door — and after 2022, a political door. Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. CLAS: still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the dialect.

### Language

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 30.8 percent speak a language other than English; about 13.2 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Many elders read Ukrainian in Cyrillic. Some U.S.-born adults do not. A notice in Russian is not a Ukrainian notice.

White appearance is not English. Do not take a light accent as “no interpreter needed” without asking. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Ukrainian coworker the interpreter.
chapters.evidence: Ukrainian is not Russian. Cyrillic literacy for many elders; some recent arrivals; some U.S.-born do not read it. Compass: ~30.8% language other than English (5+); ~13.2% LEP. Some households use Russian — ask. After 2022 a Russian interpreter can be a political door.
chapters.practitioner: Book Ukrainian if that is the language. Russian only if this household asks for Russian. Still book a qualified interpreter. Do not use a child. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  staff. Do not take a smile as consent.
chapters.title: Language and Communication

chapters.body:
Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

War trauma is real in some 2022 rooms: cities, roads, loss, a spouse still there. It is not a personality. It is not a reason to skip screening. It is a reason a government badge is not automatically help. Do not invent a Minnesota PTSD rate.

Intra-community language politics still split some rooms — Ukrainian only, Russian at the table, mixed families. You do not referee. You book the language this household asks for.

Alcohol harm and family violence exist in some households. They are not “the culture.” They are not a Slavic joke. You follow the law. You still see a family. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Immigration status fear is real for some recent arrivals, including parole that can expire. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

LGBTQ Ukrainian Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.
chapters.evidence: War trauma in some 2022 rooms is not a personality. Intra-community language politics. Alcohol and family violence exist and are not “the culture.” LGBTQ people exist. Status fear for some recent arrivals. White skip of CI.
chapters.practitioner: Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Do not collect status you do not need.
chapters.title: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice

chapters.body:
Compass (ACS 2019–2023): about 4.5 percent without health insurance among those for whom status is determined. Date it. That vintage is not the whole 2022 stream. Do not invent a PTSD rate to fill this chapter. Trauma sits in some rooms. It is not every household.

### Access

Believe reported pain. Do not invent a Slavic or “European stoicism” slide. Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic refugee module.

Mental-health stigma exists in some families. Naming a counselor is not the same as a family accepting one. A smile is not a PHQ-9. War does not make screening optional. It does not make every person a case study.

Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it. Book the language they name even if the person is white. Confirm Ukrainian, not a “former Soviet” default.
chapters.evidence: Compass uninsured 4.5% (ACS 2019–2023) — date it; it is not the 2022 arrival. Do not invent a PTSD rate. Trauma in some streams. Mental-health stigma. Believe reported pain. Do not invent Slavic stoicism.
chapters.practitioner: Book the language they name. Offer gender match. Do not skip screening. Do not ask a person to narrate Bucha for your professional development.
chapters.title: Health

chapters.body:
Queer and trans Ukrainian Minnesotans exist. Conservative Orthodox, Greek Catholic, and some family climates can mean silence or exile. The war does not erase this person and does not get a veto over the name they use.

### This person

Staff duty is the same as on the other spines: use the name they use; do not out them to an elder as cultural humility; Minnesota Human Rights Act still applies.

Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there. Always defer to the person in front of you.
chapters.evidence: Queer and trans Ukrainian Minnesotans exist. Conservative parish climates can mean silence. The war does not erase this person. Minnesota Human Rights Act still applies.
chapters.practitioner: Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture. Do not treat a war as a veto over this person.
chapters.title: LGBTQ

chapters.body:
Vyshyvanka is public at festivals, Independence Day tables, and some church days. It is not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

Head covering happens in some parish rooms. It is not a security threat and not a consent problem. Do not touch. Do not comment on gold, a cross, or embroidery as a case note.

Winter dress is Minnesota. It is not ethnography. Heritage Month tables that mash this with a matryoshka have already failed the adjacent-peoples chapter.
chapters.evidence: Vyshyvanka is public at festivals and some church days, not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Head covering in some parish rooms.
chapters.practitioner: Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch. Do not mash with a matryoshka Heritage Month table.
chapters.title: Hair, Dress, and Body

chapters.body:
Church chant is liturgy, not a playlist. Kobzar and folk forms, popular song, and wartime music exist in some rooms. Named variation, not a “Slavic mix.”

### Variation

A playlist is not engagement. A funeral or a liturgy is not staff entertainment. Knowing that 2022 can sit inside a song will stop you from putting the wrong flag on a speaker.

Festival stages are public life. They are not consultation and not a case plan.
chapters.evidence: Church chant, kobzar and folk, pop, wartime song in some rooms. Named variation. Not a Russian mix.
chapters.practitioner: A playlist is not engagement. A liturgy or a funeral is not staff entertainment. Do not put the wrong anthem on a speaker.
chapters.title: Music

chapters.body:
Soccer shows up in public Ukrainian Minnesota life. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

### Not the whole person

Sport clubs are social infrastructure for some. They are not language access and not a case plan. A club flyer in English is still a closed door for the parent who needs Ukrainian on the line.

Greater Minnesota and Twin Cities both play.
chapters.evidence: Soccer, and ordinary school sport in the second generation. Not a people-trait.
chapters.practitioner: Do not assume the kid plays. Sport clubs are not language access.
chapters.title: Sports

chapters.body:
Ukrainian is a major written language with a long literature. Shevchenko is literacy for the desk, not a prompt to quote Кобзар in the lobby. This is not a people without letters. It is not Russian literature with a different flag.

### Literacy in the lobby

Cyrillic literacy for many elders is the actual operations fact. A notice that exists only in English, or only in Russian, is a closed door. U.S.-born adults may not read Cyrillic and may still be the person who has to explain the form.

You do not need a novel. You need the language this person reads.
chapters.evidence: A vast written literature in Ukrainian. Shevchenko is literacy, not a lobby quote. Cyrillic for many elders. U.S.-born may not read it. This is not a people without letters.
chapters.practitioner: You do not need to quote Кобзар. You need the language this person reads. Ukrainian is not Russian literature with a different flag.
chapters.title: Literature

chapters.body:
Pysanky, vyshyvanka embroidery, icons, and diaspora visual work. Not matryoshka. Not a nesting-doll exhibit. Not a Russian folk-costume mash.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. An icon is not a case plan. A festival is not consultation. Do not photograph a sanctuary as professional development without being asked.

Heritage Month tables that mash a vyshyvanka, a menorah, and a matryoshka into one “Eastern European” booth have already mashed what this brief asks you to keep apart.
chapters.evidence: Pysanky, vyshyvanka, icons, diaspora visual work. Not matryoshka. Not a nesting-doll exhibit.
chapters.practitioner: Guest, not researcher. An icon is not a case plan. A festival is not consultation.
chapters.title: Art

chapters.body:
Holodomor, Soviet surveillance, 1991, 2014, 24 February 2022, Uniting for Ukraine parole, and later enforcement climate for some arrivals — that is the political stack. A DHS badge is not automatically help. For some people, a government form is a thing you survive. That is not “paranoia.” It is pattern.

### The badge

The war is current structure for some households: family under fire, mixed marriages, parole that can expire, people who left and people who have been here for three generations. It is a trap if you assume every Ukrainian is a 2022 refugee. It is also a trap if you punish someone for not performing the politics you prefer.

Do not use 2022 as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate a war for your professional development. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not open the Russian language door as this people.
chapters.evidence: Holodomor; Soviet state; 1991; 2014; 24 February 2022; Uniting for Ukraine parole and later enforcement climate for some. A DHS badge is not automatically help.
chapters.practitioner: Do not use 2022 as a personality. Do not ask a person to narrate a war. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not assume every Ukrainian is last year’s arrival.
chapters.title: War, the State, and the Russian-Door Trap

chapters.body:
Professional work, trades, small business, public employment, and under-recognized credentials all live here. A small-business owner and a waiver recipient may be the same extended family. Compass median household income about $95,000 is an average, not this kitchen table.

### Work

Ukrainian staff exist inside DHS and counties. They are not unpaid interpreters and not “the community.” Identity is not a staffing plan.

### Staff

Relationship and hospitality may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision. The notice still has to exist in the language they read.

An English eList comment period is not how this community was reached.

sections.heading: A Note on This Guide
paragraphs: Vietnamese Minnesota. Kinh majority; Hoa in some families. Compass ACS 2019–2023 near 33,891. Census Asian mixes this with Chinese, Hmong, Indian, Karen. Date the number you cite.
There is no single Vietnamese client. Defer to this family. Do not open a Hmong, Karen, Lao, or Chinese case with this page. Pronounce the name.

This brief is about Vietnamese people — người Việt — as a people with a country, a long literature, and a Minnesota community built after 1975. Kinh are the majority in this state. Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) live in some families — ask. This is not Chinese. It is not Hmong. It is not Karen. It is not Lao as a synonym. Shared continent is not shared culture. A full mosaic is not a stereotype. A stereotype is when this page becomes the person in the lobby.

### Who this is

Vietnamese sits on the DHS CLAS five-language standing written list with Hmong, Russian, Somali, and Spanish. Still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the dialect. Northern, Central, and Southern varieties exist. Put the variety on the interpreter line if it matters in this room.

### Who this is not

Minnesota Compass (ACS 2019–2023) puts Vietnamese ancestry near 33,891. About 76.3 percent Twin Cities, about 23.7 percent Greater Minnesota. About 27.2 percent age 17 or younger; about 8.4 percent 65+. About 51.0 percent foreign-born — which means a large second generation was born here and a large first generation was not. Date the number you use. A rate is not the person.

The diversity inside this people is the point. A 1975 first-wave Catholic elder, a boat-person who spent years in a camp, a Hoa family, a Buddhist grandmother with an ancestor altar, a U.S.-born nurse, a Greater Minnesota factory household, a college student who uses English with friends and Vietnamese with an elder, a person who left 1975 politics and still shows up at Tết — share a people and do not share a Tuesday.

### How to read this

Always defer to the person in front of you. This page is a hypothesis you still test on this family.

sections.heading: Origins and the Founding of a People
paragraphs: Vietnamese peoplehood is older than 1975 and older than the refugee file. Kinh majority; Hoa and other minorities. Quốc ngữ writing. Named kingdoms and a modern nation, not a camp origin myth.
History is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family. Do not start with a phở tourism sentence.

Vietnamese peoplehood is older than French Indochina, older than 1954, and older than the refugee camp. A country on the eastern mainland of Southeast Asia; Kinh as the majority people; Hoa, Khmer Krom, and highland minorities inside the Vietnamese state. Minnesota’s community is overwhelmingly Vietnamese (Kinh) with Hoa in some families. Ask. Do not lecture a St. Paul family about taxonomy they did not ask for.

### History for the meeting

Writing in quốc ngữ — the Latin-based script — is the ordinary public literacy. Older scripts and chữ Nôm are history. Many elders read quốc ngữ. Some do not. Second generation may not read Vietnamese at all.

### What people brought

1954 partition after the French war sent a large Catholic stream from north to south. That fact still sits in Minnesota parish life. It is not a speech you give the family. 1975 is the foundational event of the diaspora you will meet on this desk. Origins did not begin there.

What people brought: language, ancestor obligation, Mahayana Buddhism and Catholicism both, farming and trade skill, a memory of war and of a state that won and a state that lost. What they met in Minnesota: an English form, one “Asian” checkbox, and often one interpreter labeled “Vietnamese.”

sections.heading: The Geography of the Vietnamese World
paragraphs: Vietnam — north, central, south. Diaspora in California, Texas, Minnesota, and elsewhere. Compass: 76.3% Twin Cities, 23.7% Greater Minnesota.
Do not assume University Avenue. Do not assume they have been to Vietnam. Greater Minnesota share is real.

Vietnam is north, central, and south — tones, food, and some vocabulary shift. Most of the 1975 and boat-people stream to the United States came out of the south. Later streams include the north. Confirm the variety if it matters in the room. Do not referee Hanoi versus Saigon in a waiver meeting. Listen if they name a place.

### Homeland

The diaspora is global: California (largest U.S. community), Texas, the Gulf Coast, France, Australia, Canada, and Minnesota. Orange County is not this map. Secondary migration and family reunification built part of what you will meet here.

### Minnesota

In Minnesota: Twin Cities — University Avenue / Frogtown, inner-ring suburbs, and other metro pockets — and a real Greater Minnesota share. Compass: 76.3 percent Twin Cities, 23.7 percent Greater Minnesota. Do not assume University Avenue is the whole. Do not assume the person in front of you has been to Vietnam.

sections.heading: 1975, Boat People, and Later Streams — Foundational Event
paragraphs: American War / Vietnam War; 1975 fall of Saigon; boat people; camps; Orderly Departure; later family reunification and other streams. 1975 is the foundational event of this Minnesota community.
If you only know “refugee,” you will miss the 20-year-old who has never lived in Vietnam and still cannot get the right interpreter for a grandmother.

If the Secret War and 1975 are the foundational event of Hmong Minnesota, the American War / Vietnam War and 30 April 1975 are the foundational event of Vietnamese Minnesota.

### Foundational events

April 1975: the Republic of Vietnam collapsed. First-wave evacuations and airlifts moved people tied to the southern government and to the United States — often more urban, more Catholic, more already connected. That is a stream, not a virtue ranking. Most people were not on those planes.

### Who you meet

Boat people followed — 1978 and the years around it especially. Overcrowded boats, pirates, drowning, camps in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines, Hong Kong. Hoa families left under a separate pressure after 1978. Years in camps. Then resettlement. Church and voluntary-agency sponsors scattered people; family pulled them back together.

Orderly Departure, the Humanitarian Operation path for re-education-camp survivors, the Amerasian Homecoming Act (1987), and later family reunification and ordinary immigration are later streams. The desk in 2026 does not only meet 1975. It meets their children — U.S.-born, English-dominant with peers, still translating for parents, still unable to get the right variety in the lobby.

1975 is literacy for the desk. It is not a speech you give the family.

sections.heading: Family
paragraphs: Filial piety as hypothesis; elders; adult children in the same week. Compass average household size about 3.01. Who speaks may be a child — that is a gate.
Ask who should be in the room. Do not use a child as interpreter. A nuclear English form already has a who.

Filial piety — hiếu — is a hypothesis, not a personality. Elders often speak first. Adult children may be in the same week as a waiver meeting, a factory shift, and a school conference. Compass: average household size about 3.01. Smaller than some neighboring spines. Still not always a nuclear English form.

### Who is in the household

Who cares for a disabled adult or a child may be a son, a daughter-in-law, a sibling, not the legally recognized caregiver on the checkbox. Hour caps and “natural supports” language can dump unpaid work onto women in that network and call it culture.

### Who speaks

Who speaks in the lobby may be a child with the best English. That child is not the qualified interpreter. CLAS still stands. Using a child as the go-between is a closed door and a harm. Book the interpreter. Ask who should be in the room.

Women’s labor — shop, salon, factory, professional second generation — sits next to elder obligation. Both can be true in the same room. Minnesota law still stands. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

sections.heading: Minnesota and Vietnamese History
paragraphs: Twin Cities including University Avenue / Frogtown and suburbs; Greater Minnesota 23.7%. Vietnamese Community of Minnesota; Buddhist temples and Catholic parishes. Phở and markets are public life, not consultation.
Partners, not a harvest list. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  Vietnamese staff. Guest at Tết. A market visit does not make you the expert.

Minnesota holds a Vietnamese community large enough to put the language on the CLAS five and large enough that this department will meet it on waivers, child welfare, health care, cash, food, aging, and employment. Compass: about 33,891 (ACS 2019–2023). Greater Minnesota is 23.7 percent. Do not write this people as a Minneapolis anecdote.

### Places

Places, not a blob: University Avenue and Frogtown; Little Mekong as a public name on a stretch of street, not a reservation; inner-ring suburbs; Greater Minnesota towns with work and housing. Phở shops and markets are public life. They are not consultation. A food-court visit does not make you the expert.

### Partners

Partners: Vietnamese Community of Minnesota; Buddhist temples families name; Catholic parishes with a large Vietnamese stream because of 1954 and 1975; CECLC as a department door — not the whole community. Pay the partner this household actually uses.

Vietnamese staff are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan. Tết is optional professional development if you are invited. You are a guest. It does not make you the expert.

sections.heading: Người Việt — the heart of a people
paragraphs: Người Việt. Peoplehood after war and exile. Face, ancestor obligation, work as a family project. Asian in a U.S. checkbox that does not fit.
Do not fold this household into “Asian Pacific.” Do not copy a Hmong or Chinese sentence onto this page.

To be Vietnamese in Minnesota is to be a people with a country and a long memory of being in someone else’s war, then building a life in a cold state that filed you under Asian. Face, ancestor obligation, and not shaming the name travel into a waiver meeting. Harmony can look like agreement and then a plan nobody follows. Ask whether they agree. Do not take a smile as consent.

### In this state

1975 sits in the room for some and is a history class for others. First-wave anti-communist politics, later arrivals, U.S.-born children, and Hoa families do not share one Tuesday. You do not referee. You do not put “Fall of Saigon” on a case note as color.

In the United States another fact sits on the same desk: many Vietnamese Minnesotans are Asian in a racial order that also holds Chinese, Indian, Korean, and Hmong histories they do not share. The mash is the gate.

This guide is a working orientation. Individual variation always supersedes group generalization. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Core Concepts
paragraphs: Hiếu as hypothesis; elders; face; ancestor altar; Catholicism and Mahayana Buddhism both; work and school as family project; 1975 memory.
You work with these. You do not perform them. Do not make a priest or a monk the case plan unless this family asked.

Hiếu. Filial piety as hypothesis. Care for parents. Obligation that an English consumer form does not see. Staff do not use it as a guilt tool. If the family names it, you listen.

### Elders

First greeting, first tea, first say. A child with English is still a child.

### Face and harmony

Direct refusal may be costly. A yes that is courtesy is not a signature. Ask again, plainly, without humiliation.

### Ancestors

An altar in a living room — including in some Catholic households — is not a case plan and not a museum. Death-anniversary giỗ is family time.

### Religion as practice, not a checkbox

Mahayana Buddhism, Catholicism, Cao Đài and Hòa Hảo in some families, none. Do not make a priest or a monk the case plan unless they asked.

### Work and school as a family project

A salon, a shop, a second-generation degree. Nail-salon labor is work, not a personality.

1975 memory. Foundational for the community. Not a personality for the person in the lobby.

sections.heading: Religion
paragraphs: Mahayana Buddhist, Catholic, Cao Đài / Hòa Hảo in some families, none. Ancestor altar in a Catholic household can be true. Large Catholic stream from 1954 and 1975.
Do not make a priest or monk the case plan unless this family asked. Ask. Do not treat an altar as folklore.

Mahayana Buddhism and Catholicism are the two large public streams in Vietnamese Minnesota. Cao Đài and Hòa Hảo live in some families. None is also a Tuesday. Ask. A large Catholic stream exists because 1954 moved northern Catholics south and 1975 moved many of those families again. That is history, not a piety ranking.

### Streams

An ancestor altar in a Catholic household can be true. Do not treat that as contradiction you need to fix. Do not treat Buddhism as “more Vietnamese” than the parish.

### Practice

The temple and the parish are centers of ritual, mutual aid, and information. They are not “the community.” Do not BCC one priest or one monk and call it consultation. Do not make clergy the case plan unless this family asked.

Funerals and giỗ gather family. You still keep medical and legal time. You name the conflict instead of punishing it. Do not photograph an altar.

sections.heading: Greetings
paragraphs: Elders first. Slight bow or nod. Many second-generation people shake hands in English-language rooms. Xin chào.
Do not force a handshake on an elder. Do not import Somali or African American greeting rules. Say the name.

Elders first. A slight bow or nod with an older person is safer than a hard handshake you assume is universal. Many second-generation people will shake hands in English-language rooms. Follow this room.

### Titles

Xin chào is a common hello. English “hello” is ordinary. Say the name. The family name is often the first word in Vietnamese order; do not treat it as optional.

### This room

Do not import Somali right-hand rules or the Black nod onto this page. This is not those grammars.

Physical contact: ask the room. Cross-gender touch with elders is not a default. A hug from staff is not warmth if the household did not offer it.

sections.heading: Naming Conventions
paragraphs: Family name first in Vietnamese order: Nguyễn, Trần, Lê, Phạm, Huỳnh/Hoàng, Phan, Vũ/Võ. U.S. forms reverse it. Ask which is the family name.
Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. Do not joke about Nguyễn. The reversed name becomes a gate.

Family name first in Vietnamese order. Nguyễn, Trần, Lê, Phạm, Huỳnh / Hoàng, Phan, Vũ / Võ are common. Nguyễn is common enough that a joke about it is a closed door. Do not joke. Do not say “too many Nguyens.”

### How to file

U.S. forms reverse the order. A person who is Nguyễn Thị Lan in Vietnamese may be Lan Nguyen on a license and Lan Thi Nguyen in another database. Ask which is the family name. Ask how to file. Ask how to say it. The form that guesses will invent a person, and that invented name follows them through MHCP, school, and child welfare.

Given names and middle names (often a generational or gender marker such as Thị or Văn) are not decoration. Tones matter in speech. You do not need to become a linguist. You need to ask and to write down what they say.

Women may or may not take a husband’s family name in U.S. records. Mother and child may not match. That is not fraud until you have a reason.

sections.heading: Dates of Significance
paragraphs: Tết (Lunar New Year). April 30 is grief and politics — not a party on a case note. Hùng Kings. Ancestral death anniversaries (giỗ).
A calendar click is literacy. It is not community engagement. Do not put “Fall of Saigon party” on a file.

Tết — Lunar New Year — is the large annual public and family date. Travel, food, elders, red envelopes in some families, closed shops. Schedule around it when you can. It is not a day off the work. Guest if invited. A calendar click is not community engagement.

### Calendar

30 April 1975 — the fall of Saigon / the end of the Republic of Vietnam. In many Vietnamese American rooms this is grief and politics, sometimes marked as Black April. It is not a “Fall of Saigon party.” Do not put that phrase on a case note. Do not celebrate reunification at this desk. Listen if they name it.

Giỗ — ancestral death anniversaries — are household dates. They will not be on your state calendar. Ask. Hùng Kings commemoration exists in some community public life. Literacy, not a file.

Do not put “Asian holiday” on a case note.

sections.heading: Education
paragraphs: Compass: ~79.6% high school or higher (25+); ~36.3% bachelor’s or higher. Foreign-born 51.0%. English IEP is still a gate for the parent who does not read it.
A parent who speaks fluent Vietnamese and limited English is not illiterate. The English-only packet is the gate. Put the variety on the line.

Compass (ACS 2019–2023): among Vietnamese Minnesotans 25 and older, about 79.6 percent high school or higher; about 36.3 percent bachelor’s or higher. Date Compass. About 51.0 percent of the community is foreign-born. A large share of children are U.S.-born and in English-dominant schools. The IEP still has to reach the parent who does not read it.

### School and language

A parent who speaks fluent Vietnamese and limited English is not illiterate. Many elders read quốc ngữ. Some do not. The English-only form is the gate. Put the variety on the interpreter line if this household needs it.

Second-generation educational mobility is real. So is a gap that a room that treats everyone the same will call “culture” instead of language access plus a school that never learned the name. Do not treat a college student as proof the waiver household needs no interpreter.

sections.heading: Etiquette
paragraphs: Elders first. Shoes in some homes. Hospitality. Altars. Do not point feet at an altar.
Accept a little food. Keep medical and legal time. Do not photograph the altar. Do not use a child as the go-between.

Elders first. Shoes off in many homes. Accept a little food if offered. Hospitality is a virtue. You still keep medical and legal time.

### In the home

Do not point your feet at an altar or at a person if you are in a household that keeps one. Do not walk into a living room and photograph the altar. Do not touch ritual objects. Do not ask an elder to explain Buddhism as entertainment.

### Time

On-time for appointments. Traffic and multi-household logistics are real. So is a pattern of courtesy-yes then no-show when the plan was never agreed. Ask whether they agree. Confirm in the language they use.

Do not use a child as the go-between and call it family values. Book the interpreter.

sections.heading: Language and Communication
paragraphs: Vietnamese is tonal. Northern, Central, Southern varieties. Compass: ~68.6% language other than English (5+); ~37.3% LEP. Many elders read quốc ngữ; some do not.
Put the variety on the interpreter line if it matters in the room. Still book a qualified interpreter. Do not use a child. Do not take a smile as consent.

Vietnamese is tonal. Northern, Central, and Southern varieties are not always interchangeable in an interpreter. Put the variety on the line if it matters in this room. Still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the dialect. CLAS still stands.

### Language

Compass: among those 5 and older, about 68.6 percent speak a language other than English; about 37.3 percent speak English less than “very well.” Date the number. Many elders read quốc ngữ. Some do not. Second-generation English is common. The IEP still has to reach the parent.

A long answer may be story. A short English yes may be exhaustion or courtesy. Do not take a smile as consent. Ask whether they agree with the plan.

Do not use a child as the interpreter. Do not make a Vietnamese coworker the interpreter.

sections.heading: Other Considerations — unvarnished, not Minnesota Nice
paragraphs: Boat-people trauma; intra-community 1975 politics; gambling as a named harm in some families not a race trait; LGBTQ people exist; nail-salon labor is work; deportation of people with records.
Follow law. Still see a family. Do not out anyone. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility. Do not collect status you do not need.

Unvarnished, because Minnesota Nice is how a room that treats everyone the same deletes facts.

### Named harms

Boat-people trauma is real in some rooms: sea, camps, loss. It is not a personality. It is not a reason to skip screening. It is a reason a government badge is not automatically help.

Intra-community 1975 politics still split some rooms — first wave, later arrivals, flag, April 30. You do not referee. You do not put it on a case note as color.

Gambling is a named harm in some families. It is not a race trait. You follow the law. You still see a family.

Nail-salon labor is work, not a personality and not a joke. Chemicals, hours, and pay are labor facts. Do not write “nails” as ethnicity.

Deportation of Vietnamese people with certain convictions — including people who have lived here since childhood — is current structure, not folklore. It changes who opens the door. Do not collect status you do not need. Do not treat fear as noncompliance.

LGBTQ Vietnamese Minnesotans exist. You use the name. You do not out someone to kin and call it culture. Do not skip mandated reporting and call it humility.

Staff who share this community may add facts. They do not get to delete a fact because it is hard to say.

sections.heading: Health
paragraphs: Believe reported pain. Do not invent “Asian stoicism.” Hepatitis B screening is a U.S. public-health pattern for people born in Vietnam — date CDC if you cite. Mental-health stigma. Traditional medicine beside biomedicine.
Ask what they use. Co-create. Gender match if they want it. Do not skip screening. Peers who share language.

Believe reported pain. Do not invent “Asian stoicism.” Do not fold this history into Tuskegee or into a generic Asian slide. This is not the Hmong page and not the Chinese page.

### Access

Hepatitis B screening for people born in Vietnam is a U.S. public-health pattern — CDC has treated Vietnam as a higher-prevalence birth country in screening guidance. Date the CDC page you cite. Do not invent a Minnesota rate. Do not skip screening because the person looks well.

Mental-health stigma is real in some families. War trauma, depression, and somatic presentation exist. Naming a counselor is not the same as a family accepting one. A smile is not a PHQ-9.

Traditional medicine — thuốc nam, coining, cupping, herbs — often sits beside biomedicine. Ask. Co-create. Do not mock marks on skin as abuse by default; do not skip a child-protection duty when the facts are the facts. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care. Offer it.

Late help-seeking can be language, stigma, and a lobby that already used a child as the interpreter. Do not skip screening.

sections.heading: LGBTQ
paragraphs: Queer and trans Vietnamese Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, temple, and parish climates can mean silence.
Use the name. Do not out someone to family as culture.

Queer and trans Vietnamese Minnesotans exist. Conservative family, temple, and parish climates can mean silence or exile. Some people live a public English life and a private Vietnamese life. You use the name they use. You do not out them to an elder as cultural humility.

### This person

Minnesota’s Human Rights Act still applies. So does the duty not to treat a whole people as a family-values exhibit. Do not use this chapter to raid a household. Do not pretend the tension is not there.

Face and 1975 politics do not get a veto over this person. Always defer to the person in front of you.

sections.heading: Hair, Dress, and Body
paragraphs: Áo dài is public at Tết and weddings, not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota.
Do not ask if they “still wear the costume.” Do not touch.

Áo dài is public at Tết, weddings, and some school or parish stages. It is not a daily uniform. Second generation looks like Minnesota. Do not ask a woman in clinic whether she “still wears the costume.”

### Dress

Hair and head: follow this person. Do not touch. Gold, a Buddhist bracelet, a cross, a wedding huế — not a mascot for the unit’s Heritage Month table.

Nail-salon work may mean stained hands and chemical exposure. That is labor. It is not a joke and not a race trait.

sections.heading: Music
paragraphs: Cải lương, nhạc vàng, pop, Buddhist chant, Catholic hymn. New Year stages. Named variation.
A playlist is not engagement. A funeral is not staff entertainment.

Cải lương, nhạc vàng, diaspora pop, karaoke as social life in some rooms, Buddhist chant, Catholic hymn. New Year stages hold more than one of these. Named variation, not a playlist.

### Variation

A funeral is not staff entertainment. A playlist is not engagement. Knowing that 1975 politics can sit inside a song will stop you from putting the wrong flag on a speaker.

Tết stages are public life. They are not consultation and not a case plan.

sections.heading: Sports
paragraphs: Soccer, badminton, and ordinary school sport in the second generation.
Do not assume the kid plays. Sport clubs are not language access.

Soccer and badminton show up in public Vietnamese Minnesota life. School sport is ordinary for the second generation. Do not assume the kid plays. Do not make sport the only excellence you can see.

### Not the whole person

Sport clubs are social infrastructure for some. They are not language access and not a case plan. Greater Minnesota teams are still this people.

A Saturday tournament does not replace an interpreter on Monday.

sections.heading: Literature
paragraphs: Quốc ngữ. Oral and written. Diaspora writers and journalists. This is not a people without letters.
You do not need to quote a novel. You need the language this person reads.

Quốc ngữ made a modern written public. Oral forms, poetry, and diaspora memoir sit beside it. Minnesota and U.S. Vietnamese writers, journalists, and scholars exist. You do not need to quote a novel in the lobby.

### Literacy in the lobby

You do need to know this is not a people without letters. Many elders read Vietnamese. Some do not. A notice that exists only in English is a closed door. A notice in Vietnamese the elder cannot read is also a closed door. Ask.

Tones and diacritics are not decoration. A name stripped of marks on a form can still be the wrong person. Write what they tell you.

sections.heading: Art
paragraphs: Calligraphy, temple art, diaspora visual work. Phở and markets are public culture, not consultation.
Guest, not researcher. A market visit is not a case plan.

Calligraphy, temple sculpture and painting, diaspora visual work, and the public culture of markets and Tết. Phở and bánh mì are foodway, not consultation.

### Guest

Guest, not researcher. A market visit is not a case plan. A museum or temple visit is optional professional development. It is not consultation. Do not photograph an altar.

Heritage Month that mashes this with Hmong paj ntaub or a Chinese New Year poster has already mashed the adjacent peoples.

sections.heading: War, the State, and Deportation Climate
paragraphs: American War; 1975; camps; later policing and deportation of people with records, including people who have lived here since childhood.
A DHS badge is not automatically help. Do not use 1975 as a personality. Do not collect status you do not need.

The American War / Vietnam War, 30 April 1975, the boats, the camps, Orderly Departure, and a United States that fought, left, and then resettled — that is the political event. Later: policing, and deportation of people with records, including people who have lived here since childhood. A DHS badge is not automatically help.

### The badge

Do not use 1975 as a personality. Do not ask a veteran or a boat-person to narrate dying for your professional development. Intra-community politics about the flag and April 30 are real. You do not referee them on a case note.

Deportation climate changes who opens the door, who signs, and who will not put a relative’s name on a form. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

sections.heading: Work, Markets, and Government
paragraphs: Small business, nail-salon labor as work not personality, professional second generation, Vietnamese staff in government. Markets are economy.
Vietnamese employees are not unpaid interpreters. Identity is not a staffing plan. Nail work is a job.

Shop, restaurant, factory, professional second generation, public employment. Nail-salon labor is a documented Vietnamese American work pattern. It is work. It is not a personality, not a joke, and not the whole economy. Chemicals and hours are labor. Do not write “nails” as ethnicity.

### Work

Markets and University Avenue commerce are economy and culture. A food-court visit is not consultation.

### Staff

Vietnamese staff inside the department are not unpaid interpreters and not the community. Identity is not a staffing plan.

Relationship may precede a signature. That is not permission to skip a notice. It is a reason the first visit may not be the decision.

sections.heading: Health-care and Human-service Encounters
paragraphs: Variety on the interpreter line; family-name order; child as interpreter; who is in the room; traditional medicine; deportation climate.
Confirm variety. Do not use a child. Believe reported pain. Ask who should hear. Mandated reporting still exists.

Language and variety. Family-name order. Who is in the room. A child pushed forward as English. An altar or a priest or a monk in the story. Pain you must believe. Deportation climate. A nuclear form that reversed the name.

### Language

Confirm the variety if it matters. Still book a qualified interpreter. Do not use a child. Offer gender match. Ask who should hear. Ask which name is the family name. Do not make staff the interpreter.

### The meeting

If they name traditional medicine, listen. Mandated reporting still exists. Believe reported pain. Do not invent Asian stoicism.

sections.heading: Adjacent Peoples — Do Not Mash
paragraphs: Not Hmong, not Lao, not Cambodian, not Chinese, not Korean, not “Asian American” as the file. Hoa in some families — ask.
Never one Asian module. Open the Hmong CI for Hmong. Open this for Vietnamese. Ask this household.

Not Hmong. Not Lao. Not Cambodian. Not Chinese. Not Korean. Not “Asian American” as the file. Open the Hmong CI for Hmong. Open this for Vietnamese. Some households are mixed. Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) in some families — ask this household. Do not file them under Chinese by default and do not deny it if they name it.

### Adjacent doors

Shared war in Southeast Asia is not shared culture. Camps in Thailand are a Hmong and other story as well — do not mash the camp into one Asian refugee. Karen is a different spine.

Never one Asian module. Never one “Southeast Asian” interpreter.

sections.heading: Counts, Dated
paragraphs: Compass ACS 2019–2023: ~33,891; 76.3% metro; 23.7% Greater MN; 27.2% 17 or younger; foreign-born 51.0%; LEP 37.3%; poverty 9.1%; owner 69.5%. Date them. Do not invent other rates.
A rate is not the person. Language and child-as-interpreter are gates.

Minnesota Compass, ACS 2019–2023, Vietnamese cultural community: about 33,891; Twin Cities 76.3%; Greater Minnesota 23.7%; age 17 or younger 27.2%; 65+ 8.4%; foreign-born 51.0%; language other than English (age 5+) 68.6%; English less than “very well” 37.3%; high school or higher (25+) 79.6%; bachelor’s or higher 36.3%; median household income about $90,000; poverty 9.1%; owner-occupied 69.5%; average household size 3.01.

### Counts

Date Compass. Do not invent other rates. Counts disagree across ACS vintages and definitions (ancestry vs. birthplace vs. language). Date the number you cite.

### What the count is not

A young age structure is not a personality. An owner rate is not proof the gates closed. Language and child-as-interpreter are gates. A rate is not the person.

sections.heading: Doors and Sources
paragraphs: Compass Vietnamese profile ACS 2019–2023. Vietnamese Community of Minnesota. Temples and parishes families name. CECLC is a door, not the community. DHS LEP five.
Learn on your own time. Do not make a Vietnamese colleague your unpaid tutor. Pay partners.

Minnesota Compass Vietnamese profile (ACS 2019–2023). DHS Equal Opportunity and Access LEP resources — Vietnamese on the five, the ten-language block, and the fifteen interpreter cards. A list is not the notice and not the interpreter.

### Public doors

Vietnamese Community of Minnesota. Buddhist temples and Catholic parishes families name. CECLC is a door, not the whole community.

### Learn on your own time

Learn on your own time. Do not make a Vietnamese colleague your unpaid tutor. Do not BCC a temple or a parish and call it consultation. Pay partners. Report back. Guest at Tết if invited — it is not consultation.

sections.heading: How it hits DHS gates — the 40%
paragraphs: Northern/Central/Southern variety; family-name order on nuclear forms; English IEPs; child as interpreter; Asian mash with Hmong/Karen; eList comment periods; harvesting Vietnamese staff; Greater Minnesota share.

Put the variety on the interpreter line if it matters. Ask which name is the family name. Do not use a child. Toolkit disposition on the packet. If the family cannot run the exception in English, the cap is the policy. Statute may still stand. Name who the packet was built for.

Workplace culture and service delivery are both candidates.

Language: an interpreter labeled Vietnamese who does not speak this household’s variety is a closed door. Still book a qualified interpreter. A list is not the person and not the dialect. Do not use a child. Gender match may be requested in maternal and intimate care.

Names: family name first in Vietnamese order. The database that reverses Nguyễn without asking invents a person. Do not joke about Nguyễn.

Hour caps, exception processes, and life-sharing matches without language are not culturally neutral.

Child welfare and disability: help-seeking that becomes a report is part of why people wait. Mandated reporting still exists. So does the duty not to treat a whole community as a risk score. Do not invent Asian stoicism.

Deportation climate: people skip clinic, school, and waiver meetings when a relative can be moved. That is not noncompliance. Do not collect status you do not need.

Notices and comment: an eList and an English PDF is not how this community was reached. Empty follow-up cells are theater. Greater Minnesota is 23.7 percent — a St. Paul meeting is not the whole channel.

Workforce: Vietnamese staff are not the interpreter pool and not the community. Staff are colleagues, not the curriculum. Do not treat  them.

Asian mash: opening Hmong or Karen or Chinese because the checkbox says Asian is a closed door.

Legislation, funding, rule: you cannot advocate for a channel you will not study. This cultural intelligence exists so the 40% has a household in it — not a paternalistic program designed in a building that never learned the family name.
